the clause is circumstantial. ﴿أَفَلَمْ﴾: the hamza is for interrogation, the fāʾ is resumptive, and لم governs the jussive. ﴿يَدَّبَّرُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive, and the wāw is fāʿil. ﴿الْقَوْلَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَمْ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿جاءَهُمْ﴾: a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi. ﴿ما لَمْ﴾: ما is a relative noun, fāʿil, and لم is a jussive particle. ﴿يَأْتِ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive by the dropping of the weak letter; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿آباءَهُمُ﴾: mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of آباءهم, accusative with the yāʾ; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative.

daas-irab:69-72.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿لَمْ يَعْرِفُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil (agent). ﴿رَسُولَهُمْ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَهُمْ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; هم is mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لَهُ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) منكرون. ﴿مُنْكِرُونَ﴾: khabar (predicate); the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَمْ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِهِ﴾: attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿جِنَّةٌ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿بَلْ﴾: a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿جاءَهُمْ﴾: a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾: attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial, and a mubtadaʾ; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لِلْحَقِّ﴾: attached to كارهون. ﴿كارِهُونَ﴾: khabar, nominative with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is circumstantial. ﴿وَلَوِ﴾: the wāw is resumptive; لو is a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿اتَّبَعَ الْحَقُّ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿أَهْواءَهُمْ﴾: mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation; the clause has no grammatical position because it is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿لَفَسَدَتِ﴾: the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; a past verb, and the tāʾ is for the feminine. ﴿السَّماواتُ﴾: fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of لو. ﴿وَالْأَرْضُ﴾: conjoined to السموات. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, conjoined to السموات. ﴿فِيهِنَّ﴾: attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, and the nūn is a particle indicating the feminine plural. ﴿بَلْ﴾: a particle of digression. ﴿أَتَيْناهُمْ﴾: a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِذِكْرِهِمْ﴾: attached to أتيناهم, and the hāʾ is in the position of genitive by annexation. ﴿فَهُمْ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction and هم is mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَنْ ذِكْرِهِمْ﴾: attached to معرضون, and the hāʾ is in the position of genitive by annexation. ﴿مُعْرِضُونَ﴾: khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative with the wāw; the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَمْ تَسْأَلُهُمْ﴾: a conjunction, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the hāʾ is first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿خَرْجاً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَخَراجُ﴾: the fāʾ is causal (taʿlīliyya), and a mubtadaʾ, which is muḍāf. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, and the kāf is in the position of genitive by annexation. ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾: khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is causal (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَهُوَ﴾: the wāw is the wāw of circumstance (ḥāl); هو is a detached pronoun, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾: khabar; the clause is circumstantial. ﴿الرَّازِقِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the yāʾ.

daas-irab:73-77.t: ﴿وَإِنَّكَ﴾: the wāw is the wāw of circumstance (ḥāl); إن is a particle resembling the verb and the kāf is its noun; the clause is circumstantial. ﴿لَتَدْعُوهُمْ﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the wāw because of heaviness; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنت", and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إن. ﴿إِلى صِراطٍ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) تدعوهم. ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of صراط. ﴿وَإِنَّ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and إن is a particle resembling the verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as the noun of إن. ﴿لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾: لا is negative; an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بِالْآخِرَةِ﴾: attached to يؤمنون. ﴿عَنِ الصِّراطِ﴾: attached to ناكبون. ﴿لَناكِبُونَ﴾: the lām is the shifted lām, and the khabar of إن. ﴿وَلَوْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive; لو is a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿رَحِمْناهُمْ﴾: a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿وَكَشَفْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بِهِمْ﴾: attached to an omitted ṣila. ﴿مِنْ ضُرٍّ﴾: attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لَلَجُّوا﴾: the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis of "لولا", with no grammatical position. [Translator's note: so in the source; the apodosis is that of لو.] ﴿فِي طُغْيانِهِمْ﴾: attached to لجوا. ﴿يَعْمَهُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is circumstantial. ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial, the lām occurs in the complement of an oath, and قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿أَخَذْناهُمْ﴾: a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the complement of an oath, with no grammatical position. ﴿بِالْعَذابِ﴾: attached to أخذناهم. ﴿فَمَا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction and ما is negative. ﴿اسْتَكانُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿لِرَبِّهِمْ﴾: attached to استكانوا, and the hāʾ is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and ما is negative. ﴿يَتَضَرَّعُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿حَتَّى﴾: a particle of commencement (ḥarf ibtidāʾ) with no grammatical position. ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb for future time, putting its condition in the genitive and made accusative by its apodosis. ﴿فَتَحْنا﴾: a past verb and fāʿil; the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: attached to فتحنا. ﴿باباً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿ذا﴾: a naʿt of بابا, accusative with the alif because it is one of the five nouns. ﴿عَذابٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿شَدِيدٍ﴾: naʿt of عذاب. ﴿إِذا﴾: [the إذا] of surprise (al-fujāʾiyya). ﴿هُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿فِيهِ﴾: attached to مبلسون. ﴿مُبْلِسُونَ﴾: khabar, nominative with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

daas-irab:78-83.t: ﴿وَهُوَ﴾: the wāw is resumptive and هو is a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive. ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a relative noun, khabar (predicate). ﴿أَنْشَأَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿لَكُمُ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) أنشأ; the clause is ṣila (relative clause). ﴿السَّمْعَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَالْأَبْصارَ وَالْأَفْئِدَةَ﴾: conjoined to what precedes. ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq, standing in for the absolute object). ﴿ما تَشْكُرُونَ﴾: ما is maṣdariyya; an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause, interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), is the fāʿil of قليلا. ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; a mubtadaʾ, and the relative noun is its khabar; the clause is conjoined. ﴿ذَرَأَكُمْ﴾: a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and its fāʿil is latent; the clause is ṣila. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾: attached to ذرأكم. ﴿وَإِلَيْهِ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إليه is attached to تحشرون. ﴿تُحْشَرُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, passive; the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَهُوَ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a relative noun, khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يُحْيِي﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative with the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ because of heaviness, and its fāʿil is latent; the clause is ṣila. ﴿وَيُمِيتُ﴾: conjoined to يحيي, and its i'rab is like it. ﴿وَلَهُ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and [the preposition and pronoun] are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿اخْتِلافُ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿اللَّيْلِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالنَّهارِ﴾: conjoined to الليل. ﴿أَفَلا﴾: the hamza is for interrogation, the fāʾ is resumptive and لا is negative. ﴿تَعْقِلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بَلْ﴾: a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿قالُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِثْلَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿قالَ الْأَوَّلُونَ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, nominative with the wāw; the clause is ṣila. ﴿قالُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَإِذا﴾: the hamza is for interrogation; إذا is an adverb containing the meaning of condition. ﴿مِتْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَكُنَّا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; كان and its noun; the clause is conjoined. ﴿تُراباً﴾: khabar. ﴿وَعِظاماً﴾: conjoined to ترابا. ﴿أَإِنَّا﴾: the hamza is for interrogation; إن and its noun. ﴿لَمَبْعُوثُونَ﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and a khabar, nominative with the wāw; the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿لَقَدْ﴾: the lām occurs in the complement of the oath, and قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿وُعِدْنا﴾: a passive past verb, and نا is nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿نَحْنُ﴾: tawkīd (emphasis) of the nāʾib fāʿil نا. ﴿وَآباؤُنا﴾: conjoined to the nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿هذا﴾: the hāʾ is for alerting (tanbīh), and ذا is a demonstrative, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾: attached to وعدنا. ﴿إِنْ﴾: a particle of negation with no governing effect. ﴿هذا﴾: the hāʾ is for alerting, and ذا is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿أَساطِيرُ﴾: khabar. ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause of the complement of the oath has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:84-89.t:
﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿لِمَنِ﴾: the lām is a preposition and من is a relative noun; both attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate). [Translator's note: من here is interrogative; the source says "relative noun".] ﴿الْأَرْضُ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَمَنْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; من is a relative noun conjoined to الأرض. ﴿فِيها﴾: attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِنْ﴾: a jussive-governing conditional particle. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾: كان and its noun; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿تَعْلَمُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause is khabar, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted. ﴿سَيَقُولُونَ﴾: the sīn is for the future; an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty is genitive (majrūr) by the lām; both attached to an omitted khabar, and the mubtadaʾ is omitted, its implied form being "هي لله" (it belongs to Allah); the clause is the object of saying. ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَفَلا﴾: the hamza is for interrogation, the fāʾ is a conjunction and لا is negative. [Translator's note: the bracket of this word is broken in the source and has been restored.] ﴿تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause is the object of saying. ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مَنْ﴾: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿رَبُّ﴾: khabar. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿السَّبْعِ﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is the object of saying. ﴿وَرَبُّ﴾: conjoined to رب. ﴿الْعَرْشِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الْعَظِيمِ﴾: naʿt. ﴿سَيَقُولُونَ﴾: the sīn is for the future; an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil. ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty is genitive by the lām; both attached to the khabar of the omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هي لله"; the clause is the object of saying. ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَفَلا﴾: the hamza is for interrogation, the fāʾ is a conjunction and لا is negative. ﴿تَتَّقُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the clause is the object of saying. ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿مَنْ﴾: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ, and its clause is the object of saying. ﴿بِيَدِهِ﴾: attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مَلَكُوتُ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من. ﴿كُلِّ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَهُوَ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial; هو is mubtadaʾ; the clause is circumstantial. ﴿يُجِيرُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is khabar. ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لا is negative. ﴿يُجارُ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is omitted. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾: attached to يجار. ﴿إِنْ﴾: conditional. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾: كان and its noun; the clause is initial. ﴿تَعْلَمُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause is khabar, and the apodosis is omitted.
﴿سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ قُلْ﴾: its i'rab has preceded. ﴿فَأَنَّى﴾: the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and أنى is an interrogative noun, ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿تُسْحَرُونَ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is the object of saying.

daas-irab:90-93.t: ﴿بَلْ﴾: a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿أَتَيْناهُمْ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَإِنَّهُمْ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial; إن and its noun. ﴿لَكاذِبُونَ﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ) with the wāw, and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); the clause is circumstantial. ﴿مَا﴾: negative. ﴿اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ﴾: a past verb, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil. ﴿مِنْ﴾: a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿وَلَدٍ﴾: mafʿūl bihi in position. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and ما is negative. ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿مَعَهُ﴾: an adverb of place attached to the omitted khabar, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِنْ﴾: a redundant preposition. ﴿إِلهٍ﴾: the noun of كان, genitive (majrūr) in wording and nominative in position. ﴿إِذاً﴾: a particle of response. ﴿لَذَهَبَ كُلُّ﴾: the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو [Translator's note: i.e. an implied لو]; a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿إِلهٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِما﴾: ما is relative; both attached to ذهب. ﴿خَلَقَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَلَعَلا﴾: conjoined to ذهب. ﴿بَعْضُهُمْ﴾: the fāʿil of علا, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَلى بَعْضٍ﴾: attached to علا. ﴿سُبْحانَ﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, and its clause is resumptive. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَمَّا﴾: عن is a preposition and ما is a relative noun; both attached to سبحان. ﴿يَصِفُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause is ṣila. ﴿عالِمِ﴾: badal (substitute) of the Name of Majesty. ﴿الْغَيْبِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالشَّهادَةِ﴾: conjoined to الغيب. ﴿فَتَعالى﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿عَمَّا﴾: its i'rab has preceded. ﴿يُشْرِكُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause is ṣila. ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿رَبِّ﴾: the one addressed (munādā) with an omitted vocative particle; it is accusative (manṣūb) by the vocative with the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, which was dropped for lightness; the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿إِمَّا﴾: composed of the conditional إن and the redundant ما. ﴿تُرِيَنِّي﴾: an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; it is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), the yāʾ is first mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿يُوعَدُونَ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is ṣila.

daas-irab:94-99.t: ﴿رَبِّ﴾: its i'rab has preceded. ﴿فَلا﴾: the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and لا is prohibitive. ﴿تَجْعَلْنِي﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا; the nūn is for protection (wiqāya) and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. ﴿فِي الْقَوْمِ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) تجعلني. ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of قوم, genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ. ﴿وَإِنَّا﴾: the wāw is resumptive; إن and its noun; the clause is resumptive. ﴿عَلى﴾: a preposition. ﴿أَنْ﴾: a maṣdar-forming particle governing the accusative. ﴿نُرِيَكَ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and the kāf is first mafʿūl bihi; أن and what follows it are to be interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) whose position is genitive by على, both attached to قادرون. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿نَعِدُهُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause is ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لَقادِرُونَ﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and the khabar (predicate) of إنا, nominative (marfūʿ) with the wāw. ﴿ادْفَعْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بِالَّتِي﴾: a relative noun; both attached to ادفع. ﴿هِيَ أَحْسَنُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar; the clause is ṣila. ﴿السَّيِّئَةَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿نَحْنُ﴾: mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَعْلَمُ﴾: khabar; the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿بِما﴾: attached to أعلم. ﴿يَصِفُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative; the clause is ṣila, and the wāw is fāʿil. ﴿وَقُلْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿رَبِّ﴾: the one addressed (munādā), muḍāf. ﴿أَعُوذُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). The meaning of أعوذ is "I seek protection". ﴿بِكَ﴾: attached to أعوذ. ﴿مِنْ هَمَزاتِ﴾: attached to أعوذ. ﴿الشَّياطِينِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَأَعُوذُ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِكَ﴾: attached to أعوذ. ﴿رَبِّ﴾: the one addressed with an omitted vocative particle, accusative with the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, which was dropped for lightness. ﴿أَنْ يَحْضُرُونِ﴾: أن governs the accusative, and an imperfect verb, accusative by أن, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn; the nūn is for protection, and the omitted yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿حَتَّى﴾: a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition. ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb containing the meaning of condition. ﴿جاءَ أَحَدَهُمُ الْمَوْتُ﴾: a past verb, its fronted mafʿūl bihi and its postponed fāʿil; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قالَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿رَبِّ﴾: the one addressed, muḍāf. ﴿ارْجِعُونِ﴾: a verb of supplication, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and the omitted yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the object of saying.

daas-irab:100-102.t: ﴿لَعَلِّي﴾: لعل and its noun; the clause is causal (taʿlīl). ﴿أَعْمَلُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿صالِحاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of لعل. ﴿فِيما﴾: ما is relative; both attached to (mutaʿalliq) صالحا. ﴿تَرَكْتُ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is ṣila (relative clause). ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a particle of rebuke (zajr). ﴿إِنَّها كَلِمَةٌ﴾: إن, its noun and its khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿هُوَ قائِلُها﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar; the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of كلمة, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَمِنْ وَرائِهِمْ﴾: attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بَرْزَخٌ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِلى يَوْمِ﴾: attached to an omitted naʿt of برزخ. ﴿يُبْعَثُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَإِذا﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and إذا is an adverb containing the meaning of condition. ﴿نُفِخَ﴾: a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil is latent. ﴿فِي الصُّورِ﴾: attached to نفخ; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَلا﴾: the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis of إذا, and لا is the lā of generic negation, operating like إن. ﴿أَنْسابَ﴾: its noun. ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾: attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb annexed to one like it; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لا is negative. ﴿يَتَساءَلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَمَنْ﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and من is a jussive-governing conditional, mubtadaʾ. ﴿ثَقُلَتْ مَوازِينُهُ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the tāʾ is for the feminine and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَأُولئِكَ﴾: the fāʾ binds the apodosis; أولاء is mubtadaʾ, the lām is for distance [Translator's note: so in the source; أولئك has no lām] and the kāf for address. ﴿هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾: mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is the khabar of أولئك, and the two clauses of condition and apodosis are the khabar of فمن.

daas-irab:103-106.t: ﴿وَمَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوازِينُهُ فَأُولئِكَ﴾: its i'rab is like the i'rab of the preceding one. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar (predicate) of أولئك; the clause is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿خَسِرُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. ﴿أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فِي جَهَنَّمَ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) the fronted khabar; جهنم is genitive (majrūr) with the fatḥa because it is a diptote. ﴿خالِدُونَ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is a badal (substitute) of the ṣila of the relative. [Translator's note: so in the source; خالدون is usually parsed as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ "هم", with في جهنم attached to it.] ﴿تَلْفَحُ وُجُوهَهُمُ النَّارُ﴾: an imperfect verb, its fronted mafʿūl bihi and its postponed fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial; هم is mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِيها﴾: attached to كالحون. ﴿كالِحُونَ﴾: khabar, nominative with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿أَلَمْ﴾: the hamza is for interrogation; لم governs the jussive. ﴿تَكُنْ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb. ﴿آياتِي﴾: the noun of تكن, nominative with the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl) of an omitted قال. ﴿تُتْلى﴾: a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is khabar. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: attached to تتلى. ﴿فَكُنْتُمْ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; كان and its noun. ﴿بِها﴾: attached to تكذبون; the clause is conjoined. ﴿تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كنتم. ﴿قالُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾: the one addressed (munādā) with an omitted vocative particle, accusative (manṣūb), and نا is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the object of saying. ﴿غَلَبَتْ﴾: a past verb, and the tāʾ is for the feminine. ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾: attached to the verb. ﴿شِقْوَتُنا﴾: fāʿil, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the object of saying. ﴿وَكُنَّا قَوْماً﴾: كان, its noun and its khabar; the clause is conjoined. ﴿ضالِّينَ﴾: a naʿt (adjective), accusative with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural.

dervis-irab:29-36.t:
* I'rab:
(وَقُلْ رَبِّ أَنْزِلْنِي مُنْزَلًا مُبارَكاً وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الْمُنْزِلِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (قل) is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; (رب) is the one addressed in the vocative (munādā), muḍāf to the omitted yāʾ of the first person, and the vocative particle is omitted; (أنزلني) is an imperative verb used for supplication, its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "you"; the nūn is the nūn of protection (al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (منزلا) is a noun of place or a maṣdar (verbal noun): a second mafʿūl bihi, or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); (مباركا) is an adjective (ṣifa); in (وأنت) the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), (أنت) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (خير المنزلين) is the khabar (predicate). (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ وَإِنْ كُنَّا لَمُبْتَلِينَ) The clause is resumptive, introduced to give the reason for what was mentioned. (إن) is a particle resembling the verb; (في ذلك) is its fronted khabar; in (لآيات) the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) and (آيات) is the noun (ism) of inna. (إن) is lightened from the heavy form, and it is mostly left without effect; (كنا) is kāna and its noun; the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa), and (مبتلين) is the khabar of (كنا). It is also permissible that its noun be the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) and the clause its khabar; and it is permissible that (إن) be negating and the lām mean "except" (illā). (ثُمَّ أَنْشَأْنا مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ قَرْناً آخَرِينَ) (ثم) is a conjunction expressing delay (tarākhī); (أنشأنا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (من بعدهم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (قرنا) is a mafʿūl bihi, meaning "a people"; (آخرين) is an adjective; they are the people of ʿĀd. (فَأَرْسَلْنا فِيهِمْ رَسُولًا مِنْهُمْ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (أرسلنا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (فيهم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أرسل); (رسولا) is a mafʿūl bihi and (منهم) is an adjective. (أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ ما لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلهٍ غَيْرُهُ أَفَلا تَتَّقُونَ) (أن) is explicative (mufassira), because sending carries the meaning of saying without its letters, i.e. We said to them through the tongue of the messenger: worship Allah; moreover, the sending of messengers is for conveying [the message]. It is also permissible that it be maṣdariyya, forming with what follows an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "with: worship", the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (أرسلنا). The rest has been parsed recently in exactly these words, so refresh your memory of it. (وَقالَ الْمَلَأُ مِنْ قَوْمِهِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِلِقاءِ الْآخِرَةِ وَأَتْرَفْناهُمْ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا) The wāw is a conjunction; (قال الملأ) is a verb and its fāʿil. The clause containing their false speech is conjoined to his true speech, so the conjunction here is to show the contrast. A like expression occurred earlier in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf without the wāw, as though it were the answer to an implied question, so it did not need it. (من قومه) is a ḥāl; (الذين) is an adjective of (قومه); the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause), and what follows is conjoined to it and falls within its scope. He described them at length to show the enormity of what they committed in ingratitude for the blessings and denial of the blessings heaped upon them one after another, so as to then cite, on their tongues, two of the specious arguments of the unbelievers, upon which they built their denial of the resurrection and their attack on his messengership, upon him be peace. (ما هذا إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ يَأْكُلُ مِمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ مِنْهُ وَيَشْرَبُ مِمَّا تَشْرَبُونَ) (ما) is negating; (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (بشر) is the khabar; (مثلكم) is an adjective; the clause (يأكل) is a second adjective; (مما) is attached to (يأكل); the clause (تأكلون) is the ṣila, and you may make (ما) maṣdariyya, i.e. "of what you eat"; likewise His saying (ويشرب مما يشربون) [Translator's note: so in the source; the Qur'anic text reads (تشربون)]. The returning pronoun is omitted from the second, the first returning pronoun, which is (منه), sufficing. The whole clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and it contains the first specious argument.
(وَلَئِنْ أَطَعْتُمْ بَشَراً مِثْلَكُمْ إِنَّكُمْ إِذاً لَخاسِرُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); (إن) is conditional; (أطعتم) is a verb and its fāʿil, in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (بشرا) is a mafʿūl bihi and (مثلكم) an adjective; (إن) and its noun, the shifted lām, and (خاسرون) its khabar. As for (إذن): this is not the one that puts the imperfect verb in the accusative; rather it is the conditional (إذا) whose clause, to which it is annexed, was omitted and the tanwīn substituted for it, as in (يومئذ). For this reason it is not restricted to entering upon the imperfect, but enters upon the past and upon the noun. It occurs often in the Qur'an, as in «إنكم إذن من المقربين», where it has entered upon the noun, and of its entering upon the past is His saying «وإذن لآتيناهم». This states their second specious argument. The clause is the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), because the oath comes first, according to the rule. (أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذا مِتُّمْ وَكُنْتُمْ تُراباً وَعِظاماً أَنَّكُمْ مُخْرَجُونَ) The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and of deeming something far-fetched; the clause (يعدكم) is resumptive, introduced to reinforce what preceded it, namely their deterring [people] from following him, by denying the occurrence of that which he calls them to believe in and deeming it far-fetched. (يعدكم) is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "he"; the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi, and (أن) with what falls within its scope is in the position of the accusative as a second mafʿūl bihi; (أن), its noun, and (مخرجون) its khabar; (إذا) is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (مخرجون), and the clause (متم) is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; (كنتم ترابا وعظاما) is conjoined to (إذا متم). The second (أنكم) is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the first, since the separation between the noun of inna, which is the kāf, and its khabar, which is (مخرجون), grew long; and since it is merely for verbal emphasis, it did not need a khabar. This is one of several views the grammarians mentioned; we shall come to them in the Benefits section, for they are all sound, and what we have mentioned is the easiest of them.
(هَيْهاتَ هَيْهاتَ لِما تُوعَدُونَ) (هيهات) is a verbal noun with the sense of a past verb (ism fiʿl māḍin), meaning "it is far"; it will be discussed at length in the Benefits section. The second is a verbal emphasis of it; the lām is redundant (zāʾida); (ما) is a relative noun, the fāʿil of the verbal noun, which is (هيهات); its near position is the genitive by the redundant lām and its remote position is the nominative as the fāʿil of (هيهات). It is also permissible that (ما) be maṣdariyya and the interpreted maṣdar be the fāʿil of (هيهات). More views on the i'rab of this construction will come in the Benefits section.

* Benefits:
1- On His saying «أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذا مِتُّمْ», the verse: the opinions of the leading grammarians and exegetes differed over the i'rab of this verse. In the i'rab we mentioned what we saw as most accessible and closest to logic, and here we will present to you what they said, for its merit, and so that you may see what you choose. Sībawayh said: the khabar of the first «أن» is omitted because the khabar of the second indicates it, its implied form being «أنكم مخرجون», and it is what governs the adverb; and the second «أن» with what falls within its scope is a badal (substitute) of the first.
Al-Jarmī, al-Mubarrad and al-Farrāʾ held that the khabar of the first «أن» is (مخرجون), and it is what governs «إذا», and the second was repeated for emphasis since the separation grew long; this is the view we chose.
Abū al-Baqāʾ chose that the noun of the first is omitted [Translator's note: i.e. a muḍāf is omitted], the muḍāf ilayhi being put in its place, the implied form being "that your bringing forth", with «إذا» as the khabar, and «أنكم مخرجون» a repetition, because «أن» and what it governs are for emphasis or to indicate what was omitted.
It was also said that «أنكم مخرجون» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the adverb fronted before it, and the clause is a khabar of the first «أنكم», the implied meaning being: does he promise you that your bringing forth is occurring, or established, at the time of your death? It is not permissible for the governor of «إذا» to be (مخرجون), because what falls within the scope of «أن» does not govern what precedes it; nor does «متم» govern it, because it is a muḍāf ilayhi. (أنكم) with what falls within its scope is in the position of the accusative or the genitive after the omission of the preposition, since the original is "does he promise you with [the fact] that you…"; and it is permissible not to assume a preposition, so that it is in the position of the accusative only, as in "I promised Zayd good".
2- هيهات:
There are many dialectal forms of this word, exceeding forty. We mention below the best known of them and those in which it has been read. The well-known one is (هيهات) with fatḥa on the tāʾ and no tanwīn; it is indeclinable (mabnī) because it occupies the place of an indeclinable [i.e. the verb], or because of its resemblance to the particle; the generality read it so, and it is the dialect of the Ḥijāzīs. Then (هيهاتا) with fatḥa and tanwīn; (هيهات) with ḍamma and tanwīn, and with ḍamma without tanwīn; (هيهات) with kasra and tanwīn, and with kasra without tanwīn; (هيهات) with a sukūn on the tāʾ; (هيهه) with a hāʾ at the end, both in continuous reading and in pausing; and (أيهات), replacing the hāʾ with a hamza, with fatḥa on the tāʾ. These are nine forms; it has been read in all of them, but none of them is mutawātir except the first. It is permissible to replace the first hāʾ with a hamza in all the foregoing, which brings the number to sixteen forms [Translator's note: so in the source]; also (ايهان) with a nūn at the end and (ايها) with an alif at the end. The noun after it occurs in the nominative by it, as the fāʿil is made nominative by its verb, because it functions like the verb and so requires a fāʿil as the verb requires one. Jarīr said:
فهيهات هيهات العقيق ومن به ... وهيهات خلّ بالعقيق نواصله
(Far, far away is al-ʿAqīq and whoever is in it, and far away is a friend at al-ʿAqīq with whom we keep company.)
Al-ʿAqīq is a valley at Medina, about which Jarīr says, and excels:
ولم أنس يوما بالعقيق تخايلت ... ضحاه وطابت بالعشي أصائله
(I have not forgotten a day at al-ʿAqīq whose forenoon was splendid and whose late afternoons were pleasant at evening.)
رزقنا به الصيد العزيز ولم نكن ... كمن نبله محرومة وحبائله
(In it we were granted precious game, and we were not like one whose arrows and snares come away empty.)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: "What you are promised" is what is deemed far, and it ought to be made nominative by (هيهات), as it is made nominative in his saying "فهيهات هيهات العقيق وأهله"; so what is this lām? I say: al-Zajjāj said in his commentary: "Remoteness to what you are promised", or "a remoteness to what you are promised" for those who read it with tanwīn, so he treated it as a maṣdar. There is another view: that the lām is to explain what is deemed far, after the utterance of the word of deeming-far, just as the lām came in (هيت لك) to explain the one being called.» What we chose in the i'rab is easier and closer.

dervis-irab:37-43.t:
* Vocabulary:
(غُثاءً): al-ghuthāʾ is what the flood carries along; similar to it is al-jufāʾ. It is also what has broken up and been crushed of pasture when it dries. Its plural is aghthiya, like ghurāb and aghriba, and ghuthyān, like ghurāb and ghirbān. Al-Zajjāj said: it is the decayed leaves of trees when the flood runs and mixes with its foam. It was also said: it is the refuse and filth the flood throws up, of which no use is made. Its final radical is wāw, because it is from ghathā al-wādī, yaghthū, ghathwan [the valley carried scum], and likewise the cooking-pot. As for ghathiyat nafsuhu, taghthā, ghathayānan, i.e. [his soul] became nauseated, it is close to it in meaning but is from a root with yāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «He likened them in their destruction to ghuthāʾ, which is what the flood carries of decayed things and of what has blackened among decayed sticks and leaves.»

* I'rab:
(إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا حَياتُنَا الدُّنْيا نَمُوتُ وَنَحْيا وَما نَحْنُ بِمَبْعُوثِينَ) A resumptive clause, introduced to state their belief that the world is eternal by nature, has always been so and was not brought into being by a creator, and that people are like plants: they sprout and return through death to dry stubble. This is open unbelief and far error; more on the belief of the Dahriyya (materialists) will come in the Benefits section. (إن) is negating; (هي) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (حياتنا) is the khabar (predicate) and (الدنيا) an adjective. The clause (نموت ونحيا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), or explicative of their claim that their life is the life of this world, i.e. some of us die and some of us pass away until the age passes away. The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negating mā; (نحن) is its noun; in (بمبعوثين) the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (مبعوثين) is genitive by the bāʾ in form and the khabar of mā in position. (إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا رَجُلٌ افْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً وَما نَحْنُ لَهُ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ) (إن) is negating; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (رجل) is the khabar; the clause (افترى) is an adjective; (على الله) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (افترى); (كذبا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is the Ḥijāzī mā; (نحن) is its noun; (له) is attached to (مؤمنين); (مؤمنين) is, in its near position, genitive by the redundant bāʾ, and in its remote position the khabar of mā. (قالَ رَبِّ انْصُرْنِي بِما كَذَّبُونِ) (قال) is a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent, its implied form being "he"; (رب) is the one addressed (munādā), with the vocative particle omitted, muḍāf to the omitted yāʾ of the first person; (انصرني) is an imperative verb meaning supplication; the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya) and the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "you". In (بما) the bāʾ is a preposition and (ما) is relative or maṣdariyya; (كذبوني) is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the ṣila of (ما); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (انصرني). (قالَ عَمَّا قَلِيلٍ لَيُصْبِحُنَّ نادِمِينَ) (عما قليل): (عن) is a preposition, (ما) is redundant and (قليل) is genitive by (عن); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (يصبحن), or to (نادمين), or to an omitted [verb], its implied form being "after a little We will give victory", omitted because what precedes it, namely (رب انصرني), indicates it. The lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); (يصبحن) is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb; the wāw, omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is its noun; it is nominative by the retention of the nūn, which was omitted because of the succession of identical letters; the doubled nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis; (نادمين) is the khabar of (يصبحن). (فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الصَّيْحَةُ بِالْحَقِّ فَجَعَلْناهُمْ غُثاءً فَبُعْداً لِلْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (أخذتهم الصيحة) is a verb, a mafʿūl bihi and a fāʿil; (بالحق) is a ḥāl of (الصيحة). (فجعلناهم) is conjoined to (فأخذتهم); the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi and (غثاء) the second. The fāʾ is a conjunction; (بعدا) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) mentioned as a substitute for uttering its verb, so it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb that must remain unexpressed, because it carries the sense of an imprecation against them; the original is "they became remote, a remoteness". (للقوم) is an adjective of (بعدا) and is not attached to it, because the omission of this lām and the maṣdar reaching its genitive noun directly is never attested. The overt noun is put in place of the pronoun to give the reason. (ثُمَّ أَنْشَأْنا مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ قُرُوناً آخَرِينَ) (ثم) is a conjunction expressing delay; (أنشأنا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (من بعدهم) is attached to an omitted ḥāl; (قرونا) is a mafʿūl bihi and (آخرين) an adjective. (ما تَسْبِقُ مِنْ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلَها وَما يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ) (ما) is negating; (تسبق) is an imperfect verb; (من) is a redundant preposition and (أمة) is genitive in form and nominative in position, because it is the fāʿil of (تسبق); (أجلها) is a mafʿūl bihi; (وما يستأخرون) is conjoined to what precedes. The pronoun is made masculine after being made feminine out of regard for the meaning, because (أمة) means "a people".

* Benefits:
In the Commentary on the Nahj by Ibn Abī al-Ḥadīd: «The Chief Judge said: none of the rational people has held the denial of a Maker of the world; but a group of the copyists (warrāqūn) gathered and composed among themselves a doctrine that no one had held, namely that the world is eternal, has always been in this state of its, that the world has no god and no maker at all, and that it is simply so, always has been and always will be, without a maker or an effecting cause. Among the best known of the Arabs who took up this doctrine is Ibn al-Rāwandī; he took up this doctrine and championed it in his book known as Kitāb al-Tāj.» I say: Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī mentioned Ibn al-Rāwandī and this Tāj of his in Risālat al-Ghufrān, and among what he said is: «As for Ibn al-Rāwandī, he was not guided to what is right; and as for his Tāj (crown), it is not fit to be a fillet; and is his Tāj anything but as the soothsayer woman said: uff and tuff, a sock and a slipper.» About these people Abū al-ʿAlāʾ says in his Luzūmiyyāt:
ضل الذي قال البلاد قديمة ... بالطبع كانت والأنام كنبتها
(He has gone astray who said the lands are eternal, existing by nature, and mankind like their vegetation.)
وأمامنا يوم تقوم هجوده ... من بعد إبلاء العظام ورفتها
(Before us lies a day when its sleepers will rise, after the bones have decayed and crumbled.)

dervis-irab:44-50.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَتْرا) will come in the I'rab section.
(رَبْوَةٍ): al-rabwa and al-rabāwa: raised ground; the rāʾ in both may take any of the three vowels. The exegetes differed over what is meant by it: it was said Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis), and it was said Damascus and its Ghūṭa; from al-Ḥasan: Palestine and al-Ramla.
(مَعِينٍ): a passive participle from ʿāna, yaʿīnu, like bāʿa, yabīʿu, so it is maʿīn like mabīʿ; the mīm is augmentative and its original form is maʿyūn, like mabyūʿ, and it has undergone vowel-weakening (iʿlāl). Al-maʿīn is visible water running on the surface of the earth. There is disagreement as to whether its mīm is augmentative or radical. The argument of those who make it a passive participle is that it is perceived by the eye (ʿayn) because it is visible, from ʿānahu when he perceived it with his eye, like rakabahu when he struck him with his knee (rukba). The argument of those who make it of the pattern faʿīl is that it is very beneficial through its being visible and running, from al-māʿūn, which is benefit. Al-Rāghib said: it is from maʿana al-māʾ, [the water] ran; a watercourse is called miʿyān; amʿana al-faras, the horse went far in its running; amʿana bi-ḥaqqī, he made off with my right; and so-and-so is maʿin in his errand, i.e. quick.

* I'rab:
(ثُمَّ أَرْسَلْنا رُسُلَنا تَتْرا) (ثم) is a conjunction expressing delay; (أرسلنا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (رسلنا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (تترى): the tāʾ is substituted for a wāw, its original being (وترى). It is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like shabʿā and daʿwā, so its alif is for the feminine; it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "following one another", being a maṣdar occurring in the position of a ḥāl. It is also permissible that it be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being "a sending tatrā", i.e. successive. On its alif there are three views:
1- It is for assimilation (ilḥāq) to jaʿfar, like the alif in arṭā; for this reason it is [given the tāʾ of] the feminine [Translator's note: the source has «تؤنث»; the usual statement is that it takes tanwīn (تنوّن)] in the view of those who make it fully declinable.
2- It is a substitute for the tanwīn.
3- It is for the feminine, like sakrā; for this reason it takes no tanwīn in the view of those who make it a diptote.
(كُلَّ ما جاءَ أُمَّةً رَسُولُها كَذَّبُوهُ) (كلما) is an adverb (ẓarf) containing the sense of a condition; the clause (جاء أمة) is either annexed to it or has no grammatical position; the detailed discussion of (كلما) has preceded. (أمة) is a fronted mafʿūl bihi and (رسولها) a postponed fāʿil; the clause (كذبوه) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (فَأَتْبَعْنا بَعْضَهُمْ بَعْضاً وَجَعَلْناهُمْ أَحادِيثَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (أتبعنا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (بعضهم) is the first mafʿūl bihi and (بعضا) the second; (جعلناهم) is conjoined to (أتبعنا); the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi and (أحاديث) the second. (الأحاديث) may be a quasi-plural noun (ism jamʿ) of ḥadīth, and from it are the aḥādīth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; or it may be the plural of uḥdūtha, which is like uḍḥūka, ulʿūba and uʿjūba: that which people talk about to pass their idle time, seek consolation, ward off boredom, and for wonder and amusement. In al-Qāmūs: «It is said: ṣārū aḥādīth, i.e. they passed away.» (فَبُعْداً لِقَوْمٍ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ) The fāʾ is resumptive; (بعدا) is the maṣdar of an omitted verb, i.e. "they became remote, a remoteness", and this is an imprecation against them. As for (لقوم), the discussion of this lām has preceded recently, so refresh your memory of it; the clause (لا يؤمنون) is an adjective of (قوم). (ثُمَّ أَرْسَلْنا مُوسى وَأَخاهُ هارُونَ بِآياتِنا وَسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ) (ثم) is a conjunction expressing delay; (أرسلنا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (موسى) is a mafʿūl bihi; (أخاه) is conjoined to it; (هارون) is a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); (بآياتنا) is a ḥāl, i.e. while both were accompanied by Our signs, so the bāʾ is for accompaniment (mulābasa). (سلطان مبين) is conjoined to (آياتنا); these are the signs he brought. (سلطان) was conjoined to (آياتنا) only because of the excellence by which those prefiguring signs were distinguished, so that it is as though it were not one of them; otherwise a thing is not conjoined to itself. Among those decisive, clear proofs are the hand and the staff.
(إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَائِهِ فَاسْتَكْبَرُوا وَكانُوا قَوْماً عالِينَ) (إلى فرعون) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أرسلنا); (ملئه) is conjoined to (فرعون); (فاستكبروا) is conjoined to (أرسلنا); (كانوا قوما عالين) is kāna, its noun and its khabar (predicate). The meaning of (عالين) is "arrogant", or "overbearing towards people, subduing them by transgression and injustice". Allah, glorified be He, indicated this in another verse, saying: «وإن فرعون علا في الأرض». (فَقالُوا أَنُؤْمِنُ لِبَشَرَيْنِ مِثْلِنا وَقَوْمُهُما لَنا عابِدُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (قالوا) is a verb and its fāʿil, the pronoun referring to Pharaoh and his chiefs; the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval; (نؤمن) is an imperfect verb; (لبشرين) is attached to (نؤمن). (البشر) applies to the singular, the dual and the plural, the masculine and the feminine. (مثلنا) is an adjective; it is like (غير) in that two, a plural, a masculine and a feminine may be described by them. Allah the Exalted said: «إنكم إذن مثلهم», and He said: «ومن الأرض مثلهن». It is also said: humā mithlāhu and hum amthāluhu. (وقومهما): the wāw is circumstantial; (قومهما) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (لنا) is attached to (عابدون), and (عابدون) is the khabar of (قومهما).
(فَكَذَّبُوهُما فَكانُوا مِنَ الْمُهْلَكِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (كذبوهما) is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; (فكانوا) is conjoined to (كذبوهما); kāna and its noun, and (من المهلكين) its khabar. (وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسَى الْكِتابَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ) The wāw is resumptive; (قد) is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (آتينا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (موسى) is the first mafʿūl bihi and (الكتاب) the second; laʿalla and its noun; the pronoun refers to Moses' people, because Pharaoh and his people had perished by drowning. (وَجَعَلْنَا ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ وَأُمَّهُ آيَةً) The wāw is a conjunction; (جعلنا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (ابن مريم) is the first mafʿūl bihi; (أمه) is conjoined to (ابن مريم); (آية) is the second mafʿūl bihi. He did not say "two signs" because the sign in the two of them is one, namely birth without a father. Had He said "two signs" it would have been acceptable, because Mary gave birth without being touched, and Jesus is a spirit from Allah cast into her; he spoke in the cradle and used to bring the dead to life, along with other miracles, so he was a sign in more than one respect. (وَآوَيْناهُما إِلى رَبْوَةٍ ذاتِ قَرارٍ وَمَعِينٍ) (آويناهما) is conjoined to (جعلنا), i.e. We settled them both; (إلى ربوة) is attached to (آويناهما), and its discussion has preceded; (ذات) is an adjective of (ربوة) and (قرار) is muḍāf ilayhi. The meaning of (القرار) is settling, i.e. We made it suitable for settling in, through the crops, resources [Translator's note: the source has «طاقات»], fruits and water in it. (معين) is conjoined to (قرار).

dervis-irab:51-56.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الرُّسُلُ كُلُوا مِنَ الطَّيِّباتِ) (يا أيها الرسل): its i'rab has preceded. The address is to all the prophets, according to the differences of the far-apart times between them. (كلوا) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (من الطيبات) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كلوا). What is meant by "good things" is what is lawful and wholesome. (وَاعْمَلُوا صالِحاً إِنِّي بِما تَعْمَلُونَ عَلِيمٌ) (اعملوا) is conjoined to (كلوا); (صالحا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). The clause (إني) gives the reason for the command; inna and its noun; (بما) is attached to (عليم); the clause (تعملون) is the ṣila (relative clause); and (عليم) is the khabar (predicate) of inna. (وَإِنَّ هذِهِ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً وَأَنَا رَبُّكُمْ فَاتَّقُونِ) The wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, introduced to draw attention to the orderliness of this community's affair and the perfection of its rightness. Inna and its noun; (أمتكم) is its khabar; (أمة) is a necessary (lāzima) ḥāl (circumstantial) and (واحدة) an adjective. In (وأنا) the wāw is a conjunction; (أنا) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (ربكم) the khabar. In (فاتقون) the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition); (اتقوني) is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the omission of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ, omitted following the orthography of the Muṣḥaf, is a mafʿūl bihi. (فَتَقَطَّعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ زُبُراً كُلُّ حِزْبٍ بِما لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ) The fāʾ is resumptive; (تقطعوا) is a past verb and the wāw its fāʿil. (أمرهم): its i'rab preceded in [Sūrat] al-Anbiyāʾ, namely that it is either accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. they split up in their affair, or it is a mafʿūl bihi, (تقطعوا) being made transitive to it because it has the meaning of (قطعوا). (بينهم) is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (تقطعوا); (زبرا) is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of (تقطعوا), i.e. as mutually opposed factions. (الزبر) is the plural of zubra, meaning a piece, or the plural of zabūr, meaning a group; it has another plural, which preceded in [Sūrat] al-Kahf, namely zubar with fatḥa on the bāʾ. (كل) is a mubtadaʾ and (حزب) muḍāf ilayhi; (بما) is attached to (فرحون); (لديهم) is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila; and (فرحون) is the khabar of (كل حزب). (فَذَرْهُمْ فِي غَمْرَتِهِمْ حَتَّى حِينٍ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; (ذرهم) is an imperative verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil, its implied form being "you", and the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi. The address is to Muhammad ﷺ and the pronoun refers to the unbelievers of Mecca. (في غمرتهم) is a ḥāl, i.e. floundering in their confusion, or a second object of (ذر), i.e. leave them floundering in their confusion. (حتى) is a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition; (حين) is genitive by (حتى), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (ذرهم). (أَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّما نُمِدُّهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ مالٍ وَبَنِينَ) The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and reproach; (يحسبون) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; (أن) and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of (يحسبون). (أن), and (ما) is its noun; it ought to have been written separately, but it was written joined following the orthography of the Muṣḥaf. The clause (نمدهم) is the ṣila; (به) is attached to (نمدهم); (من مال وبنين) is a ḥāl of the relative noun. (نُسارِعُ لَهُمْ فِي الْخَيْراتِ بَلْ لا يَشْعُرُونَ) The clause is the khabar of (أن). (نسارع) is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "we"; (لهم) is attached to (نسارع); (في الخيرات) is a ḥāl. (بل) is a particle of transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī) away from [their] supposition; (لا) is negating; (يشعرون) is a verb and its fāʿil, conjoined to an implied [clause] over which the speech extends, i.e. We do not do that; rather they perceive nothing at all, like cattle, having no discernment and no perception that would allow them to reflect and so know that this supply is nothing but a leading of them on by degrees (istidrāj) and a drawing of them into more sin.

dervis-irab:57-63.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ هُمْ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ رَبِّهِمْ مُشْفِقُونَ) The clause is initial and resumptive, introduced to mention the righteous who are apprehensive out of fear of their Lord. Inna and its noun; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (من خشية ربهم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (مشفقون); (مشفقون) is the khabar (predicate) of (هم). The maṣdar (verbal noun), (خشية), is annexed to its object, i.e. fearing His punishment. The clause (هم من خشية ربهم مشفقون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين). In (الإشفاق) there is a meaning that adds to the meaning of (الخشية): the meaning of tenderness and weakness.
(وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ بِآياتِ رَبِّهِمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ) Conjoined to the previous clause, and its i'rab is like it; the clause (يؤمنون) is their khabar. (وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْتُونَ ما آتَوْا وَقُلُوبُهُمْ وَجِلَةٌ أَنَّهُمْ إِلى رَبِّهِمْ راجِعُونَ) Also conjoined to (إن الذين). The clause (يؤتون) is the ṣila of (الذين); (ما) is the object of (يؤتون), and the clause (آتوا) is the ṣila. In (وقلوبهم) the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (قلوبهم) is a mubtadaʾ and (وجلة) its khabar. (أنهم): (أن) and what follows it are accusative by removal of the preposition, and it gives the reason for His saying (وجلة); the implied form is "fearful of that they…", i.e. afraid of their return to their Lord. (أن) and its noun; (إلى ربهم) is attached to (راجعون), and (راجعون) is the khabar of (أنهم). (أُولئِكَ يُسارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْراتِ وَهُمْ لَها سابِقُونَ) The clause is the khabar of (إن الذين هم من خشية ربهم) and what is conjoined to it; so the noun of inna is four relative nouns and its khabar is the clause (أولئك). (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يسارعون) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; (في الخيرات) is attached to (يسارعون). The wāw is a conjunction and the clause is conjoined to the one before it, serving as an emphasis of it. (هم) is a mubtadaʾ; (لها) is attached to (سابقون); (سابقون) is their khabar. The pronoun in (لها) refers to (الخيرات) because it precedes it in wording, and this is what is apparent from the context; it was also said that it refers to Paradise, and that is not far-fetched. The object of (سابقون) is omitted, i.e. outstripping people to them; one says sabaqa lahu and sabaqa ilayhi. It is also permissible that the lām be causal, i.e. outstripping [others] for their sake. (وَلا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْساً إِلَّا وُسْعَها)
The wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, introduced to indicate that the imposition of obligation does not go beyond the limits of capacities and abilities. (لا) is negating; (نكلف) is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent, its implied form being "we"; (نفسا) is the first object of (نكلف); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (وسعها) is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (وَلَدَيْنا كِتابٌ يَنْطِقُ بِالْحَقِّ وَهُمْ لا يُظْلَمُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (لدينا) is an adverb attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (كتاب) is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause (ينطق) is an adjective; (بالحق) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. accompanied by the truth. In (وهم) the wāw is a conjunction; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (لا يظلمون) the khabar. (بَلْ قُلُوبُهُمْ فِي غَمْرَةٍ مِنْ هذا) (بل) is a particle of digression (iḍrāb), for moving on to the narrated states of the unbelievers; (قلوبهم) is a mubtadaʾ; (في غمرة) is the khabar; (من هذا) is an adjective of (غمرة), i.e. arising from this with which the believers have been described. (وَلَهُمْ أَعْمالٌ مِنْ دُونِ ذلِكَ هُمْ لَها عامِلُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (لهم) is a fronted khabar and (أعمال) a postponed mubtadaʾ; (من دون ذلك) is an adjective of (أعمال); the clause (هم…) is a second adjective of (أعمال). (هم) is a mubtadaʾ; (لها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (عاملون); and (عاملون) is the khabar of (هم), i.e. persisting in them. The meaning of (من دون ذلك) is: going beyond and exceeding what the believers have been described with.

dervis-irab:64-70.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُتْرَفِيهِمْ): their rich men and their chiefs.
(يَجْأَرُونَ): they cry out clamorously. In al-Qāmūs: «jaʾara, like manaʿa, jaʾran and juʾāran: he raised his voice in supplication, humbled himself and cried for help; [said of] the cow and the bull: they lowed; of a plant: it grew tall; of the land: its vegetation grew tall; al-juʾār, of plants: the fresh and the abundant; and the bulky man.» In al-Lisān and al-Asās he said: al-juʾār is crying out for help.
(تَنْكِصُونَ): in al-Mukhtār there is what indicates that it belongs to both the pattern of jalasa and that of dakhala, and the maṣdar is nukūṣ.
(سامِراً): al-sāmir is taken from al-samar, which is staying up at night. Al-Rāghib said: al-sāmir is the dark night [Translator's note: so in the source]. It is a quasi-plural noun (ism jamʿ), like ḥājj, ḥāḍir, rākib and ghāʾib. They used to gather around the House at night conversing (yasmurūn), and most of their night-talk was mention of the Qur'an, calling it sorcery and poetry, and reviling the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
(تَهْجُرُونَ): with fatḥa on the tāʾ, it is from al-hijrān, which is abandoning; or from hajara, hajran: he raved and spoke senselessly because of illness or the like. It has been read with ḍamma on it, from ahjara, ihjāran: he spoke obscenely.

* I'rab:
(حَتَّى إِذا أَخَذْنا مُتْرَفِيهِمْ بِالْعَذابِ إِذا هُمْ يَجْأَرُونَ) (حتى) here is inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya): speech begins with it. (إذا) is an adverb (ẓarf) for future time, putting its condition in the genitive and made accusative by its apodosis, which is (يجأرون). The clause (أخذنا) is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; (نا) is the fāʿil (agent), (مترفيهم) the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and (بالعذاب) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أخذنا). The second (إذا) is the particle of surprise (mufājaʾa), standing in place of the fāʾ of the apodosis as a link, and the clause after it is the apodosis of the first (إذا), with no grammatical position, as though it were said: "then they cry out". It was also said that (حتى) is a particle of limit and a preposition.
(لا تَجْأَرُوا الْيَوْمَ إِنَّكُمْ مِنَّا لا تُنْصَرُونَ) (لا) is prohibitive; (تجأروا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا), and the wāw is the fāʿil; (اليوم) is attached to (تجأروا). (إنكم) gives the reason for the prohibition; inna and its noun; (منا) is attached to (تنصرون); (لا) is negating; the clause (تنصرون) is the khabar (predicate) of (إنكم), and the wāw is a nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (قَدْ كانَتْ آياتِي تُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ فَكُنْتُمْ عَلى أَعْقابِكُمْ تَنْكِصُونَ) (قد) is a particle of realisation; (كانت آياتي) is kāna and its noun; the clause (تتلى) is its khabar; (عليكم) is attached to (تتلى). In (فكنتم) the fāʾ is a conjunction, and kāna and its noun; (على أعقابكم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of (تنكصون), and the clause (تنكصون) is the khabar of (كنتم).
(مُسْتَكْبِرِينَ بِهِ سامِراً تَهْجُرُونَ) (مستكبرين) is a second ḥāl of the fāʿil of (تنكصون); (به) is attached to (مستكبرين), i.e. because of it. The pronoun in (به) refers to the Ancient House and the Sanctuary; it was also said that it refers to the Qur'an. (سامرا) is a third ḥāl and the clause (تهجرون) a fourth ḥāl; so they are overlapping (mutadākhila) ḥāls, i.e. each one [is a ḥāl] of what precedes it. (أَفَلَمْ يَدَّبَّرُوا الْقَوْلَ أَمْ جاءَهُمْ ما لَمْ يَأْتِ آباءَهُمُ الْأَوَّلِينَ) The clause is resumptive, introduced to explain the reasons for their riding the back of error; it will be seen that they are five, and we shall point to them in their places. The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and affirmation (taqrīr); (لم) is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and jussive; (يدبروا) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لم); (القول) is a mafʿūl bihi. The fāʾ conjoins to an omitted [clause] upon which the hamza entered, i.e. they did what they did, of what has been mentioned, and did they not then ponder the word? (أم) is a conjunction in the sense of the transitional (بل), i.e. "nay, has there come to them…", "nay, did they not know…", "nay, do they say…". His saying (أفلم يدبروا القول) is the first reason for their venturing upon error and their daring to commit it, i.e. they turned away from reflecting on the proofs of his prophethood ﷺ, foremost among them the inimitable Qur'an. (جاءهم) is a verb and a second [Translator's note: so in the source; it is simply the mafʿūl bihi] mafʿūl bihi; (ما) is a relative noun, the fāʿil; the clause (لم يأت آباءهم الأولين) is the ṣila (relative clause). This is the second reason: their belief that the sending of Muhammad ﷺ was something strange, because it had not been heard of among the past nations.
(أَمْ لَمْ يَعْرِفُوا رَسُولَهُمْ فَهُمْ لَهُ مُنْكِرُونَ) Conjoined to what precedes, as we mentioned. This is the third reason for their venturing to ride error: their not knowing the trustworthiness of the claimant to messengership and his truthfulness before he claimed it. But the matter is not like this; rather they had sounded his depths, known his reality, grasped his truthfulness to its core, and given him the title al-Amīn (the Trustworthy). So how did they belie him after they had agreed unanimously that he was worthy of the title they bestowed on him? The fāʾ is a conjunction; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (له) is attached to (منكرون); (منكرون) is their khabar.
(أَمْ يَقُولُونَ بِهِ جِنَّةٌ بَلْ جاءَهُمْ بِالْحَقِّ وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ لِلْحَقِّ كارِهُونَ) Also conjoined to what precedes. This is the fourth reason: their believing him to be mad; and this belief contradicts what they used to believe about him of perfect sound judgement and complete good sense. (به) is a fronted khabar and (جنة), i.e. madness, a postponed mubtadaʾ. (بل) is a conjunction and a particle of transitional digression; (جاءهم) is a verb, a mafʿūl bihi and a latent fāʿil; (بالحق) is attached to (جاءهم) or to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. accompanied by the truth. The wāw is circumstantial; (أكثرهم) is a mubtadaʾ; (للحق) is attached to (كارهون); and (كارهون) is the khabar of (أكثرهم).

* Benefits:
The meaning of (وأكثرهم):
Al-Zamakhsharī raised an objection against himself, putting a question to himself and answering it. The following is the text of the question and the answer; he said: «If you say: His saying "وأكثرهم" implies that the fewer of them did not dislike the truth, I say: there were among them those who refrained from believing in it out of disdain and haughty refusal of their people's reproach, and of their saying "he has turned renegade (ṣabaʾa) and abandoned the religion of his forefathers", not out of dislike of the truth, as is related about Abū Ṭālib.
If you say: some people claim that Abū Ṭālib's Islam is established, I say:
Glory be to Allah! As if Abū Ṭālib were the most obscure of the uncles of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so that the Islam of Ḥamza and al-ʿAbbās became well known while his Islam remained hidden!»
This is fine on the part of al-Zamakhsharī, but more appropriate than that is that the pronoun in His saying «وأكثرهم» refer to the genus, to mankind as a whole; when He mentioned this group from the genus, He built the speech in His saying (وأكثرهم) on the genus in its entirety, as in His saying:
«إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين» and His saying: «وما أكثر الناس ولو حرصت بمؤمنين». This is indicated by His saying «بَلْ جاءَهُمْ بِالْحَقِّ», and the Prophet ﷺ came to all people and was sent to everyone. It is also possible that "most" be taken to mean "all", just as "few" is taken to mean negation. As for al-Zamakhsharī's saying that whoever persisted in unbelief and preferred to remain in it in imitation of his forefathers does not dislike the truth, it is rejected: whoever loves a thing dislikes its opposite, so if they loved remaining in unbelief, they necessarily disliked moving from it to faith. Then the discussion was drawn on to deeming Abū Ṭālib's faith unlikely, and to establishing that he died in unbelief; he argued this on the grounds that he was the best known of the Prophet's ﷺ uncles, so had he accepted Islam his Islam would have become well known, as the Islam of al-ʿAbbās and Ḥamza became well known, since he was better known. But one who holds that he accepted Islam may excuse its not being well known by [saying] that he only accepted Islam shortly before the throes of death, so he had no stands in Islam for which he would become well known, as others among his uncles became well known.

dervis-irab:71-76.t:
* Vocabulary:
(خَرْجاً): a wage and tribute (kharāj). Kharj is mostly used for the levy on persons (literally "money of the neck") and kharāj for the levy on landed property, and [kharj is] the opposite of dakhl (income). It was also said: kharj is what you give voluntarily and kharāj is what you are obliged to pay. The [correct] view is that kharj is more specific than kharāj. The meaning of the verse is: or do you ask them, for your guiding them, for a little of the giving of creatures? The abundance of the Creator's giving is better.
(ناكبون): deviating, swerving and inclining away; everyone who does not believe in the Hereafter deviates from the right course.
(لجوا): al-lajāj is persisting in obstinacy. In al-Miṣbāḥ: lajja fī al-amr, lajajan, on the pattern of taʿiba, and lajājan and lajāja, so he is lajūj, and lajūja as an intensive, when he clings to a thing and keeps at it; on the pattern of ḍaraba it is a dialectal form.
(يَعْمَهُونَ): in al-Miṣbāḥ: «ʿamiha fī ṭughyānihi, ʿamahan, on the pattern of taʿiba, when he wavers in bewilderment; and taʿāmaha is taken from their saying arḍ ʿamhāʾ, when there are no signs in it pointing to safety; so he is ʿamih and aʿmah.» [Translator's note: the closing quotation mark is missing in the source.]
(اسْتَكانُوا): it is said: istakāna, i.e. he moved from one state of being (kawn) to another, like istaḥāla when he moves from one condition (ḥāl) to another. Its original form is istakwana: the vowel of the wāw was transferred to the letter before it, then [the wāw] was changed to an alif. This is what the lexicologists said. But some of them objected to this comparison, their argument being that istakāna, on this interpretation, is one of the kinds of istafʿala whose meaning is transformation, as in their saying istaḥjara al-ṭīn (the clay turned to stone) and istanwaqa al-jamal (the camel became like a she-camel). As for istaḥāla, its triliteral is ḥāla, when he moves from one condition to another; and if the triliteral conveys transformation, no effect remains for the form istafʿala in it. So istaḥāla is not of the istafʿala of transformation, but of istafʿala in the sense of faʿala, which is one of its kinds, when the six-letter form adds no meaning to the triliteral.
Then we return to its interpretation and say: on it, the meaning is: they did not move from the state of arrogance, tyranny and seeking substitutes [Translator's note: so in the source, «الاعتياض»] to the state of submission and humble entreaty to Allah the Exalted. Someone might say: on the said interpretation, istakāna conveys moving from one state to another, so taking it to be a move from arrogance to submission is no more fitting [than the reverse]; and you see that this form conveys only one of the two moves; had it been derived from absolute "being", it would have been ambiguous, admitting both moves together. The answer is that its origin is indeed so, in absolute terms, but usage prevailed in employing it for the specific move, as it prevailed in others.
When Aḥmad ibn Fāris the lexicologist, the vizier, entered Baghdad in the time of the Imam al-Nāṣir, all the scholars of Baghdad were gathered for him, and a gathering for debate was held with them. The discussion was drawn to this verse, and [one of them] said: the lexical origin is that it is derived from the Arabs' saying:
kuntu laka, when I submitted [to you], which is a Hudhalī dialectal usage; and Ibn Fāris approved of this from him [Translator's note: the source does not name the speaker who gave this answer]. On this [view] it is of istafʿala in the sense of faʿala, as in their saying istaqarra, istaʿlā, and ḥāla and istaḥāla, as has preceded. It was not made of the istafʿala built for intensiveness, like istaḥsara and istaʿṣama from ḥasara and ʿaṣama, because the meaning refuses it. That is because it came in a negation, and what is intended by it is to censure these people for harshness, hardness and lack of submission despite what would necessitate the utmost humble entreaty, namely their being seized by punishment. Had it been made intensive, it would convey a reduction of the intensiveness, because negating the more intensive is less than negating the less intensive; it would be as though they were censured on that basis by negating much submission, and that they did not reach the utmost in entreaty. That is not the reality, for they were not marked by entreaty, not even for a moment of it; so how could the utmost be negated of them, which would suggest that the beginning had occurred?
The pattern istafʿala is of two kinds, transitive and intransitive. The transitive is as in their saying istaḥaqqahu and istaqbaḥahu, and the intransitive istaqdama and istaʾkhara. Its faʿala [form] may be transitive or intransitive: the transitive as in ʿalima and istaʿlama, fahima and istafhama; and the intransitive as in qabuḥa and istaqbaḥa, ḥasuna and istaḥsana. It has [several] meanings. One of them is requesting and summoning, as in your saying istaʿṭaytu, i.e. I asked for a gift, and istaʿtabtuhu, i.e. I asked him for satisfaction (al-ʿutbā); and of it are istafhamtu and istakhbartu. The second is that it be for finding [a quality in something], as in your saying istajadtuhu and istakramtuhu, i.e. I found him good and generous. It may mean moving and changing from one condition to another, as in their saying istanwaqa al-jamal when it takes on the nature of a she-camel, and istatyasat al-shāt when the ewe resembles the he-goat; and of it is istaḥjara al-ṭīn when it changes to the nature of stone in hardness. It may be in the sense of tafaʿʿala, for affecting a thing and engaging in it, as in istaʿẓama in the sense of taʿaẓẓama, and istakbara in the sense of takabbara, as in their saying tashajjaʿa and tajallada. Sometimes it alternates with faʿala: they said qarra fī al-makān and istaqarra, and ʿalā qirnahu and istaʿlāhu. Allah the Exalted said: «وإذا رأوا آية يستسخرون». What predominates in this form is requesting and finding; whatever is other than those two is learned by rote (yuḥfaẓ) and not taken as a basis for analogy.

* I'rab:
(وَلَوِ اتَّبَعَ الْحَقُّ أَهْواءَهُمْ لَفَسَدَتِ السَّماواتُ وَالْأَرْضُ وَمَنْ فِيهِنَّ) The wāw is resumptive; (لو) is conditional; (اتبع الحق) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (أهواءهم) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The lām occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (فسدت السموات والأرض) is a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (من) is conjoined to (السموات والأرض), and (فيهن) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila of (من). (بَلْ أَتَيْناهُمْ بِذِكْرِهِمْ فَهُمْ عَنْ ذِكْرِهِمْ مُعْرِضُونَ)
(بل) is a particle of transitional digression; (آتيناهم) is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; (بذكرهم) is attached to (آتيناهم). The meaning is: how can they dislike the truth, when the Qur'an has come to them to honour them and to make their name renowned? The fāʾ is a conjunction; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (عن ذكرهم) is attached to (معرضون); and (معرضون) is the khabar (predicate) of (هم).
(أَمْ تَسْأَلُهُمْ خَرْجاً فَخَراجُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الرَّازِقِينَ) A transitional conjunction to «أم به جنة» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads «أم يقولون به جنة»]. This is the fifth of the reasons for their riding the back of blind error. (تسألهم) is an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil, its implied form being "you", and a first mafʿūl bihi; (خرجا) is a second mafʿūl bihi. The fāʾ is causal, or it is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa occurring by way of giving the reason for the question understood from the disapproval. (خراج) is a mubtadaʾ, (ربك) muḍāf ilayhi, and (خير) the khabar. In (وهو) the wāw is a conjunction; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (خير الرازقين) the khabar.
(وَإِنَّكَ لَتَدْعُوهُمْ إِلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; inna and its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (تدعوهم) is an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; (إلى صراط) is attached to (تدعوهم), and (مستقيم) is an adjective. (وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ عَنِ الصِّراطِ لَناكِبُونَ)
The wāw is a conjunction; inna and its noun; the clause (لا يؤمنون) is the ṣila (relative clause); (بالآخرة) is attached to (يؤمنون); (عن الصراط) is attached to (ناكبون); the shifted lām; and (ناكبون) is the khabar of inna. (وَلَوْ رَحِمْناهُمْ وَكَشَفْنا ما بِهِمْ مِنْ ضُرٍّ لَلَجُّوا فِي طُغْيانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ) The wāw is resumptive, [the clause being] introduced to describe how they were struck by famine after the Prophet ﷺ left for Medina, so that it is related that they ate ʿilhiz, which, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, is a food they used to make from blood and camel hair in the years of famine; the details of this event will come in the Benefits section. (لو) is conditional; (رحمناهم) is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; (كشفنا) is conjoined to (رحمناهم); (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi; (بهم) is attached to an omitted ṣila of (ما); (من ضر) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). In (للجوا) the lām links the apodosis of (لو), and the clause (لجوا) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; (في طغيانهم) is attached to (يعمهون), and the clause (يعمهون) is circumstantial. (وَلَقَدْ أَخَذْناهُمْ بِالْعَذابِ فَمَا اسْتَكانُوا لِرَبِّهِمْ وَما يَتَضَرَّعُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; the lām is [in] the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of realisation; (أخذناهم) is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; (بالعذاب) is attached to (أخذناهم). (فما استكانوا) is conjoined to (أخذناهم); (ما) is negating; (استكانوا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (لربهم) is attached to (استكانوا). The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; (يتضرعون) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. The secret of conjoining the imperfect to the past will come in the Rhetoric section.

* Rhetoric:
The imperfect is conjoined to the past because the past conveys the existence and realisation of the act, and it is more fitting for [the negation of] submission (istikāna), unlike entreaty, for He informed about them by negating that in the future.

* Benefits:
His saying: «وَلَوْ رَحِمْناهُمْ», the verse, and the verse that follows it: these two verses are Medinan, for their being struck by famine came only after he ﷺ left from among them. History relates that when Thumāma ibn Uthāl al-Ḥanafī accepted Islam, went to al-Yamāma and cut off provisions from the people of Mecca, and Allah seized them with years [of drought] until they ate ʿilhiz (we have already explained it), Abū Sufyān came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said to him: I adjure you by Allah and by kinship, do you not claim that you were sent as a mercy to the worlds? He said: Yes. He said: You have killed the fathers with the sword and the sons with hunger. So the verse was revealed.

dervis-irab:77-83.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُبْلِسُونَ): in al-Miṣbāḥ: «al-balās, like salām, is sackcloth (al-misḥ); it is an Arabised Persian word, and the plural is bulus with two ḍammas, like ʿanāq and ʿunuq. Ablasa al-rajul, iblāsan: he fell silent; and ablasa: he despaired. In the Revelation: "فإذا هم مبلسون".»
(ذَرَأَكُمْ): He created you and spread you through procreation.

* I'rab:
(حَتَّى إِذا فَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ باباً ذا عَذابٍ شَدِيدٍ إِذا هُمْ فِيهِ مُبْلِسُونَ) (حتى) is a particle with which clauses begin; its like preceded recently. It was also said that it is [a particle of] limit and a preposition. (إذا) is a conditional adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) (مبلسون); the clause (فتحنا) is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; (عليهم) is attached to (فتحنا); (بابا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ذا عذاب) is an adjective of (بابا). The second (إذا) is the particle of surprise, standing in place of the fāʾ of the apodosis as a link, and the clause after it is the apodosis of the first (إذا), as though it were said: "then they are in it despairing". (هم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (فيه) is attached to (مبلسون); (مبلسون) is the khabar (predicate) of (هم). (وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَنْشَأَ لَكُمُ السَّمْعَ وَالْأَبْصارَ وَالْأَفْئِدَةَ قَلِيلًا ما تَشْكُرُونَ) The wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, introduced to reproach the unbelievers and remind the believers, so it is a general address. (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (الذي) the khabar; the clause (أنشأ) is the ṣila (relative clause); (لكم) is attached to (أنشأ); (السمع) is a mafʿūl bihi, and (الأبصار) and (الأفئدة) are conjoined to it. (قليلا) is accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), being an adjective of an omitted [noun] which is in reality the mafʿūl muṭlaq, its implied form being "a little thanks"; (ما) is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, in the sense of "truly".
