He singled out these organs only because there depend on them benefits that do not depend on others; this from one side; and from another side, whoever does not employ these organs for what they were created for is like one who lacks them. More elaboration on this matter will come in the Rhetoric section. (وَهُوَ الَّذِي ذَرَأَكُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَإِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ) Conjoined to what precedes, and its i'rab is clear. (وَهُوَ الَّذِي يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ وَلَهُ اخْتِلافُ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ أَفَلا تَعْقِلُونَ) (وهو الذي) is conjoined to what precedes; (له) is a fronted khabar and (اختلاف الليل والنهار) a postponed mubtadaʾ. The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval; the fāʾ conjoins to an omitted, implied [clause]; (لا) is negating; (تعقلون) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). (بَلْ قالُوا مِثْلَ ما قالَ الْأَوَّلُونَ) (بل) is a particle of transitional digression; (قالوا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (مثل) is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. a saying like the saying of the ancients; (ما) is maṣdariyya, forming with what follows it a maṣdar to which (مثل) is annexed; and (الأولون) is the fāʿil. (قالُوا: أَإِذا مِتْنا وَكُنَّا تُراباً وَعِظاماً أَإِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ) The clause is a badal (substitute) of the clause before it, i.e. resumptive [Translator's note: so in the source]. The hamza is for the interrogative of deeming far-fetched; (إذا) is a future adverb containing the sense of a condition; the clause (متنا) is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of (إذا) to it; (كنا) is conjoined to (متنا); kāna and its noun, (ترابا) its khabar, and (عظاما) conjoined to (ترابا). The hamza is also for the interrogative of deeming far-fetched; inna and its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and (مبعوثون) its khabar. (لَقَدْ وُعِدْنا نَحْنُ وَآباؤُنا هذا مِنْ قَبْلُ) The lām is [in] the answer to an omitted oath; (وعد) is a past verb in the passive; (نا) is a nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (نحن) is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the pronoun; (آباؤنا) is conjoined to the attached pronoun, the conjunction being made permissible by the separation with the detached pronoun. (من قبل) is attached to (وعدنا) or to an omitted adjective of His saying (آباؤنا), i.e. those who were before. On all [views] the meaning is: we and our fathers were promised the resurrection, and we did not see this promise to be true; rather we saw it as the tales of the ancients.
(إِنْ هذا إِلَّا أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ) (إن) is negating; (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (أساطير الأولين) is the khabar of (هذا).

* Rhetoric:
1- He made (السمع) singular in His saying «وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَنْشَأَ لَكُمُ السَّمْعَ وَالْأَبْصارَ وَالْأَفْئِدَةَ» because what is heard is one, unlike sights and hearts; or because it is originally a maṣdar, and maṣdars are not pluralised, so it alludes to the origin. This was pointed out earlier in [Sūrat] al-Baqara, so refresh your memory of it.
2- In His saying «بل قالوا مثل ما قال الأولون» there is faṣl (disjunction), i.e. cutting one of the two clauses off from the other because of their unity. (قالوا أئذا متنا وكنا ترابا…) has been disjoined from what precedes it with the intent of substitution (badal), because it fulfils the purpose more fully than the first, since "what the ancients said" comprises many sayings and it is not known which of those sayings is meant. It is better to say: if what is meant by His saying (مثل ما قال الأولون) is what was transmitted from them of their saying (أئذا متنا…), which is the apparent meaning, then it is a badal of the whole for the whole.

dervis-irab:84-96.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ لِمَنِ الْأَرْضُ وَمَنْ فِيها إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ) (قل) is an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; the clause is resumptive. (لمن) is a fronted khabar (predicate), (من) being interrogative; (الأرض) is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); (من) is conjoined to (الأرض), and this (من) is relative. They are referred to with (من) giving precedence to rational beings, as has been established. (فيها) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila of (من). (إن) is conditional; (كنتم تعلمون) is kāna and its noun, and the clause (تعلمون) its khabar; (كنتم) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and the apodosis is omitted, i.e. "then tell me of their Creator". In this there is a hint at their dullness.
(سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ قُلْ أَفَلا تَذَكَّرُونَ) The clause is resumptive, introduced to inform from Allah the Exalted of what their answer would be before it occurs. (لله) is attached to an omitted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "it [belongs]"; and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (قل) is an imperative verb, and what is meant by the command is rebuke and reproof. The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and rebuke; the fāʾ conjoins to an omitted [clause]; (لا) is negating; (تذكرون) is an imperfect verb with one of the two tāʾs omitted, the original being (تتذكرون). (قُلْ مَنْ رَبُّ السَّماواتِ السَّبْعِ وَرَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ) (من) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ; (رب السموات السبع) is its khabar, and (رب العرش العظيم) is conjoined to it. (سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ قُلْ أَفَلا تَتَّقُونَ) (لله) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. they cannot but say that. The lām was brought in view of the meaning of the question, for your saying "who is its lord?" and "to whom does it belong?" have one meaning, as when you say "who is the owner of this house?" and one answers "Zayd" or "[it belongs] to Zayd". (قُلْ مَنْ بِيَدِهِ مَلَكُوتُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ يُجِيرُ وَلا يُجارُ عَلَيْهِ) (من) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ; (بيده) is a fronted khabar and (ملكوت كل شيء) a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of (من). The tāʾ and the wāw in (ملكوت) are augmentative for intensiveness, as they are augmented in raḥamūt and rahabūt, from raḥma and rahba. Al-malakūt is the mighty dominion, might and authority; and the heavenly malakūt is the abode of the saints in heaven. The wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يجير) the khabar; the wāw is a conjunction and the clause (لا يجار) is conjoined to (يجير). The meaning is: He succours whom He wills and guards him, and no one is succoured against Him. It is made transitive with (على) because it contains the sense of giving victory.
(إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ) (إن) is conditional; (كنتم) is the protasis and the apodosis is omitted, as before, i.e. "then tell me". (سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ قُلْ فَأَنَّى تُسْحَرُونَ) (لله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. In it regard is paid to the meaning being "to whom belongs what was mentioned?"; the implied form in the first is "say: to whom belong the seven heavens?" and in the second "say: to whom belongs the dominion of everything?". So the genitive lām is implied in the question and appeared in the answer in view of the meaning. It has been read without it, with the Majestic Name in the nominative, as an answer according to the wording of His saying (من), because what is asked with, namely (من), is nominative in position, so its answer came in the nominative, matching it in wording. In (فأنى) the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; (أنى) is an interrogative noun meaning "how", in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); (تسحرون) is an imperfect verb in the passive and the wāw is a nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (بَلْ أَتَيْناهُمْ بِالْحَقِّ وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكاذِبُونَ)
(بل) is a particle of digression and conjunction; (أتيناهم) is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (بالحق) is a ḥāl. The wāw is circumstantial; inna and its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and (كاذبون) is the khabar of inna.
(مَا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ مِنْ وَلَدٍ وَما كانَ مَعَهُ مِنْ إِلهٍ) (ما) is negating; (اتخذ الله) is a verb and its fāʿil; (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (ولد) is genitive in form and accusative in position because it is a mafʿūl bihi. The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; (كان) is a defective past verb; (معه) is an adverb of place attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (من) is a redundant preposition; (إله) is genitive in form and nominative in position because it is the noun of kāna. (إِذاً لَذَهَبَ كُلُّ إِلهٍ بِما خَلَقَ وَلَعَلا بَعْضُهُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ) (إذن) is a particle of answer and requital, without governing effect; al-Farrāʾ held this, and the discussion of it preceded in [Sūrat] al-Isrāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī inclined to it; he said: «If you say: (إذن) only enters upon speech that is an answer and a requital, so how did His saying (إذن لذهب) occur as an answer and a requital when no condition and no questioner's question preceded? I say: the condition is omitted, its implied form being "if there were gods with Him"; it was omitted because (وما كان معه من إله) indicates it.» Others than al-Farrāʾ and al-Zamakhsharī chose that (إذن) be in the sense of the (لو) of impossibility (imtināʿ), and al-Bayḍāwī followed this; he said: «i.e. if there were gods with Him, as you say, each of them would have taken away what he created, kept it exclusively to himself, and his dominion would have been distinct from the dominion of the others, and fighting and mutual overpowering would have occurred between them, as is the state of the kings of this world; so the dominion of everything would not be in His hand alone. The consequent is false by consensus, by induction, and by the establishment of proof that all existing things rest upon one Necessary [Being].» The lām occurs in the apodosis of the condition on both views. (ذهب كل إله) is a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause has no grammatical position; (بما خلق) is attached to (ذهب), and the clause (خلق) is the ṣila (relative clause). (ولعلا بعضهم على بعض) is conjoined to what precedes. (سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ) (سبحان الله) is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun); (عما) is attached to (سبحان) and the clause (يصفون) is the ṣila; it is also permissible that (ما) be maṣdariyya, i.e. "above their describing". (عالِمِ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهادَةِ فَتَعالى عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ) (عالم الغيب) is genitive as a badal (substitute) of the Majestic Name or an adjective of it; it has been read in the nominative by cutting off (qaṭʿ), so it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. In (فتعالى) the fāʾ is a conjunction, as though He said "He knew the unseen, so He is exalted"; (عما) is attached to (تعالى) and the clause (يشركون) is the ṣila. (قُلْ رَبِّ إِمَّا تُرِيَنِّي ما يُوعَدُونَ) (رب) is the one addressed (munādā), muḍāf to the omitted yāʾ of the first person. (إما): the conditional (إن) has been assimilated into the redundant (ما). (تريني) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and it is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis; the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya), the yāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi, and (ما) is a second mafʿūl bihi. It is visual [seeing] made transitive to two objects by means of the hamza, because it is from the quadriliteral arā. The clause (يوعدون) is the ṣila of (ما) and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. the punishment they are promised. (رَبِّ فَلا تَجْعَلْنِي فِي الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ) This is the apodosis of the condition and the fāʾ is a link. The word (رب) was repeated as a munādā for emphasis in humble entreaty and imploring. (لا) is prohibitive; (تجعلني) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لا); the nūn is for protection; the yāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi; (في القوم) is the second mafʿūl bihi, and (الظالمين) an adjective.
(وَإِنَّا عَلى أَنْ نُرِيَكَ ما نَعِدُهُمْ لَقادِرُونَ) The wāw conjoins to what precedes; inna and its noun; (على أن نريك) is attached to (قادرون). (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (نرى) is an imperfect, accusative by (أن), its fāʿil latent, its implied form being "we"; the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi and (ما) the second; the discussion of visual arā has preceded. The shifted lām, which is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ) shifted to the khabar; and (قادرون) is the khabar of (إنا).
(ادْفَعْ بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ السَّيِّئَةَ نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِما يَصِفُونَ) Resumptive speech, introduced to urge the Prophet ﷺ to pardon their offence and to meet it with as much kindness as possible. (ادفع) is an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "you"; (بالتي) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ادفع); (التي) is an adjective (naʿt) of an omitted [noun], i.e. "the trait"; (هي أحسن) is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the nominal clause is the ṣila of (التي); (السيئة) is a mafʿūl bihi. The clause (نحن أعلم) is circumstantial; (نحن) is a mubtadaʾ and (أعلم) the khabar; (بما) is attached to (أعلم), and the clause (يصفون) is the ṣila. It is also permissible that (ما) be maṣdariyya, i.e. "of their describing you" and their speaking ill [of you].

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «ادْفَعْ بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ السَّيِّئَةَ» there is a departure from what the context requires for an eloquent secret. The apparent [wording] would be to say "repel the evil deed with the good deed", but He departed from what the speech requires because of the [element of] preference in it. The meaning is: repel the evil deed with as much kindness as possible, so that when pardon, kindness and the exertion of one's ability in it come together, it is a multiplied good deed in exchange for one evil deed. An objector might say: how is this comparison (mufāḍala) permissible, which is a sharing in one thing and a distinction in another, when there is no sharing at all between the good deed and the evil deed, for they are two opposed contraries? What then is the point of this comparison?
The answer: the good deed, among good deeds, exceeds the evil deed among evil deeds; so the comparison comes from something more general than this being good and that being evil. This is the case with every comparison between two contraries, as in your saying "honey is sweeter than vinegar", meaning that among sweet kinds it is more distinguished than vinegar among sour kinds, not because there is a specific sharing between them. Of this sort is what is related of Ashʿab the jester, that he said: al-Aʿmash and I grew up in the care of so-and-so; he kept rising and I kept sinking until we were level, meaning that they were level in each of them reaching the utmost: Ashʿab reached the utmost at the bottom and al-Aʿmash reached the utmost at the top.
Moreover, another aspect may be intended: that the comparison be among the good deeds with which the evil deed is repelled. For it may be repelled by pardon and overlooking, being content with that in repelling it; generosity may be added to pardon; and its utmost may be reached by exerting one's ability. These kinds of repelling are all repelling by a good deed, but the best of these good deeds in repelling is the last, because it comprises a number of good deeds. So the Prophet ﷺ was commanded [to use] the best of good deeds in repelling the evil deed, and then the comparison holds in its literal sense without reinterpretation.

dervis-irab:97-104.t:
* Vocabulary:
(هَمَزاتِ): plural of hamza, which is a prod and a push with the hand or otherwise. In al-Asās and al-Lisān: «hamaza raʾsahu: he squeezed his head; hamaza al-jawza bi-kaffihi: he cracked the walnut with his palm. Of figurative usage: hamaza al-rajula fī qafāhu: he winked at him [behind his back]; a man who is humaza and hammāz [a backbiter]; and Satan yahmizu man: he whispers insinuations into his heart. It is said: I seek refuge in Allah from his whispering, his prodding and his slander; and "أعوذ بك من همزات الشياطين".» In al-Mukhtār: «The hamazāt of Satan are his suggestions which he makes pass through a person's heart.» I say: the origin of hamz is prodding, and from it is the trainer's spur (mihmāz). Their urging people to acts of disobedience is likened to the trainer's spurring animals to move; and the plural is for the [repeated] times or for the variety of insinuations.
(بَرْزَخٌ): a barrier that prevents them from returning to this world. Al-barzakh is the barrier between two mutually exclusive things; it was also said: the screen between two things [preventing] one of them from reaching the other. Al-Rāghib said: its origin is barzah, which was Arabised; at the Resurrection it is what stands between a person and the lofty stations. And al-barzakh, it was said, is what stands between a person and the return he wishes for.
(تَلْفَحُ): lafḥ is more severe than nafḥ, because it is striking with severity, whereas nafḥ is striking in general, as in His saying: «وَلَئِنْ مَسَّتْهُمْ نَفْحَةٌ مِنْ عَذابِ رَبِّكَ». In al-Qāmūs: lafaḥa, yalfaḥu, on the pattern of fataḥa, so-and-so with the sword: he struck him with it; and the fire lafaḥat, lafḥan and lafaḥānan, or the hot wind with its heat, so-and-so: it struck his face and burned it.
(كالِحُونَ): kulūḥ is that the lips contract and draw back from the teeth, as you see in roasted heads. From Mālik ibn Dīnār: the cause of the [repentance] [Translator's note: the source has «نوبة»; probably «توبة» (repentance) is intended] of ʿUtba al-Ghulām was that he passed in the market by a head that had been taken out of the oven, and he fainted for three days and their nights. It is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: «The Fire will roast him, so that his upper lip contracts until it reaches the middle of his head and his lower lip hangs down until it reaches his navel.» In al-Mukhtār: «Kulūḥ is baring the teeth with a scowl, and its pattern is khaḍaʿa.» I say: from it is the kulūḥ of the lion, i.e. its baring its fangs; and a dahr kāliḥ and a bard kāliḥ, i.e. a severe [time] and [cold].

* I'rab:
(وَقُلْ رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ هَمَزاتِ الشَّياطِينِ) The wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive; you may conjoin it to what precedes. (رب) is the one addressed (munādā), muḍāf to the omitted yāʾ of the first person; (أعوذ) is an imperfect verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), its implied form being "I"; (بك) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أعوذ), and likewise His saying (من همزات الشياطين). (وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ رَبِّ أَنْ يَحْضُرُونِ) Conjoined to what precedes; both the governing verb and the vocative were repeated for emphasis and greater attention to this seeking of refuge. (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (يحضرون) is accusative by (أن), the sign of its accusative being the omission of the nūn; the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya); the wāw is the fāʿil; and the omitted yāʾ of the first person is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (حَتَّى إِذا جاءَ أَحَدَهُمُ الْمَوْتُ قالَ رَبِّ ارْجِعُونِ) (لَعَلِّي أَعْمَلُ صالِحاً فِيما تَرَكْتُ) It is permissible that [(حتى)] be [a particle of] limit for (يصفون), attached to it, i.e. they continue speaking ill until this time; and it is permissible that it be inceptive. (إذا) is a future adverb attached to (قال); the clause (جاء) is that to which the adverb is annexed; (أحدهم) is a fronted mafʿūl bihi and (الموت) a postponed fāʿil; the clause (قال) has no grammatical position. (رب) is the munādā, muḍāf to the omitted yāʾ of the first person; (ارجعون) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn; the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; the nūn is for protection, and the yāʾ, omitted following the orthography of the Muṣḥaf, is a mafʿūl bihi. It is plural, though the one addressed is one, namely Allah the Exalted, for magnification. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «There are three views on it. The first is that it is plural for magnification, as Allah the Exalted said: "إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر", and as in His saying:
"ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا". The second is that he meant: O angels of my Lord, send me back. The third is that by the plural form he indicated the repetition of the saying, as though he said: send me back, send me back.» What we mentioned is more fitting. Laʿalla and its noun, and the clause (أعمل) its khabar (predicate); (صالحا) is a mafʿūl bihi or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); (فيما) is an adjective of (صالحا) or attached to (أعمل); the clause (تركت) is the ṣila (relative clause), i.e. what I wasted of my life without use or benefit. (كَلَّا إِنَّها كَلِمَةٌ هُوَ قائِلُها وَمِنْ وَرائِهِمْ بَرْزَخٌ إِلى يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ) (كلا) is a particle of deterrence and rebuke; the discussion of it will come in detail; i.e. he will have no return. Inna and its noun; (كلمة) is its khabar; a useful discussion of (الكلمة) will come in the Benefits section. (هو) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (قائلها) the khabar, and the nominal clause is an adjective of (كلمة). The wāw is either a conjunction or circumstantial; (من ورائهم) is a fronted khabar and (برزخ) a mubtadaʾ; (إلى يوم) is an adjective of (برزخ), and the clause (يبعثون) is that to which the adverb is annexed. What is meant is not that they return on the Day of Resurrection; rather it is a total cutting off of hope of returning to this world. So the limit is not included in what is limited; what is meant is that He set the limit of their return at something impossible, so it resembles His saying:
«حَتَّى يَلِجَ الْجَمَلُ فِي سَمِّ الْخِياطِ».
(فَإِذا نُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ فَلا أَنْسابَ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَلا يَتَساءَلُونَ) The fāʾ is resumptive; (إذا) is a future adverb attached to the sense of negation in the apodosis, i.e. that is negated [then]; the clause (نفخ) is that to which the adverb is annexed; (في الصور) is attached to (نفخ). The fāʾ links the apodosis of (إذ) [Translator's note: so in the source; (إذا) is meant]; (لا) is the lā of generic negation; (أنساب) is its noun, indeclinable on the fatḥa; (بينهم) is an adverb attached to its omitted khabar; (يومئذ) is an adverb attached to an omitted adjective of (أنساب), or to the omitted [element] to which the khabar is attached. The tanwīn in (يومئذ) substitutes for a clause whose implied form is "the day the trumpet is blown". The meaning of negating lineages will come in the Rhetoric section. (ولا يتساءلون) is conjoined to what precedes; (يتساءلون) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, i.e. they will not ask one another about them, as will come.
(فَمَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوازِينُهُ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ) The fāʾ is for ramification (tafrīʿ) and the clause is conjoined or resumptive. (من) is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; (ثقلت) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and (موازينه) its fāʿil. In (فأولئك) the fāʾ links the apodosis because it is a nominal clause; (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ; (هم) is a second mubtadaʾ or a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); (المفلحون) is the khabar of (أولئك), or the khabar of (هم), the clause being the khabar of (أولئك). (وَمَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوازِينُهُ فَأُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ فِي جَهَنَّمَ خالِدُونَ) The clause is conjoined to the one before it and is like it. (في جهنم) is attached to (خالدون); (خالدون) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or a khabar after a khabar of (أولئك). Al-Zamakhsharī considered that it is a badal (substitute) of (خسروا أنفسهم), and neither the badal nor what it substitutes has a position, because the ṣila of the relative noun has no position. (تَلْفَحُ وُجُوهَهُمُ النَّارُ وَهُمْ فِيها كالِحُونَ) The clause is resumptive, or a second khabar, or a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وجوههم) is a fronted mafʿūl bihi and (النار) a postponed fāʿil. The wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ; (فيها) is attached to (كالحون) or to an omitted ḥāl of (هم); and (كالحون) is the khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «فَلا أَنْسابَ بَيْنَهُمْ» there is the device of tankīt (making a subtle point), which has been discussed before. By negating lineages, which exist, He intended something else, for a subtle point in it. Lineages are established and cannot validly be negated, and the Arabs used to boast of them in this world; but He inclined to negating them either because they become void in the Hereafter, since mutual severance will occur among them and they will be separated, punished or rewarded; or because by the negation He intended an omitted attribute of the lineages, i.e. [lineages] that count, since they will vanish altogether and become void through the disappearance of mutual mercy and affection, out of extreme breathlessness and exhaustion and the bewilderment that overwhelms them.

* Benefits:
The word kalima is applied in the language to [a whole piece of] speech (kalām). The scholars differed over this application. Al-Sanhūrī in his commentary on the Ājurrūmiyya and Ibn Hishām in Shudhūr al-Dhahab held that the application is literal (ḥaqīqī), existing in the original language. The author of al-Qāmūs said: «Al-kalima, its plural kalim and kalimāt: the word (lafẓa), and whatever a person utters, whether single or compound.» It was also said that the said application is by way of metaphor (istiʿāra): since the parts of speech are bound to one another, it acquires thereby a unity, so it resembles the kalima in this, and its term is applied to it. The verse is explicit in confirming this application; similar to it is his saying ﷺ: The truest kalima a poet has said is the kalima of Labīd:
ألا كل شيء ما خلا الله باطل ... وكلّ نعيم لا محالة زائل
(Indeed everything other than Allah is vain, and every bliss is inevitably passing.)
And their saying "the kalima of the testimony" (kalimat al-shahāda), by which they mean: There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.

dervis-irab:1-11.t:
* Vocabulary:
(اللَّغْوِ): al-laghw: everything that is forbidden, or disliked, or permissible but not called for by necessity or need. Al-laghw is everything, of speech or action, that does not concern you, such as play and jest, and what manly virtue requires one to drop and discard, and everything that is of no account.
(لِفُرُوجِهِمْ): al-furūj is the plural of farj, which in a human being is the private parts.

* I'rab:
(قَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ) (قد) is a particle of realisation; (أفلح) is a past verb and (المؤمنون) the fāʿil (agent). (الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي صَلاتِهِمْ خاشِعُونَ) (الذين) is a naʿt (adjective) of (المؤمنون); (هم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (في صلاتهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خاشعون); (خاشعون) is the khabar (predicate) of «هم», and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين). The preposition and its noun were placed before what they attach to in order to give it importance, and this was made fitting by the fact that what they attach to is a verse-ending (fāṣila). (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنِ اللَّغْوِ مُعْرِضُونَ) (والذين) is conjoined to (الذين); (هم) is a mubtadaʾ; (عن اللغو) is attached to (معرضون); (معرضون) is the khabar of «هم», and the clause is the ṣila of (الذين). (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِلزَّكاةِ فاعِلُونَ) (والذين) is conjoined to (الذين); (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and (فاعلون) the khabar; (للزكاة) is attached to (فاعلون), and (فاعلون) is made to contain the meaning of "payers". It has been said that the lām is redundant (zāʾida) on the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) because it precedes its governor.
(وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حافِظُونَ) (والذين) is conjoined to what preceded; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and (حافظون) the khabar; (لفروجهم) is attached to (حافظون). (إِلَّا عَلى أَزْواجِهِمْ أَوْ ما مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُهُمْ) (إلا) is a particle of exception; (على أزواجهم) is in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. except as having charge over their wives, or as maintainers of them. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «[It is] from your saying: "So-and-so was over (ʿalā) so-and-so [a woman], then he died leaving her, and so-and-so succeeded him over her"; its parallel is "Ziyād was over Basra", i.e. governor over it; and from it is their saying "so-and-so [a woman] is under so-and-so", and hence the wife is called firāsh. The meaning is that they guard their private parts in all states except in the state of their marrying or taking concubines. Or (على) is attached to something omitted indicated by «غير ملومين», as though it were said: they are blamed, except regarding their wives, i.e. they are blamed for every intimacy except what has been made free for them, for they are not blamed for that. Or you may make it a complement of (حافظين), from your saying "guard the rein of my horse for me (ʿalayya)", on the basis that it is made to contain the meaning of negation, just as their saying "I adjure you by Allah, except that you do (illā faʿalta)" contains the meaning of "I ask of you nothing but your doing".» Al-Farrāʾ held that (على) means (من), i.e. except from their wives, just as (من) came meaning (على) in His saying «ونصرناه من القوم». (أو) is a conjunction and (ما) is conjoined to (أزواجهم); the clause (ملكت أيمانهم) is the ṣila. He expressed it with (ما) rather than (من), though the context calls for the latter, because of their deficiency, since they are concubines (sarārī). Al-surriyya is the slave-woman for whom you have provided a dwelling; it is of the pattern fuʿliyya, related to al-sirr, which is intercourse, or concealment, because a man often keeps her secret and hides her from his free wife. The sīn takes ḍamma because word patterns may be altered in relative adjectives, as they said dahrī [Translator's note: so in the source; the standard form cited is duhrī] in the relative adjective from al-dahr, and suhlī from soft ground (al-arḍ al-sahla), with ḍamma on the first letter of both. The plural is sarārī. Al-Akhfash said it is derived from al-surūr (joy), because a man is gladdened by her. The wording of al-Miṣbāḥ: «Al-surriyya is of the pattern fuʿliyya; it is said to be taken from al-sirr with kasra, which is marriage, so the ḍamma is irregular, to distinguish between her and a free woman when married secretly, for she is called sirriyya with kasra, regularly; and it is said to be from al-surr with ḍamma, meaning joy, because her owner is gladdened by her, so it is regular.»
(فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ) The clause gives the reason for the exception; (إن) and its noun, and (غير ملومين) its khabar. (فَمَنِ ابْتَغى وَراءَ ذلِكَ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ العادُونَ) The fāʾ is resumptive; (من) is a conditional noun that puts the verb in the jussive, as mubtadaʾ; (ابتغى) is a past verb in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its fāʿil latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he". (وراء): the adverb is attached to an omitted naʿt, and this omitted [noun] is the object of (ابتغى), i.e. he sought something lying beyond that; you may make (وراء) mean "other than" and put it in the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi. (ذلك) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ, (هم) a second mubtadaʾ, and (العادون) the khabar of (أولئك) [Translator's note: so in the source; on this analysis (العادون) is strictly the khabar of (هم)]; or (هم) is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) and (العادون) the khabar; and the clause is the khabar of (أولئك). (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِأَماناتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ راعُونَ) (والذين) is conjoined to what preceded; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and (راعون) its khabar; (لأماناتهم) is attached to (راعون), and (عهدهم) is conjoined to (أماناتهم).
(وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلى صَلَواتِهِمْ يُحافِظُونَ) Its iʿrāb has been given, and it is conjoined to what preceded. (أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْوارِثُونَ) (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ; (هم) is a pronoun of separation and (الوارثون) the khabar. It was said before that (هم) may be parsed as a second mubtadaʾ, but it is better that it be for separation, to indicate specification. (الَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ الْفِرْدَوْسَ هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ) (الذين) is a second khabar or a naʿt of (الوارثون); the clause (يرثون) is the ṣila; (الفردوس) is the mafʿūl bihi; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ; (فيها) is attached to (خالدون), and (خالدون) is the khabar of (هم). (الفردوس) is treated as feminine with regard to the meaning, that it is Paradise (al-janna). The clause (هم فيها خالدون) is a ḥāl.

* Rhetoric:
1- Detailing (al-tafṣīl):
The sūra is distinguished by the excellence of its opening (barāʿat al-istihlāl), because it mentions the states of the believers in detail. Detailing is of two kinds: connected and separated. The connected is every speech in which (أما) or (ما) occurs, like His saying, Exalted is He: «يَوْمَ تَبْيَضُّ وُجُوهٌ وَتَسْوَدُّ وُجُوهٌ فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ اسْوَدَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ» to the end of the passage. The separated is that whose summary comes in one place and its detail in another, like His saying, Exalted is He: «قَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ» up to His saying, Exalted is He, «والذين هم لفروجهم حافظون» up to His saying, Exalted is He, «فمن ابتغى وراء ذلك فأولئك هم العادون»; for His saying (وراء ذلك) is a summary of the forbidden women, and they have already come in detail in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ in His saying, Exalted is He:
«وَلا تَنْكِحُوا ما نَكَحَ آباؤُكُمْ مِنَ النِّساءِ» up to His saying, Exalted is He, «وَأُحِلَّ لَكُمْ ما وَراءَ ذلِكُمْ»; for this verse contains fifteen forbidden categories of women: thirteen categories of blood relatives and two categories of non-relatives.
2- Antithesis (al-ṭibāq):
In His saying, Exalted is He, «الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي صَلاتِهِمْ خاشِعُونَ، وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنِ اللَّغْوِ مُعْرِضُونَ» there is affirmative antithesis (ṭibāq al-ījāb): in this description He, Glorified is He, combined for the believers doing and refraining, since He described them with humility in prayer and abandoning idle talk; all of this is affirmative antithesis in meaning. They praised humility (khushūʿ) greatly. It is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he saw a man fiddling with his beard in prayer and said: «Had his heart been humble, his limbs would have been humble.» And al-Ḥasan looked at a man fiddling with the pebbles while saying: "O Allah, marry me to the wide-eyed houris", and he said:
"What a bad suitor you are: you propose while you fiddle."

dervis-irab:12-16.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ مِنْ سُلالَةٍ مِنْ طِينٍ) The clause has no grammatical position, because it is the answer to an omitted oath. The lām is the answer to the omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of realisation; (خلقنا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (الإنسان) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من سلالة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خلقنا), and (من) is for beginning; (من طين) is a naʿt (adjective) of (سلالة), or is attached to (سلالة) because it means "drawn out" (maslūla), so (من) is explicative. Pay no attention to the statement of some parsers that the wāw is a conjunction conjoining one sentence of speech to another; the speech is resumptive, with no connection to what precedes it. (ثُمَّ جَعَلْناهُ نُطْفَةً فِي قَرارٍ مَكِينٍ)
(ثم) is a conjunction; (جعلناه) is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; (نطفة) is the second object; (في قرار) is a third object; (مكين) is a naʿt. (ثُمَّ خَلَقْنَا النُّطْفَةَ عَلَقَةً) (ثم) is a conjunction; (خلقنا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (النطفة) is the first object and (علقة) the second object, because (خلقنا) is made to contain the meaning of "We made (it) become". (فَخَلَقْنَا الْعَلَقَةَ مُضْغَةً فَخَلَقْنَا الْمُضْغَةَ عِظاماً) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (خلقنا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (العلقة) is the first object and (مضغة) the second object; (فخلقنا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (المضغة) is the first object and (عظاما) the second object. (فَكَسَوْنَا الْعِظامَ لَحْماً ثُمَّ أَنْشَأْناهُ خَلْقاً آخَرَ فَتَبارَكَ اللَّهُ أَحْسَنُ الْخالِقِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (كسونا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (العظام) is the first object and (لحما) the second object; (ثم) is a conjunction; (أنشأناه) is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; (خلقا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) and (آخر) a naʿt. (فتبارك): the fāʾ is resumptive; (تبارك) is a past verb and (الله) the fāʿil; (أحسن) is a badal (substitute) of (الله) and (الخالقين) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). It is not an adjective, because it is indefinite even though annexed, since the muḍāf ilayhi is a substitute for (من); and so it is with the whole chapter of the elative noun. The tamyīz (specification) of (أحسن) is omitted because it is known, i.e. "in creating". (ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ لَمَيِّتُونَ ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ تُبْعَثُونَ) (ثم) is a conjunction of delay; (إن) and its noun; (بعد ذلك): the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl, or to (ميتون); the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (ميتون) is the khabar (predicate) of (إن). (ثم إنكم) is conjoined to what preceded, and the clause (تبعثون) is the khabar of (إن).

* Rhetoric:
1- Variation in the conjunctions:
In the successive conjunctions in these verses there are secrets subtle in derivation and fine in meaning. The Exalted mentioned the details of the creature's state in its transitions: He began with the first creation, the creation of Adam from clay; and when He conjoined to it the second creation, the creation of the progeny, He conjoined it with (ثم) because of the delay between them [Translator's note: the text has «بيتهما», a misprint for «بينهما»]. Where He came to the determining [of stages] that follow one another without delay, He conjoined with the fāʾ. And when He reached making him male or female, which is the last of the creation, He conjoined with (ثم). We know that the time in which the drop becomes a clot is long, but the two states are connected; so sometimes the length of time is considered and the conjunction is with (ثم), and sometimes the connection of the two states, the second with the first, without anything else separating them, is considered, and the conjunction is with the fāʾ. Like this is "Muḥammad married, and (fa-) a child was born to him."
Another thing: the becoming of dust into a drop is something improbable in outward appearance, and likewise the becoming of the drop into a clot, because of their evident difference from each other; but the becoming of the clot into a lump of flesh has nothing strange in it, because of their closeness. For this reason He conjoined with (ثم) in His saying, Exalted is He: «يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ فِي رَيْبٍ مِنَ الْبَعْثِ فَإِنَّا خَلَقْناكُمْ مِنْ تُرابٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ مُضْغَةٍ»; while in the verse we are dealing with, the stages of creation and the distance of the times between every two stages were taken into account. In the gloss of al-Shihāb al-Khafājī on al-Bayḍāwī there is the following, in summary:
The variation of the conjunctions between the fāʾ and (ثم) is due to the difference of the transformations, i.e. some of them are improbable to arise from what precedes, and that is what is conjoined with (ثم); so improbability, rational or in rank, is treated as delay and physical distance, because the production of a drop from earthy particles is very strange, and likewise making the white drop into red fluid; unlike making the blood into flesh resembling it in colour and form, and likewise hardening it until it becomes bone, because that can happen through remaining [a while], as is observed; and likewise extending the flesh of the lump over it to cover it. That would require conjoining all of them with (ثم) if the end and beginning of the period were considered, and conjoining with the fāʾ if only its end were considered.
2- Likening the womb to a resting place:
In His saying, Exalted is He, «فِي قَرارٍ مَكِينٍ» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): the thing likened is omitted and the thing it is likened to is kept. The thing likened is the womb; He likened it to a qarār, i.e. a place of settling, then described it as makīn in the sense of mutamakkin (firmly established), because it is firmly established in itself so that no disorder befalls it, or because what dwells in it is firmly established, as in their saying "a travelling road", i.e. a road travelled upon. There remains the clarification of His saying, Exalted is He, «خَلْقاً آخَرَ». The statements about it are many and conflicting, and the best that is said about it is that it is general, and what is meant is its very great difference from the first creation: He made him an animate being when he had been inanimate, speaking when he had been mute, hearing when he had been deaf, seeing when he had been blind from birth; and He deposited in his inner and outer being, in every organ of his organs and every part of his parts, wonders beyond description and marvels beyond comprehension.

dervis-irab:105-110.t:
* Vocabulary:
(شِقْوَتُنا): one of the maṣdars (verbal nouns) of shaqiya. In al-Mukhtār: «al-shaqāʾ and al-shaqāwa, with fatḥa, are the opposite of happiness; Qatāda read (شقاوتنا) with kasra, and it is a dialectal form. Shaqiya, with kasra, shaqāʾan and shaqāwatan as well; and Allah ashqāhu, so he is shaqī, of evident shiqwa.» In al-Qāmūs and its commentary: «shaqiya, yashqā, on the pattern of taʿiba, shaqan, shaqāwa, shiqāwa, shiqwa and shaqwa, the opposite of saʿida; so he is shaqī, and the plural is ashqiyāʾ.»
(اخْسَؤُا): be abased in it and be driven off, as dogs are driven off when they are chased away. In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: «I chased the dog away (khasaʾtu), and it went away of itself (khasaʾa); it is transitive and intransitive.» In al-Mukhtār: «khasaʾa al-kalb: he drove the dog away, on the pattern of qaṭaʿa; and khasaʾa itself: it submitted.» Khāʾ with sīn, as first and second radicals, has one particular property: the word indicates contempt and abasement. The discussion of khasaʾa has preceded. Khasira al-tājir fī bayʿihi, khusrānan and khusran: the merchant lost in his sale; a losing merchant (khāsir); akhsara al-mīzān and khassarahu: he made the scale short, and a short scale (makhsūr); akhsara fulān and akāsada: he fell into loss and slack trade; and akhsartu al-rajul is the opposite of arbaḥtuhu (I made him profit). Salm was called al-Khāsir (the Loser) because he sold a copy of the Qur'an he had inherited and bought with its price a lute to play. Khissa is well known: it is baseness. You say: khasasta, O man, takhissu, like masasta, tamassu, khissatan and khasāsatan; a base man (khasīs), base people (akhissa); and I have not seen anyone baser than him. Lettuce (al-khass) is an antidote; and it is said: Where did the lettuce grow from the eloquence of Quss? Both are from Iyād; but where are the hollows of the foot from the necks? [Translator's note: this is a play on words in the source, contrasting Khass and Quss, both of the tribe of Iyād, as the soles of the feet differ from the necks.] Khasafa al-qamar (the moon was eclipsed); khasafat al-arḍ and inkhasafat: the earth sank with what was on it; and Allah khasafa bihim al-arḍ (caused the earth to swallow them). Of figurative usage: sāmahu khasfan, i.e. he imposed humiliation and abasement on him; he accepted khasf; he spent the night ʿalā al-khasf: hungry; they drank ʿalā al-khasf: without a heavy [meal]; a khāsifa eye: one that was gouged until its pupil disappeared in the head; khasafat ʿaynuhu and inkhasafat; khasafa badanuhu: he grew lean; so-and-so's body is khāsif and his colour kāsif. [A poet] said, describing a hunter:
أخو قترات قد تبين أنه ... إذا لم يصب لحما من الوحش خاسف
(A dweller of hunting-hides, it is clear that when he gets no meat of the game he grows lean.)
Your camels and sheep khasafat and the khasfa afflicted them, which is the drying up of the waters [Translator's note: the source has «تولية الطرق», which is unclear]; property has two khasfas: a khasfa in the heat and a khasfa in the cold. And he is makhsūl and mukhassal [i.e. rejected, despised]: khasalahu and khassalahu. [A poet] said:
ونحن الثريا وجوزاؤها ... ونحن الذراعان والمرزم
(We are the Pleiades and their Gemini; we are the two Forearms and al-Mirzam.)
وأنتم كواكب مخسولة ... ترى في السماء ولا تعلم
(And you are despised stars, seen in the sky but not known.)
And their saying akhasan am zakan, i.e. odd or even; and the boys takhāsaw: they played that game. Al-Mumazzaq said:
تخاس يداها بالحصى وترضّه ... بأسمر صرّاف إذا جمّ مطرق
(Her two forefeet toss the pebbles as if playing odd-or-even, and she crushes them with a dark, grinding [hoof] when ... [Translator's note: the end of the verse is obscure in the source].)
In this amount there is what suffices.
(سِخْرِيًّا): with kasra and ḍamma, a maṣdar of sakhira, like al-sukhr, except that the yāʾ of relation (nisba) adds to the force of the action, as has been said of khuṣūṣiyya in relation to khuṣūṣ. From al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ: the form with kasra is from mockery, and the form with ḍamma is from forced service (sukhra) and servitude; the first [making both the same] is the school of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh. Those meant by them [i.e. the ones mocked] are the Companions; and it was said: the people of the Ṣuffa in particular. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «sakhirtu minhu, sakharan, on the pattern of taʿiba: I mocked him; al-sikhrī with kasra is a dialectal form of it; al-sukhra, on the measure of ghurfa, is the servant or beast that you put to work without wage; al-sukhrī with ḍamma has its meaning; sakhkhartuhu fī al-ʿamal, with doubling: I employed him for free; and Allah sakhkhara the camels: He subdued them and made them tractable.»

* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَكُنْ آياتِي تُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ فَكُنْتُمْ بِها تُكَذِّبُونَ) The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr) and rebuke; (لم) is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and jussive; (تكن) is a defective imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لم); (آياتي) is its noun and the clause (تتلى) its khabar (predicate); (عليكم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تتلى). In (فكنتم) the fāʾ is a conjunction, and kāna and its noun; (بها) is attached to (تكذبون), and the clause (تكذبون) is the khabar of (كنتم). (قالُوا رَبَّنا غَلَبَتْ عَلَيْنا شِقْوَتُنا وَكُنَّا قَوْماً ضالِّينَ) (قالوا) is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is attached to the wāw, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (ربنا) is a muḍāf munādā (one addressed in the vocative); (غلبت) is a past verb and the tāʾ is for the feminine; (علينا) is attached to (غلبت); (شقوتنا) is the fāʿil of (غلبت). In (وكنا) the wāw is a conjunction; kāna and its noun; (قوما) is its khabar and (ضالين) an adjective. (رَبَّنا أَخْرِجْنا مِنْها فَإِنْ عُدْنا فَإِنَّا ظالِمُونَ) (ربنا) is a muḍāf munādā, repeated out of concern for it; (أخرجنا) is an imperative verb meaning supplication; (منها) is attached to (أخرج). The fāʾ is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (عدنا) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the pronoun is the fāʿil. The fāʾ links the apodosis because it is a nominal clause; inna and its noun, and (ظالمون) its khabar; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
(قالَ اخْسَؤُا فِيها وَلا تُكَلِّمُونِ) The clause (اخسئوا) is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); it is an imperative verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (فيها) is attached to (اخسئوا). In (ولا) the wāw is a conjunction and (لا) is prohibitive; (تكلمون) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لا); the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya), and the omitted yāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (إِنَّهُ كانَ فَرِيقٌ مِنْ عِبادِي يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنا آمَنَّا فَاغْفِرْ لَنا وَارْحَمْنا وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الرَّاحِمِينَ) A clause giving the reason for the rebuke before it. Inna and its noun [i.e. the pronoun of the matter], and the clause (كان) its khabar; (فريق) is the noun of kāna; (من عبادي) is an adjective of (فريق); the clause (يقولون) is the khabar of kāna; (ربنا) is a muḍāf munādā; the clause (آمنا) is the maqūl al-qawl. In (فاغفر لنا) the fāʾ is a conjunction and (اغفر) is an imperative verb meaning supplication; (ارحمنا) is conjoined to it. In (وأنت) the wāw is resumptive; (أنت) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (خير الراحمين) the khabar. (فَاتَّخَذْتُمُوهُمْ سِخْرِيًّا حَتَّى أَنْسَوْكُمْ ذِكْرِي وَكُنْتُمْ مِنْهُمْ تَضْحَكُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (اتخذتموهم) is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural and the wāw is for lengthening the ḍamma of the mīm; (سخريا) is a second mafʿūl bihi. Among these were the Emigrants Bilāl, Ṣuhayb, ʿAmmār and Khabbāb. (حتى) is a particle of limit and a preposition; (أنسوكم) is a past verb, its fāʿil and a first mafʿūl bihi; (ذكري) is a second mafʿūl bihi. (كنتم) is kāna and its noun; (معهم) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads (منهم)] is attached to (تضحكون), and the clause (تضحكون) is the khabar of (كنتم). The meaning is: you had no occupation left except mocking them and laughing at them.

dervis-irab:111-118.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْعادِّينَ): with a doubled dāl, plural of ʿādd, from ʿadda al-shayʾa, yaʿudduhu, with ḍamma on the ʿayn in the imperfect, when he counted it and reckoned it.
(عَبَثاً): al-ʿabath, with two fatḥas: play, and what has no benefit in it, and everything in which there is no sound purpose. One says ʿabitha, yaʿbathu, ʿabathan, when he mixes his work with play. Its origin is from their saying ʿabathtu al-aqiṭ, i.e. I mixed the dried curd; al-ʿabath is mixed food, and from it is al-ʿawbathānī, [a dish] of dates, sawīq and clarified butter mixed together.

* I'rab:
(إِنِّي جَزَيْتُهُمُ الْيَوْمَ بِما صَبَرُوا أَنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْفائِزُونَ) Resumptive speech, introduced to show the excellence of their state: that they benefited from [the unbelievers'] harming them. Inna and its noun, and the clause (جزيتهم) is the khabar (predicate) of inna. (جزيتهم) is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (اليوم) is an adverb of (جزيتهم); (بما) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (جزيتهم), the bāʾ being causal, i.e. because of their patience, and (ما) is maṣdariyya. (أن) and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is the second object of (جزيتهم), i.e. I have rewarded them with their triumph. (أن) and its noun; (هم) is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); and (الفائزون) is the khabar of (أن). (قالَ كَمْ لَبِثْتُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ عَدَدَ سِنِينَ) (كم) is interrogative, in the position of the accusative as an adverb of time, attached to (لبثتم); (في الأرض) is attached to (لبثتم) or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (عدد سنين) is the tamyīz (specification) of (كم), and (سنين) is muḍāf ilayhi. The meaning is: how long did you stay, in number of years? (قالُوا لَبِثْنا يَوْماً أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ فَسْئَلِ الْعادِّينَ) The clause (لبثنا) is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); (يوما) is an adverb attached to (لبثنا); (أو) is a conjunction and (بعض يوم) is conjoined to (يوما). In (فاسأل) the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; (اسأل) is an imperative verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil, its implied form being "you"; (العادين) is a mafʿūl bihi. They said this because, the punishment having overwhelmed them and its terrors having surrounded them, it was no longer in their capacity to count that or to remember; so they said: if you want to know the truth, ask those who count; as for us, we are far removed from that. (قالَ إِنْ لَبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ) (قال) is a verb whose fāʿil is latent, referring to Allah, glorified be He. (إن) is negating; (لبثتم) is a verb and its fāʿil; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (قليلا) is an adjective of an omitted adverb, i.e. a short time. (لو) is a particle of impossibility because of impossibility (imtināʿ li-imtināʿ); (أن) and its noun, and the clause (كنتم) its khabar; the clause (تعلمون) is the khabar of (كنتم), and the object of (تعلمون) is omitted, i.e. the length of your stay. It is also permissible to parse (قليلا) as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. a short staying. (أَفَحَسِبْتُمْ أَنَّما خَلَقْناكُمْ عَبَثاً وَأَنَّكُمْ إِلَيْنا لا تُرْجَعُونَ) The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and rebuke; (حسبتم) is a verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive, introduced to rebuke them for persisting in heedlessness and turning away from sound reflection. (أنما) is [a particle] restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa) [Translator's note: so in the source; on the other common view (ما) is relative or maṣdariyya]; it and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar standing in place of the two objects of (حسبتم). (خلقناكم) is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi. (عبثا) may be parsed as accusative as a maṣdar occurring in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. "playing"; it may also be parsed as accusative as a maṣdar [i.e. a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)], or as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. for the sake of play. (وأنكم) may be conjoined to (أنما خلقناكم), so that the supposition extends over it, or conjoined to (عبثا), i.e. for play. (أن) and its noun; (لا) is negating; the clause (ترجعون) is the khabar of (أن); it is an imperfect verb in the passive, and the wāw is a nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (فَتَعالَى اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ الْحَقُّ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْكَرِيمِ) The fāʾ is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, introduced to extol Allah the Exalted. (تعالى) is a past verb and (الله) its fāʿil; (الملك) and (الحق) are two adjectives of it; the clause (لا إله إلا هو) is a ḥāl, and its i'rab has preceded many times; (رب العرش) is a third adjective, and (الكريم) is an adjective (naʿt) of (العرش). (وَمَنْ يَدْعُ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلهاً آخَرَ لا بُرْهانَ لَهُ بِهِ فَإِنَّما حِسابُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ) The wāw is resumptive; (من) is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (يدع) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm) by the omission of the weak letter; (مع الله) is an adverb attached to (يدع); (إلها) is the mafʿūl bihi of (يدع) and (آخر) an adjective. (لا) is the lā of generic negation; (برهان) is its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; (له) is the khabar of lā; and the clause is a second adjective of (إلها). It is a necessary adjective (ṣifa lāzima), like His saying (يطير بجناحيه), and it was brought for emphasis. It is also permissible that it be a parenthetical clause between the protasis and its apodosis. If it is an adjective, what is intended by it is sarcasm towards whoever claims a god alongside Allah, as in His saying «بل أشركوا بالله ما لم ينزل به سلطانا», where He negated the sending down of authority for it, even though in reality there is no authority, neither sent down nor not sent down. Of the same kind as a clause coming after an indefinite noun and being diverted from being its adjective is what preceded at His saying «فاجعل بيننا وبينك موعدا لا نخلفه نحن ولا أنت»; refer back to it if you wish.
In (فإنما) the fāʾ links the apodosis of the condition because the clause is nominal; (إنما) is [a particle] restraining and restrained; (حسابه) is a mubtadaʾ; (عند ربه): the adverb is attached to an omitted khabar of (حسابه); and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). The protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of (من).
(إِنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ الْكافِرُونَ) The clause is causal, with no grammatical position. Inna and its noun; the clause (لا يفلح) is the khabar of (إنه), and (الكافرون) is the fāʿil. (وَقُلْ رَبِّ اغْفِرْ وَارْحَمْ وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الرَّاحِمِينَ) The wāw is resumptive; (رب) is the one addressed (munādā), muḍāf to the omitted yāʾ of the first person; (اغفر) is an imperative verb, what is intended by it being supplication; (ارحم) is conjoined to it. In (وأنت) the wāw is resumptive; (أنت) is a mubtadaʾ and (خير الراحمين) the khabar.

* Rhetoric:
At the close of Sūrat «al-Muʾminūn» is His saying: «إنه لا يفلح الكافرون», and at its opening «قد أفلح المؤمنون»; how great is the difference between the opening and the close!

dervis-irab:17-21.t:
* Vocabulary:
(طَرائِقَ): the plural of ṭarīqa, which is conduct, state, way, and a line in a thing. In al-Asās and al-Lisān: «He placed the things ṭarqa upon ṭarqa and ṭarīqa upon ṭarīqa: one above another; they are ṭuruq and ṭarāʾiq. And ṭarraqa a road: he made it easy, so that people trod (ṭaraqa) it with their travelling.» The heavens were called ṭuruq because they are layered (ṭūriqa) one above another, like the layering of a sandal's soles; and everything above which is its like is a ṭarīqa.
(طُورِ سَيْناءَ): and Ṭūr Sīnīn. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «It must be either that al-ṭūr is annexed in it to a tract of land whose name is Sīnāʾ and Sīnūn, or that it is a name of the mountain compounded of a muḍāf and muḍāf ilayhi, like Imruʾ al-Qays and like Baʿlabakk for those who treat it as annexation. Whoever reads Sīnāʾ with kasra on the sīn has made it a diptote because of definiteness and foreignness, or femininity because it is a tract of land, since in the pattern fiʿlāʾ the alif is not one of femininity, as in ʿilbāʾ and ḥirbāʾ; and whoever reads it with fatḥa has not inflected it as a triptote because the alif is of femininity, as in ṣaḥrāʾ.» Sinai is a peninsula bounded by the Mediterranean Sea to the north, the Suez Canal and the Gulf of Suez to the west, and Palestine and the Gulf of Aqaba to the east; it ends in the south at Rās Muḥammad on the Red Sea. Sinai is [also] a mountain situated in the south of the Sinai Peninsula. What is meant by the tree is the olive tree; it is singled out with Mount Sinai although it grows elsewhere because its origin is from there, and it was then transferred elsewhere.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعَ طَرائِقَ وَما كُنَّا عَنِ الْخَلْقِ غافِلِينَ) A resumptive clause brought to mention the creation of the heavens that are above man, after mentioning his creation. The lām is the answer to the omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of realisation; (خلقنا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (فوقكم) is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خلقنا); (سبع طرائق) is the object of (خلقنا), and (طرائق) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) to (سبع). (وما): the wāw is circumstantial and (ما) is negative; (كان) and its noun; (عن الخلق) is attached to (غافلين), and (غافلين) is the khabar (predicate) of (كنا). (وَأَنْزَلْنا مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً بِقَدَرٍ فَأَسْكَنَّاهُ فِي الْأَرْضِ)
(وأنزلنا) is conjoined to (خلقنا); (من السماء) is attached to (أنزلنا); (ماء) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (بقدر) is a naʿt (adjective) of (ماء), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun, i.e. with a measure with which they are safe from harm and attain benefit. (فأسكناه) is conjoined to (أنزلنا); it is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; (في الأرض) is attached to (أسكناه). (وَإِنَّا عَلى ذَهابٍ بِهِ لَقادِرُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (إن) and its noun; (على ذهاب) is attached to (قادرون) and (به) is attached to (ذهاب); (قادرون) is the khabar of (إنا), and the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). (فَأَنْشَأْنا لَكُمْ بِهِ جَنَّاتٍ مِنْ نَخِيلٍ وَأَعْنابٍ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (أنشأنا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (لكم) is attached to (أنشأنا); (به) is also attached to (أنشأنا), or to an omitted ḥāl, in which case the bāʾ is for accompaniment (mulābasa); (جنات) is the mafʿūl bihi; (من نخيل) is a naʿt of (جنات) and (أعناب) is conjoined to (نخيل). (لَكُمْ فِيها فَواكِهُ كَثِيرَةٌ وَمِنْها تَأْكُلُونَ) (لكم) is a fronted khabar; (فيها) is a ḥāl; (فواكه) is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject) and (كثيرة) a naʿt; (منها) is attached to (تأكلون), and (تأكلون) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. The clause (لكم فيها …), the verse, is a ḥāl of (جنات) or a naʿt, as is the rule. (وَشَجَرَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ طُورِ سَيْناءَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (شجرة) is conjoined to (جنات); the clause (تخرج) is a naʿt of (شجرة); (من طور سيناء) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تخرج). (تَنْبُتُ بِالدُّهْنِ وَصِبْغٍ لِلْآكِلِينَ) The clause is a second naʿt of (شجرة); (بالدهن) is in the place of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. bound up with oil and accompanied by it; al-duhn is the pressed juice of every fatty thing. (صبغ) is conjoined to (الدهن), following its iʿrāb, as a conjoining of one of a thing's two descriptions to the other, i.e. it grows with the thing that combines being an oil with which one anoints and from which lamps are lit, and being a condiment with which bread is "dyed", i.e. dipped in it to eat it as a relish. (للآكلين) is a naʿt of (صبغ).
(وَإِنَّ لَكُمْ فِي الْأَنْعامِ لَعِبْرَةً نُسْقِيكُمْ مِمَّا فِي بُطُونِها) The wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is a particle resembling the verb, and (لكم) is its fronted khabar; (في الأنعام) is a ḥāl; the shifted lām; (عبرة) is the noun of (إن). The clause (نسقيكم) explains (عبرة), or is resumptive; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi; (مما) is attached to (نسقيكم), and (في بطونها) is attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of (ما). (وَلَكُمْ فِيها مَنافِعُ كَثِيرَةٌ وَمِنْها تَأْكُلُونَ) Its iʿrāb was given just above, so refresh your memory of it.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying, Exalted is He, «وَصِبْغٍ لِلْآكِلِينَ» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): He likened liquid condiment to dye (ṣibgh), then omitted the thing likened and kept the thing it is likened to, the common factor being the taking on of its colour when [bread] is dipped in it.

dervis-irab:22-28.t:
* I'rab:
َ عَلَيْها وَعَلَى الْفُلْكِ تُحْمَلُونَ) [Translator's note: the verse heading is truncated at its beginning in the source; the verse is (وَعَلَيْها وَعَلَى الْفُلْكِ تُحْمَلُونَ).]
The wāw is a conjunction; (عليها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تحملون). The pronoun refers to the camels, which are among the livestock (anʿām), and because they are what is ridden upon customarily; and He paired them with the fulk, which are ships, because they are the ships of the land.
(وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا نُوحاً إِلى قَوْمِهِ) The wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, brought to relate five stories, the first of which is the story of Noah. The lām is the answer to the omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of realisation; (أرسلنا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (نوحا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إلى قومه) is attached to (أرسلنا). (فَقالَ يا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ ما لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلهٍ غَيْرُهُ أَفَلا تَتَّقُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (قال) is a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he"; (يا) is a vocative particle and (قوم) is the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the first person; (اعبدوا الله) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi. (ما) is negative; (لكم) is a fronted khabar (predicate); (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (إله) is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject) in position, genitive by (من) in form; (غيره) is a naʿt (adjective) of (إله) according to its position, and it has been read in the genitive according to the form, which is permissible. The clause (ما لكم من إله غيره) is resumptive, functioning as the reason for the command to worship. The hamza is interrogative and the fāʾ conjoins to something implied, i.e. do you not fear to reject the worship of Allah, who is your Lord, your Creator and your Provider? (فَقالَ الْمَلَأُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ: ما هذا إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (قال الملأ) is a verb and its fāʿil; (الذين) is a naʿt of (الملأ); the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause); (من قومه) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause (ما هذا …) is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); (ما) is negative; (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (بشر) is the khabar and (مثلكم) a naʿt. This is the first of the five specious arguments they put forward. (يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَتَفَضَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ لَأَنْزَلَ مَلائِكَةً) The clause (يريد) is a naʿt; (أن) and what falls in its domain is the object of (يريد); (عليكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يتفضل). The wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; (شاء الله) is a verb and its fāʿil, and the object of the willing is omitted, understood from the content of the answer of (لو), i.e. had He willed to send down a messenger. The lām occurs in the answer of (لو), and the clause (أنزل ملائكة) has no grammatical position because it is the answer of a condition that puts the verb in the jussive [Translator's note: so in the source; (لو) is normally described as a condition that does not govern the jussive]. This is the second specious argument.
(ما سَمِعْنا بِهذا فِي آبائِنَا الْأَوَّلِينَ) The clause is resumptive, brought to relate their third specious argument. (ما) is negative; (سمعنا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (بهذا) is attached to (سمعنا); (في آبائنا) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. in the stories of our fathers; (الأولين) is a naʿt of (آبائنا).
(إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا رَجُلٌ بِهِ جِنَّةٌ فَتَرَبَّصُوا بِهِ حَتَّى حِينٍ) A resumptive clause brought to relate their fourth specious argument. (إن) is negative; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (رجل) is the khabar of (هو); (به) is a fronted khabar and (جنة), i.e. madness, a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is a naʿt of (رجل). (فتربصوا): the fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquence (al-faṣīḥa), i.e. if you want to ascertain his reality, then wait; it may also be resumptive. This is their fifth specious argument. (تربصوا) is an imperative verb, i.e. wait, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (به) is attached to (تربصوا); (حتى) is a particle of limit and of the genitive, and (حين) is genitive by (حتى), and the preposition and its noun are also attached to (تربصوا), i.e. bear with him and put up with him for a time, until his affair becomes clear to you as to its outcome; then if he recovers from his madness [well and good], and if not, you kill him. (قالَ رَبِّ انْصُرْنِي بِما كَذَّبُونِ) Resumptive speech brought to request justice against them and victory over them from his Lord, after he had despaired of their believing. (رب) is the one addressed, annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the first person; (انصرني) is an imperative verb, the fāʿil latent, the nūn for protection (wiqāya) and the yāʾ the mafʿūl bihi. The bāʾ is a preposition, and (ما) is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with the verb after it as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the genitive by the bāʾ, i.e. because of their denying me; so the bāʾ is causal. It may be for substitution, i.e. help me in exchange for their denying me, as you say "this for that", i.e. in exchange for that and in its place. The preposition and its noun are attached to (انصرني). (فَأَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْهِ أَنِ اصْنَعِ الْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنا وَوَحْيِنا) The fāʾ is resumptive; (أوحينا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (إليه) is attached to (أوحينا); (أن) is explicative because it occurs after (أوحينا), which is a verb containing the meaning of saying without its letters; (اصنع) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being "you"; (الفلك) is the mafʿūl bihi; (بأعيننا) is a ḥāl of the pronoun latent in (اصنع), i.e. under Our protection and Our guarding; (ووحينا) is conjoined to (أعيننا), i.e. and Our command. (فَإِذا جاءَ أَمْرُنا وَفارَ التَّنُّورُ فَاسْلُكْ فِيها مِنْ كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ) The fāʾ is a conjunction, to make the content of what follows it consequent upon the completion of building the ship; what is meant by the command is the punishment. The clause (جاء) is that to which the adverb is annexed; (أمرنا) is the fāʿil; (وفار التنور) is conjoined to (جاء أمرنا); the discussion of this has been given in Sūrat Hūd. (فاسلك): the fāʾ links the answer of (إذا); (اسلك) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being "you"; (فيها) is attached to (اسلك); (من كل) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was a naʿt of (اثنين); (اثنين) is the object of (اسلك). The iʿrāb of this was also given in Hūd. (وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَنْ سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ الْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ) (وأهلك) is conjoined to (اثنين); (إلا) is a particle of exception; (من) is the excepted, connected (muttaṣil), from an affirmative statement, so it must be in the accusative; the clause (سبق) is the ṣila; (عليه) is attached to (سبق); (القول) is the fāʿil and (منهم) is a ḥāl, i.e. [the word] of destruction. (وَلا تُخاطِبْنِي فِي الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا إِنَّهُمْ مُغْرَقُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (تخاطبني) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا), the fāʿil latent, its implied form being "you", the nūn for protection and the yāʾ the mafʿūl bihi; (في الذين) is attached to (تخاطبني), i.e. about leaving them undestroyed — that being after the conclusive proof had become binding on them and after time had long been extended to them, nothing remained but that they be made a lesson for those who take heed. The clause (ظلموا) is the ṣila; the clause (إنهم مغرقون) gives the reason for the prohibition of addressing [Him] on their behalf; (إن), its noun and its khabar. (فَإِذَا اسْتَوَيْتَ أَنْتَ وَمَنْ مَعَكَ عَلَى الْفُلْكِ) The fāʾ is resumptive; (إذا) is an adverb of future time; the clause (استويت) is in the position of the genitive by annexation to it; (أنت) is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the tāʾ; (من) is conjoined to the tāʾ; (معك) is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila of (من); (على الفلك) is attached to (استويت), i.e. you are settled upon it.
(فَقُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي نَجَّانا مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ) The fāʾ links the answer of (إذا); (قل) is an imperative verb. He singled him out with the command to show his merit and to indicate that in his supplication there is sufficiency in place of theirs. (الحمد) is a mubtadaʾ and (لله) its khabar, and the clause is the object of the saying; the clause of saying has no grammatical position because it is the answer of a condition that does not put the verb in the jussive. (الذي) is a naʿt of (الله); the clause (نجانا) is the ṣila; (من القوم) is attached to (نجانا), and (الظالمين) is a naʿt of (القوم).

farraa:5-6.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حَافِظُونَ﴾ ﴿لاَّ عَلَىٰ أَزْوَاجِهِمْ﴾ «[Translator's note: the quotation appears thus in the source; the Qurʾānic text is إِلَّا عَلَىٰ أَزْوَاجِهِمْ.]» — the meaning is: except from their wives whom Allah has made lawful, out of the four, not to be exceeded.
His saying: ﴿أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُمْ﴾ — (ما) is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ). He is saying: there is no set limit on them regarding slave-women; they may take as many as they wish. That is His saying: they guarded their private parts except from these two [kinds], ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ﴾ in it — He is saying: not sinning.

farraa:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿ٱلْفِرْدَوْسَ﴾ — al-Kalbī said: it is "the garden" in the language of the Romans (al-Rūm). Al-Farrāʾ said: it is Arabic too; the Arabs call a garden al-firdaws.

farraa:12-12.t: His saying: ﴿مِن سُلاَلَةٍ﴾ — al-sulāla is that which is drawn out of every soil.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿فَكَسَوْنَا ٱلْعِظَامَ لَحْماً﴾ — also (العَظْمَ). In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is ﴿ثم جَعَلنا النطفة عظماً وعَصَباً فكسوناه لحماً﴾, and this is evidence for whoever says ʿaẓman [in the singular]; some have indeed read it (عظما).
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ أَنشَأْنَاهُ خَلْقاً آخَرَ﴾ — it [the pronoun] refers to the human being; or, if you wish, to the bone, the sperm-drop and the sinew, treating them as a single thing.

farraa:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ لَمَيِّتُونَ﴾ — it is read (لَميْتون) and (لمائتونَ), and mayyitūn is more common. The Arabs say to someone who has not died: "You are mayyit (going to die) shortly", and also māʾit. But they do not say of a dead man who has already died: "This is māʾit"; it is said only of the future and is not extended beyond the future. Likewise it is said: "This is the sayyid (lord) of his people today", and when you report that he will become their lord shortly, you say: "This one is sāʾid of his people shortly", and also sayyid. Likewise with greed: you say "He is ṭāmiʿ (hoping) for what you have, tomorrow"; but when «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 123b]» you describe him as [habitually] greedy you say: "He is ṭamiʿ". Likewise sharīf (noble): you say "He is the sharīf of his people", and "He is shārif shortly". This whole category in Arabic is as I have described to you.

farraa:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعَ طَرَآئِقَ﴾ — He means the heavens; each heaven is a ṭarīqa (layer). ﴿وَمَا كُنَّا عَنِ ٱلْخَلْقِ غَافِلِينَ﴾ — [i.e.] of what We created (عافِلينَ) «[Translator's note: so in the source, apparently for غافلين.]» — He is saying: We were guarding it.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿وَشَجَرَةً تَخْرُجُ مِن طُورِ سَيْنَآءَ﴾ — it is the olive tree. ﴿تَنبُتُ بِٱلدُّهْنِ﴾ — al-Ḥasan read (تُنْبِتُ بالدهنِ). They are two dialectal usages; one says nabatat and anbatat, as in the saying of Zuhayr:
رأيت ذوى الحاجات حول بيوتهم * قَطِيناً لهم حَتَّي إِذا أنبت البقلُ
(I saw those in need settled around their houses, until the herbs sprouted.)
(and nabata); it is like your saying: maṭarat al-samāʾ and amṭarat. The people of the Ḥijāz read (فَاسْرِ بأهْلِكَ) with a connecting [hamza], from saraytu; our reading is ﴿فأَسْرِ بأَهْلِك﴾ (from asraytu), and Allah said: ﴿سُبّحَانَ الذِى أَسْرَى بعَبْدِهِ لَيْلاً﴾ (and that is better). In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (تُخْرجُ الدهْنَ).
His saying: ﴿وَصِبْغٍ لِّلآكِلِيِنَ﴾ — He is saying: (those who eat dip [their bread] in the oil. Had it been (وصِبْغا), on the sense of (and a dip We caused to grow), it would be) like His saying: ﴿إنَّا زَيَّنَّا السَمَاء الدنْيَا بِزِينَةٍ الكَواكبِ وَحِفْظاً﴾. That is because the dip (ṣibgh) is the oil itself. Had it been something other than it, it would be genitive, and nothing else would be permissible. An example of that is your saying: "I passed by ʿAbd Allāh, and a man — what a man!": if you make "the man" a description of ʿAbd Allāh, you put it in the accusative; if he is someone else, you put it in the genitive, because you mean: I passed by ʿAbd Allāh and another.
The people of the Ḥijāz read (سِينَاء) with kasra on the sīn and with the long vowel, and ʿĀṣim and others read (سَيْنَاء) with the long vowel and fatḥa on the sīn. The tree is accusative by being referred back to the gardens (al-jannāt); had it been nominative, since no verb accompanies it, it would be correct, like whoever read ﴿وَحُورٌ عِينٌ﴾. Someone recited to me:
ومن يأت مَمْشَانا يصادِف غنيمة * سِواراً وخَلخالاً وبُرْدٌ مُفَوَّف
(Whoever comes to where we walk will find booty: a bracelet, an anklet, and a striped cloak.)
as though he said: and along with that, a striped cloak. Another recited to me:
هزِئت حُمَيدة أن رأت بى رُتّة * وفماً به قَصَم وجلدٌ أسودُ
(Ḥumayda mocked me when she saw in me a stammer, a mouth with broken teeth, and black skin.)
as though he said: and along with that, black skin.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿جِنَّةٌ﴾ — it is madness. The jinn are also sometimes called al-jinna, so the noun and the maṣdar (verbal noun) coincide.
His saying: ﴿فَتَرَبَّصُواْ بِهِ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ﴾ — by al-ḥīn no fixed time is intended. In meaning it is like your saying: "Leave him until a day", without meaning a single known day ahead, nor the length of a known day; it is only like your saying: until some day or other.

farraa:33-33.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَشْرَبُ مِمَّا تَشْرَبُونَ﴾ — the meaning is: of what you drink of [minhu]. Omitting (منه) is permissible because you say: "I drank of your water", so (ما تشربونَ) became equivalent to "your drink". And had you omitted (من) [i.e. "of it"] from (تأكلونَ) "منه", it would be correct.

farraa:35-35.t: His saying: ﴿أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتٌّمْ وَكُنتُمْ تُرَاباً وَعِظاماً أَنَّكُمْ مُّخْرَجُونَ﴾ — (أنكم) is repeated twice while their meaning is one; but that became good because you separated (أنكم) from its khabar (predicate) with إذا. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (أيعدكم إذا متم وكنتم تراباً وعظاماً أنكم مخرجُون). You do the same with every noun on which you bring (أن) to bear with ẓanna (to think) and the sisters of ẓanna, and then a conditional (jazāʾ) intervenes before its predicate: if you wish you repeat its noun, and if you wish you omit it «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 124a]» first or last. So you say: "I think that you, if you go out, that you will regret". If you omit the first or the second (أنك), it is sound; if both remain, it is sound. But if you do not interpose anything between them, it is not permissible: it is an error to say "I think that you that you will regret", unless you repeat it as a kind of tawkīd (emphasis).

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿هَيْهَاتَ هَيْهَاتَ لِمَا تُوعَدُونَ﴾ — had there been no lām on (ما), it would be correct; the entry of the lām is good Arabic. Similar in speech is: "hayhāt for you", "hayhāt are you from us", and "hayhāt for your land". The poet said:
فأيْهات أيهات العقِيقُ ومَن به * وأيهات وصل بالعقيق نُواصله
(Far, far is al-ʿAqīq and whoever is in it, and far is a union at al-ʿAqīq that we might keep up.)
Whoever brings in the lām «[Translator's note: so in the source («فمن يدخل اللام»); the context and the verse cited suggest «فمن لم يدخل اللام», whoever does not bring in the lām.]» puts the noun in the nominative. The meaning of hayhāt is "far", as though He said: far is (what you are promised), and far is al-ʿAqīq and its people. Whoever brings in the lām says hayhāt is a particle not derived from a verb, equivalent to "far" and "near", so the lām was brought in with it, as one says halumma laka, since it is not derived from a verb. But when they say aqbil (come forward), they do not say aqbil laka, because it [the verb] bears the pronoun of the noun.
When you pause on hayhāt, you pause with the tāʾ in both of them, because some Arabs put the tāʾ in the genitive [i.e. with kasra], which shows that it is not the feminine hāʾ; so it became like darāki and naẓāri. Others among them pause on the hāʾ, because its usual vowel is the fatḥa (naṣb), so they treat it like the hāʾ. The fatḥa (naṣb) in both is because they are two particles joined together, so they became like khamsata ʿashara (fifteen). And if you say that each one of them is self-sufficient and it is permissible to pause on it, then its fatḥa is like the fatḥa in the saying ﴿قُمت ثُمَّتَ جلست﴾ «[Translator's note: this is ordinary speech, "I stood, then sat", not a Qurʾānic verse, though the source places it in ornate brackets.]», and like the poet's saying:
ما وِيّ بل رُبَّتما غارةٍ * شَعْوَاءَ كالَلذْعة بالمِيسَم
(O Māwiyya, nay, many a widespread raid, like the burn of a branding iron!)
So the fatḥa of hayhāt is equivalent to this hāʾ which is in rubbat, because it entered upon rubba and upon thumma; these were two particles, and it did not change them from being particles, so they took fatḥa. Al-Farrāʾ said: al-Kisāʾī preferred the hāʾ, and I pause on the tāʾ.

farraa:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿فَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ غُثَآءً﴾ — like the scum (ghuthāʾ) of the valley, dried up by the punishment.

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ أَرْسَلْنَا رُسُلَنَا تَتْرَى﴾ — most Arabs do not give it tanwīn, treating it like taqwā. Some of them give it tanwīn and make its alif like the alif of iʿrāb [i.e. the accusative ending], so in the change of its wāw [into a tāʾ] it became like al-turāth
and al-tujāh. And if you wish, you may treat its yāʾ [i.e. the final alif maqṣūra] as though it were radical, so that it would be like al-miʿzā, which takes tanwīn and also does not; the pause on it would then be with the yāʾ and with a hint of kasra. But if you make it the alif of iʿrāb, you do not hint [at kasra], because you do not hint at the alifs of iʿrāb with kasra; you do not say "raʾaytu Zaydī" nor "ʿAmrī".

farraa:50-50.t:
His saying: ﴿وَآوَيْنَاهُمَآ إِلَىٰ رَبْوَةٍ﴾ — al-rabwa is raised ground. His saying: ﴿ذَاتِ قَرَارٍ﴾ — level. His saying ﴿وَمَعِينٍ﴾ — visible, flowing water. You may make al-maʿīn a mafʿūl form (passive participle pattern) from al-ʿuyūn (springs), or make it faʿīl from al-māʿūn, its root then being al-maʿn. Al-Farrāʾ said: (al-maʿn is straightness/steadiness); and ʿAbīd ibn al-Abraṣ said:
واهية أو معين مَعْنٍ * أو هَضْبة دونَها لَهُوب
(A leaking [skin], or a flowing spring, or a hill with a cleft below it.)

farraa:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلرُّسُلُ كُلُواْ مِنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَاتِ﴾ — He meant the Prophet, and used the plural, as one says in speech to a single man: "O «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 124b]» people, keep your harm away from us".
