Similar to it is ﴿الذِينَ قَالَ لَهُمُ الناسُ إنَّ الناسَ قَدْ جَمَعْوا لَكُمْ فاخْشَوْهُمْ﴾: "the people" was one person (known: he was a man of Ashjaʿ called Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd).

farraa:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّ هَـٰذِهِ أُمَّتُكُمْ﴾ — ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it with kasra, as a fresh start (iʾtināf); the people of the Ḥijāz and al-Ḥasan read it (وأَنَّ هذه أُمَّتكم). The fatḥa is on [the basis of] His saying ﴿إنى بما تعملُون عليم﴾: and [I am] knowing that this is your community. So its position is genitive, because it is referred back to (مَا). Or, if you wish, it may be accusative by an implied (muḍmar) verb, as though you said: and know this.

farraa:53-53.t: His saying: ﴿فَتَقَطَّعُوۤاْ أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ — they split it up; they divided into Jews and Christians. Whoever says ﴿زُبَراً﴾ means: pieces, like His saying ﴿آتُونِى زُبُرَ الحَدِيدِ﴾; and the meaning of zubur and zubar is one — and Allah knows best. His saying ﴿كُلُّ حِزْبٍ بِمَا لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ﴾ — He is saying: pleased with their religion, thinking that they are upon the truth.

farraa:54-54.t: His saying: ﴿فَذَرْهُمْ فِي غَمْرَتِهِمْ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ﴾ — [i.e.] in their ignorance.

farraa:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿أَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّمَا نُمِدُّهُمْ بِهِ مِن مَّالٍ وَبَنِينَ﴾ — (ما) is in the position of الذي (that which), and it is not a single particle [with أنّ].

farraa:56-56.t: His saying: ﴿نُسَارِعُ لَهُمْ﴾ — He is saying: do they think that what We give them in this world of wealth and sons, that We have made it a reward for them? Then He said: ﴿بَل لاَّ يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ that it is only a gradual leading-on [to ruin] (istidrāj) from Us for them.

farraa:60-60.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْتُونَ مَآ آتَواْ﴾ — al-Farrāʾ «[Translator's note: so in the source («الفرّاء»); probably an error for «القرّاء», the Readers.]» are upon the ḍamma of the yāʾ and the long alif in (آتَوْا). Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Mindal narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to me, from ʿAṭāʾ, from ʿĀʾisha, that she read — or said: "We used to read only" — ﴿يَأتون ما أَتَوْا﴾; and they knew Allah too well for their hearts to be afraid. Al-Farrāʾ said: by it [the other reading] is meant the zakāt. She is saying: they were too God-fearing to give their zakāt while their hearts were afraid.
His saying: ﴿وَّقُلُوبُهُمْ وَجِلَةٌ أَنَّهُمْ﴾ — [i.e.] afraid of the fact that they. When you drop (مِن), you put it in the accusative. For everything in the Qurʾān from which a genitive-governing particle has been omitted, al-Kisāʾī used to say: it is genitive as it was. And we have explained that it is accusative when the genitive-governing particle is missing (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ, accusative by removal of the preposition).

farraa:61-61.t: His saying: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ يُسَارِعُونَ فِي ٱلْخَيْرَاتِ﴾ — they hasten to [good] deeds. ﴿وَهُمْ لَهَا سَابِقُونَ﴾ — He is saying: they are foremost towards them. It is also said: ﴿وهم لها سَابقونَ﴾, that is, felicity has already been decreed for them.

farraa:63-63.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَهُمْ أَعْمَالٌ مِّن دُونِ ذٰلِكَ هُمْ لَهَا عَامِلُونَ﴾ — He is saying: deeds yet awaited, of those they will do; so He said ﴿مِّن دُونِ ذٰلِكَ﴾.

farraa:64-64.t: His saying: ﴿يَجْأَرُونَ﴾ — they cry out loudly; it is al-juʾār.

farraa:66-66.t: His saying: ﴿عَلَىٰ أَعْقَابِكُمْ تَنكِصُونَ﴾ — in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (عَلَى أدباركم تنكُصونَ). He is saying: you turn back; that is al-nukūṣ.

farraa:67-67.t: His saying: ﴿مُسْتَكْبِرِينَ بِهِ﴾ — (the hāʾ refers to the Ancient House [the Kaʿba]): you say "We are its people", and when night comes and you hold your night-talk (samar), you abandon (hajartum) the Qurʾān and the Prophet. This is from al-hijrān, that is, you leave it and reject it. Ibn ʿAbbās read (تُهْجِرونَ), from ahjartu; al-hujr is that they used to revile the Prophet ﷺ when they were alone around the House at night. And if a reader reads (تَهْجُرونَ), he makes it like raving; it is said: "the man hajara in his sleep" when he raved. That is: you say about him what is not in him and does not harm him, so it is like raving.

farraa:69-69.t: His saying: ﴿أَمْ لَمْ يَعْرِفُواْ رَسُولَهُمْ﴾ — that is, the lineage of their messenger.

farraa:71-71.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَوِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلْحَقُّ أَهْوَآءَهُمْ﴾ — it is said that al-ḥaqq (the Truth) is Allah; and it is said that it is the Revelation: had it come down with what they wish, ﴿لَفَسَدَتِ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتُ وَٱلأَرْضُ وَمَن فِيهِنَّ﴾. Al-Kalbī said: (ومَنْ فِيهِنَّ) of creatures. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (لفسدت السّموات والأرض وما بينهما). It is possible in Arabic that what is in them is what is between them, «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 125a]» because the sky is like a roof over the earth; you say "In the house there is such-and-such" and "Between its floor and its ceiling there is such-and-such"; therefore it is permissible to treat the earth and the sky like a house.
His saying: ﴿بَلْ أَتَيْنَاهُمْ بِذِكْرِهِمْ﴾ — [i.e.] with their honour.

farraa:72-72.t: His saying: ﴿أَمْ تَسْأَلُهُمْ خَرْجاً﴾ — He is saying: for what you have brought; He means a wage — for the wage of your Lord is better.

farraa:74-74.t: His saying: ﴿لَنَاكِبُونَ﴾ — He is saying: turning away from the religion. The path (al-ṣirāṭ) here is the religion.

farraa:80-80.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَهُ ٱخْتِلاَفُ ٱللَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ﴾ — He is saying: He is the one who made them alternate, as you say in speech: "Yours is the reward and the kindness", that is, you are rewarded and you show kindness.

farraa:84-85.t:
His saying: ﴿قُل لِّمَنِ ٱلأَرْضُ وَمَن فِيهَآ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ ﴿سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ﴾ — there is no question about this one, because the question was asked with a lām, so [the lām] returned in the answer to the questioner. As for the other two, the people of Medina and most of the people of Kufa read them (للهِ), (لله), and they are likewise in the reading of Ubayy: (لِله) (لِلهِ) (لله), all three of them. The people of Basra read the other two (اللهُ), (اللهُ), and that is clearer in Arabic, because it is given back in the nominative; do you not see [that] His saying ﴿قُلْ مَنْ رَبُّ السَّموات﴾ is nominative with no genitive in it, so its answer ran on the pattern of what it began with? It is likewise in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (للهُ) (الله). The reason for bringing the lām into the other two, according to Ubayy and his companions, is that if you said to a man "Who is your master?" and he said "I belong to so-and-so", that would suffice you instead of his saying "My master is so-and-so". Since the two meanings are one, that was used in their speech. One of the Banū ʿĀmir recited to me:
وأَعلُم أننى سَأكُون رَمْساً * إذا سار النواجع لاَ يسيرُ
(I know that I will become a grave which, when the travellers in search of pasture move on, does not move)
(he means the grave)
فقال السَّائلُونَ لمن حفرتم * فقال المخبرونَ لهم: وزير
(The askers said: "For whom have you dug?" and those who answered told them: "A vizier.")
He put it in the nominative, meaning: the dead man is a vizier.

farraa:89-89.t: His saying: ﴿فَأَنَّىٰ تُسْحَرُونَ﴾ — [i.e.] you are turned away. Similar to it is tuʾfakūn. Ufika, suḥira and ṣurifa are the same.

farraa:91-91.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ مَعَهُ مِنْ إِلَـهٍ إِذاً لَّذَهَبَ كُلُّ إِلَـٰهٍ﴾ — idhan is the answer to an implied (muḍmar) statement, that is: had there been gods with Him, ﴿إِذاً لَّذَهَبَ كُلُّ إِلَـٰهٍ بِمَا خَلَقَ﴾ — He is saying: each god would have withdrawn with his creation; ﴿وَلَعَلاَ بَعْضُهُمْ﴾ — He is saying: some of them would have transgressed against others, and some would have overcome others.

farraa:92-92.t: His saying: ﴿عَالِمِ ٱلْغَيْبِ وَٱلشَّهَادَةِ﴾ — the proper way of the sentence is the nominative, as a fresh start (istiʾnāf). The evidence for that is the entry of the fāʾ in His saying ﴿فتَعالىَ﴾. Had you put it in the genitive, the proper way of the sentence would be (وتعالى) with wāw, because whoever puts it in the genitive means only: Glory be to Allah, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and exalted is He. So the entry of the fāʾ indicates that He meant: He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, so exalted is He. Do you not see that you say: "I passed by ʿAbd Allāh the benefactor, and I did good to him"? And had you put (المحسن) in the nominative, it would not be with wāw, because you mean: he is the benefactor, so I did good to him. The genitive in (عَالِم) may also occur, making it follow what precedes it, even though it is with the fāʾ, because the Arabs sometimes start afresh with the fāʾ just as they start afresh with the wāw.

farraa:94-94.t: His saying: ﴿رَبِّ فَلاَ تَجْعَلْنِي﴾ — this fāʾ is the answer to the conditional (jazāʾ), to His saying ﴿إمّا تُرِيَنّى﴾; the vocative (nidāʾ) intervened between them, as you say: "If you come to me, O Zayd, then hurry". Had there been no conditional before it, it would not be permissible to say "O Zayd, so stand up", nor "O Lord, so forgive me", because the vocative is a fresh start, and likewise the command after it is a fresh start which neither the fāʾ nor the wāw enters. You do not say "O people, so stand up", unless it is an answer to a statement before it, as when someone says "The prayer has been called", and you say "O you people, so stand up". This is what makes it permissible.

farraa:99-99.t: His saying: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ ٱرْجِعُونِ﴾ — He made the verb as though for a plural, though he was only calling on his Lord. This is something that runs on the pattern of how Allah describes Himself, as in His saying ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَقْنَاكَ مِنْ قَبْل﴾ in more than one place in the Qurʾān; so this ran on that pattern.

farraa:100-100.t: His saying: ﴿وَمِن وَرَآئِهِمْ بَرْزَخٌ﴾ — the barzakh is from the day one dies until the day one is raised. His saying ﴿وَجَعَل بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخاً﴾ — He is saying: a barrier. "Barrier" and "respite" are close in meaning; that is, you say "Between them there is a barrier [preventing them] from visiting each other", and by "barrier" you may intend a long distance, or you may intend a preventing matter, such as an oath or enmity. So what prevents in distance became like what prevents in events, and al-barzakh applies to both.

farraa:106-106.t:
His saying: ﴿قَالُواْ رَبَّنَا غَلَبَتْ عَلَيْنَا شِقْوَتُنَا﴾ — Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Sharīk narrated to me from Abū Isḥāq, (and Qays) from Abū Isḥāq, and Zuhayr ibn Muʿāwiya Abū Khaythama al-Juʿfī from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that he read (شَقَاوَتَنَا) with an alif and fatḥa on the shīn. Al-Farrāʾ was asked: "Did Zuhayr tell you [this]?" He said: "O you people, I have not heard anything from Zuhayr." The people of Medina and ʿĀṣim read (شِقْوَتُنَا), and it is common. Abū Tharwān recited to me:
كُلِّف من عَنَائه وشِقوتِهْ * بنتَ ثمانِى عَشْرَةٍ من حِجَّتهِ
(Out of his toil and his misery, he became infatuated with a girl of eighteen years.)
Al-Farrāʾ said: were it not for ʿAbd Allāh, I would read it only (شِقْوَتُنَا).

farraa:110-110.t:
His saying: ﴿سِخْرِيّاً﴾ and ﴿سُخْرِيّا﴾ — it has been read both ways, and the ḍamma is better. Those who read with kasra said: what is from al-sukhra (forced labour) has ḍamma, and what is from mockery has kasra.
Al-Kisāʾī said: I heard the Arabs say baḥr lujjī and lijjī (a deep sea), and durrī and dirrī, related to al-durr (pearls), and al-kursī and al-kirsī; and this is common. In his view it is like their saying al-ʿuṣiyy and al-ʿiṣiyy, and al-uswa and al-iswa.

farraa:111-111.t: His saying: ﴿أَنَّهُمْ هُمُ ٱلْفَآئِزُونَ﴾ — al-Aʿmash read it with kasra as a fresh start, and others read it with fatḥa on [the sense]: I have rewarded them with triumph through Paradise; so anna is in the position of the accusative. And [it would be possible] had you made it accusative by implying a genitive particle: I rewarded them because they are the triumphant, through their deeds in the past. «[Translator's note: the final sentence is elliptical in the source; it lacks an explicit apodosis.]»

farraa:112-112.t: His saying: ﴿قَالَ كَمْ لَبِثْتُمْ﴾ — the reading of the people of Medina is ﴿قالَ كَمْ لبِثْتُم﴾, and of the people of Kufa ﴿قُلْ كَمْ لبِثْتُمْ﴾.

farraa:113-113.t: His saying: ﴿لَبِثْنَا يَوْماً أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ﴾ — that is: we do not know; (فاسْأَلِ) the recording angels (al-ḥafaẓa) — they are those who keep count.

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: The clause «فأخذتهم» is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); the preposition «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الصيحة». The clause «فجعلناهم» is conjoined to the clause «أخذتهم», and «غثاء» is the second object. As for «فبُعْدًا للقوم»: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and [«بعدًا» is] a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. بعدوا بعدًا; the preposition «للقوم» is attached to an omitted [verb] whose implied form is أعني. The clause «فبُعدًا» is the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying) of an implied verb of saying, and the clause of the implied saying is conjoined to the clause «أخذتهم».

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: The clause «ما تسبق» is a naʿt (adjective) of {قُرُونًا}; the linking pronoun is implied, its implied form being فيها. «مِن» is redundant (zāʾida), «أمة» is the fāʿil (agent), and the clause «وما يستأخرون» is conjoined to the clause «ما تسبق».

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: «تترى»: ḥāl (circumstantial) of «رسلنا». «كل» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) «كذبوه»; «ما» is maṣdariyya (infinitival); «أمة» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), «رسولها» is the fāʿil (agent); the implied sense is: كذَّبوه كل وقت مجيء رسول (they belied him every time a messenger came). «بعضًا» is the second object, and likewise «أحاديث». As for «فبعدًا»: the fāʾ is resumptive; «بُعْدا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an implied verb, ابعدوا; the preposition «لقوم» is attached to an implied أعني. The clause «فابعدوا بعدًا» is the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying) of an implied verb of saying, and the clause of the implied saying (قلنا) is conjoined to the clause «جعلناهم».

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: «هارون»: badal (substitute), accusative. «وسلطان»: a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «آياتنا».

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: The preposition «إلى فرعون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {أَرْسَلْنَا}; the clause «فاستكبروا» is conjoined to the preceding clause {أَرْسَلْنَا}. «عالين»: an adjective (ṣifa), accusative with yāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: «مثلنا»: naʿt (adjective), genitive. The wāw in «وقومهما» is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), [followed by] a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «نؤمن».

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: The clause «ولقد آتينا موسى» is conjoined to the clause {أَرْسَلْنَا} in verse (45); the clause «لقد آتينا» is the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), and the clause «لعلهم يهتدون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: «الرسل»: ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). The clause «كلوا» is the response to the vocative, resumptive; «صالحًا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «إني بما تعملون عليم» is resumptive, within the scope of the response to the vocative; «ما» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and the interpreted maṣdar is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عليم».

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: The clause «وإن هذه أمتكم» is conjoined to the preceding response to the vocative; the clause «وأنا ربكم» is conjoined to the clause «وإن هذه أمتكم»; and the clause «فاتقون» is conjoined to the clause «وأنا ربكم». The verb is an imperative, the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the implied (muqaddar) yāʾ is the object of the verb.

harrat-mujtaba:53-53.t: The clause «فتقطَّعوا» is resumptive. «بينهم» is an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), attached (mutaʿalliq). «زبرًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «تقطَّعوا». «لديهم» is an adverb attached to the ṣila (relative clause). «فَرِحون» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «كل», and the clause «كل حزب فرحون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:54-54.t: The clause «فذَرْهم» is resumptive; the preposition «في غمرتهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in «فذرهم». «حتى» is a particle of limit and a preposition; «حين» is a genitive noun, [the phrase being] attached to «ذَرْهم».

harrat-mujtaba:55-55.t: The interpreted maṣdar fills the place of the two objects of «حسب». The preposition «من مال» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ما». «أنَّ» is an abrogating particle (nāsikha); «ما» is a relative noun, its noun (ism); and the preposition «به» is attached to «نمدُّهم».

harrat-mujtaba:56-56.t: The clause «نسارع» is the khabar (predicate) of the preceding «أنَّ»; the link between the noun of inna and its khabar is implied, i.e. به. The clause «بل لا يشعرون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:57-57.t: The preposition «من خشية» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) «مشفقون».

harrat-mujtaba:58-58.t: (والذين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The relative noun is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding relative noun; the preposition «بآيات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يؤمنون».

harrat-mujtaba:59-59.t: (والذين هم بربهم لا يشركون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The relative noun is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding relative noun, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

harrat-mujtaba:60-60.t: The first object of «يؤتون» is implied (muqaddar), i.e. الناس (people); «ما» is a relative noun, the second object. The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw in «يؤتون». The interpreted maṣdar from «أن» and what follows it is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), namely the lām. The preposition «إلى ربهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «راجعون».

harrat-mujtaba:61-61.t: The clause «أولئك يسارعون» is the khabar (predicate) of {إِنَّ} in verse (57), and the clause «وهم لها سابقون» is conjoined to the clause «يسارعون».

harrat-mujtaba:62-62.t: The clause «ولا نكلف» is resumptive; «وُسْعَها» is the second object, and «إلا» is restrictive (li-l-ḥaṣr). The clause «ولدينا كتاب» is conjoined to the resumptive clause; the clause «ينطق» is a naʿt (adjective) of «كتاب»; and the clause «وهم لا يظلمون» is conjoined to the clause «ولدينا كتاب».

harrat-mujtaba:63-63.t: The clause «بل قلوبهم في غمرة» is resumptive. The preposition «من هذا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «غمرة», and the preposition «من دون» is attached to a naʿt of «أعمال». The clause «ولهم أعمال» is conjoined to the resumptive clause, and the clause «هم لها عاملون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «لهم».

harrat-mujtaba:64-64.t: «حتى» is inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya); «إذا» is an adverbial conditional particle (ẓarfiyya sharṭiyya) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the sense of the apodosis; the second «إذا» is the «إذا» of surprise (fujāʾiyya). The conditional clause is resumptive, and the clause «إذا هم يجأرون» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

harrat-mujtaba:65-65.t: The clause «لا تجأروا» is the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying) of an implied verb of saying, and the implied saying is a resumptive clause. The clause «إنكم منا لا تنصرون» is resumptive, and the preposition «منا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb «تُنْصَرون».

harrat-mujtaba:66-66.t: The clause «قد كانت آياتي» is resumptive, within the scope of the saying; the preposition «على أعقابكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تنكصون».

harrat-mujtaba:67-67.t: «مستكبرين»: ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw in {تَنْكِصُونَ}; the preposition «به» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مستكبرين». «سامرا» is a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of {تَنْكِصُونَ}, and the clause «تهجرون» is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of {تَنْكِصُونَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:68-68.t: The clause «أفلم يدبَّروا» is resumptive; «أم» is the disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) one; and the clause «جاءهم» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:69-69.t: The clause «أم لم يعرفوا» is resumptive; the clause «فهم منكرون» is conjoined to the resumptive clause; the preposition «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:70-70.t: «أم» is the disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) one, and the clause after it is resumptive; «جِنَّة» is a mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause «جاءهم» is resumptive, and the clause «وأكثرهم كارهون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in «جاءهم». The preposition «للحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «كارهون».

harrat-mujtaba:71-71.t: The conditional clause is parenthetical (muʿtariḍa) between the parts of the iḍrāb (digression). «مَن» is a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الأرض»; the preposition «فيهن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. The clause «أتيناهم» is resumptive, and the clause «فهم معرضون» is conjoined to the clause «أتيناهم»; the preposition «عن ذكرهم» is attached to «معرضون».

harrat-mujtaba:72-72.t: «أم» is the disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) one. The clause «فخراج ربك خير» is resumptive, and the clause «وهو خير» is conjoined to the clause «فخراج ربك خير».

harrat-mujtaba:73-73.t: The clause «وإنك لتدعوهم» is resumptive, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

harrat-mujtaba:74-74.t: The clause «وإن الذين ...» is conjoined to the clause «إنك لتدعوهم»; the preposition «عن الصراط» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ناكبون».

harrat-mujtaba:75-75.t: The conditional clause is resumptive. The preposition «بهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the ṣila (relative clause); the preposition «من ضر» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ما»; the preposition «في طغيانهم» is attached to «لجُّوا»; and the clause «يعمهون» is a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of «لجوا».

harrat-mujtaba:76-76.t: The clause «فما استكانوا» is conjoined to the clause «أخذناهم», and the clause «وما يتضرَّعون» is conjoined to the clause «استكانوا».

harrat-mujtaba:77-77.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; «ذا» is a naʿt (adjective) of «بابًا»; the clause «إذا هم فيه مبلسون» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the preposition «فيه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) «مُبْلسون».

harrat-mujtaba:78-78.t: The clause «وهو الذي» is resumptive. «قليلا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is an adjective of the maṣdar (verbal noun), and «ما» is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. تشكرون شكرا قليلا (you give little thanks). The clause «تشكرون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:79-79.t: The preposition «في الأرض» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause «تحشرون» is conjoined to the clause «ذرأكم».

harrat-mujtaba:80-80.t: The clause «وله اختلاف» is conjoined to the clause «يميت», and the clause «أفلا تعقلون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:81-81.t: The clause «قالوا» is resumptive; «مثل» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «ما» is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:82-82.t: «إذا» is an adverbial conditional particle (ẓarfiyya sharṭiyya) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the sense of the apodosis; it is not attached to «مبعوثون», because what comes after «إنَّ» does not govern what precedes it. So the apodosis is implied as نبعث (we will be raised), and the clause «أئنا لمبعوثون» is explicative (tafsīriyya) of the apodosis.

harrat-mujtaba:83-83.t: «نحن» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun «نا», and «آباؤنا» is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the pronoun «نا»; conjoining to the attached nominative pronoun is permissible because of the separating element. «هذا» is the second object; the preposition «من قبل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «وُعِدنا». «إن» is negating; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «أساطير» is the khabar (predicate), and «إلا» is restrictive (li-l-ḥaṣr). The clause «إن هذا إلا أساطير» is resumptive within the scope of the saying.

harrat-mujtaba:84-84.t: The preposition «فيها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause). The conditional clause is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:85-85.t: The preposition «لله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. هي لله. The fāʾ conjoins to the omitted maqūl al-qawl (object of saying), i.e. أغفلتم فلا تَذَكَّرون؟ (have you been heedless, so that you do not remember?)

harrat-mujtaba:87-87.t: The preposition «لله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. هي لله. The clause «أفلا تتقون» is conjoined to the implied maqūl al-qawl (object of saying), i.e. أغفلتم فلا تتقون؟ (have you been heedless, so that you do not fear [Him]?)

harrat-mujtaba:88-88.t: «مَن» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). The preposition «بيده» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of «ملكوت», and «ملكوت» is a mubtadaʾ; the clause «بيده ملكوت» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «من». The clause «وهو يجير» is conjoined to the khabar clause. The clause «إن كنتم تعلمون» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:89-89.t: The fāʾ in «فأنى» links the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. إن علمتم هذا فأنى (if you know this, then how…). «أنى» is an interrogative noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) in «تُسْحرون»; «تسحرون» is a passive imperfect verb with its nāʾib fāʿil. The clause «سيقولون» is resumptive, and the clause «هي لله» is the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying), in the position of the accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:90-90.t: The clause «أتيناهم» is resumptive, and the clause «وإنهم لكاذبون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:91-91.t: The clause «ما اتخذ الله» is resumptive; «ولد» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida). The clause «وما كان» is conjoined to the resumptive clause; «إله» is the noun of kāna, and «من» is redundant. The clause «لَذهب» is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. لو كان معه آلهة لذهب (had there been gods with Him, [each god] would have taken away). The preposition «على بعض» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «علا»; the preposition «عمَّا» is attached to the implied verb «نسبِّح»; and the clause «نسبِّح سبحان» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:92-92.t: «عالم»: badal (substitute) of the Divine Name. The clause «فتعالى» is conjoined to the implied governor of the preceding {سُبْحَانَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:93-93.t: «إمَّا» is composed of the conditional «إن» and the redundant «ما»; [then comes] an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of the jussive; the nūn is for emphasis. Since the nūn of protection was dropped because of the succession of identical letters, the nūn of emphasis was given kasra to suit the yāʾ, and the yāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «ما» is a relative noun, the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:94-94.t: The clause «ربِّ» is parenthetical (muʿtariḍa); the clause «فلا تجعلني» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the preposition «في القوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:95-95.t: The clause «وإنا لقادرون» is resumptive. The genitive maṣdar «على أن نريك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قادرون». «ما» is a relative noun, the second object; and the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).

harrat-mujtaba:96-96.t: The clause «هي أحسن» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; the clause «نحن أعلم» is resumptive; «ما» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and the genitive interpreted maṣdar is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أعلم», i.e. أعلم بوصفهم (more knowing of their describing).

harrat-mujtaba:97-97.t: The two preposition and its genitive nouns are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb «أعوذ».

harrat-mujtaba:98-98.t: The interpreted maṣdar «أن يحضرون» is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ) «مِنْ». The clause «ربِّ» is parenthetical (muʿtariḍa). «يحضرون» is accusative by dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the implied (muqaddar) yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:99-99.t: The conditional clause is resumptive, and «حتى» is inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya).

harrat-mujtaba:100-100.t: The clause «لعلي أعمل» is resumptive; «صالحا» is an object, and the preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «صالحا». «كلا» is a particle of deterrence and rebuke. The resumptive clause «إنها كلمة» has no grammatical position; «كلمة» here is a case of naming the part and intending the whole. The clause «هو قائلها» is a naʿt of «كلمة». The wāw in «ومِنْ ورائهم» is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «هو», in the sense of the plural. The preposition «إلى يوم» is attached to a naʿt of «برزخ», and the clause «يبعثون» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:101-101.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). The clause «فلا أنساب بينهم» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the adverb «بينهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate), and «يوم» is attached to the [notion of] settledness (istiqrār) to which the khabar is attached; «إذٍ» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause «ولا يتساءلون» is conjoined to the apodosis clause.

harrat-mujtaba:102-102.t: The conditional clause is conjoined to the preceding resumptive conditional clause. The clause «ثقلت» is the khabar (predicate) of the conditional «مَن». «هم» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:103-103.t: «أولئك الذين»: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The preposition «في جهنم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second khabar «خالدون».

harrat-mujtaba:104-104.t: The clause «تلفح» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in {خَالِدُونَ}; the clause «وهم فيها كالحون» is conjoined to the ḥāl clause; the preposition «فيها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «كالحون».

harrat-mujtaba:105-105.t: The interrogative clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying) of an implied verb of saying, and the implied saying is resumptive, i.e. يقال لهم (it will be said to them). The clause «تتلى» is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, and the clause «فكنتم» is conjoined to the clause «تكن».

harrat-mujtaba:106-106.t: The clause «غلبت» is the response to the vocative, resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:107-107.t: The clause «ربنا» is resumptive within the scope of the saying; the clause «فإن عدنا» is conjoined to the clause «أخرجنا».

harrat-mujtaba:108-108.t: «ولا تكلمون»: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the implied (muqaddar) yāʾ is the object of the verb.

harrat-mujtaba:109-109.t: The hāʾ in «إنه» is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). The preposition «من عبادي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «فريق». The clause «يقولون» is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, in the position of the accusative. The clause «فاغفر» is conjoined to the response to the vocative, and the clause «وأنت خير الراحمين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «ارحمنا».

harrat-mujtaba:110-110.t: (فاتخذتموهم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The fāʾ is a conjunction; [then] a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn; the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent), the mīm is for the plural, and the wāw is for prolongation (ishbāʿ). «سخريا» is the second object. The interpreted maṣdar «أن أنسوكم» is genitive by «حتى», attached to (mutaʿalliq) «اتخذتموهم». «ذِكْري» is the second object. The preposition «منهم» is attached to «تضحكون».

harrat-mujtaba:111-111.t: The second object of «جزيتهم» is omitted, i.e. الجنة (Paradise). «ما» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and the genitive maṣdar is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. «هم» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ. The clause «صبروا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative. The interpreted maṣdar from «أنَّ» and what follows it is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), namely the lām.

harrat-mujtaba:112-112.t: «كم»: an interrogative noun, an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) «لبثتم». «عدد» is a tamyīz (specification), accusative. «سنين» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive with yāʾ, because it is treated like the sound masculine plural.

harrat-mujtaba:113-113.t: «يوما»: an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. «بعض» is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «يوما». The clause «فاسأل» is conjoined to the clause «لبثنا».

harrat-mujtaba:114-114.t: «إلا» is restrictive (li-l-ḥaṣr). «قليلا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. لبثا قليلا (a short stay). The maṣdar is the fāʿil (agent) of an implied «ثبت». The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. لعلمتم قلة لبثكم (you would have known the shortness of your stay). The clause «لو ثبت أنكم كنتم» is resumptive within the scope of the saying.

harrat-mujtaba:115-115.t: The maṣdar from «أنَّ» and what follows it fills the place of the two objects of «حسب». «أنما» is a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa). «عبثا» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). The second maṣdar is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first maṣdar.

harrat-mujtaba:116-116.t: The clause «فتعالى» is resumptive; «الملك الحق» are two naʿts (adjectives) of the Divine Name. The clause of transcendence [Translator's note: «لا إله إلا هو»] is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the Divine Name; «إلا» is restrictive (li-l-ḥaṣr); «هو» is a badal (substitute) of the latent pronoun in the omitted khabar (predicate); «رب» is a badal of «هو».

harrat-mujtaba:117-117.t: The conditional clause is resumptive. The clause «يَدْعُ» is a khabar (predicate), and the clause «لا برهان له» is a second naʿt (adjective). «عند» is an adverb of place (ẓarf makān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar. The clause «إنه لا يفلح» is resumptive, and the hāʾ is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn).

harrat-mujtaba:118-118.t: The clause «وأنت خير الراحمين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «ارحم».

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The relative noun is a naʿt (adjective) of {الْمُؤْمِنُونَ}, and the preposition and its genitive noun «في صلاتهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) «خاشعون».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «عن اللغو» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) «معرضون».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The lām in «للزكاة» is for strengthening (taqwiya), redundant (zāʾida), and «الزكاة» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «فاعلون», placed first.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The lām in «لفروجهم» is for strengthening (taqwiya), redundant (zāʾida), and «فروجهم» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «حافظون», placed first.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr), and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {حَافِظُونَ}; «ما» is a relative noun conjoined to «أزواجهم»; the clause «فإنهم غير ملومين» is resumptive; «ملومين» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The fāʾ in «فمن» is a conjunction; «مَن» is a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «فمن ابتغى» is conjoined to the clause «إنهم غير ملومين», and the clause «ابتغى» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. The clause «فأولئك هم العادون» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and «هم» is for separation (faṣl), with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The lām in «لأماناتهم» is redundant (zāʾida) for strengthening (taqwiya), and «أماناتهم» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «راعون».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: (على صلواتهم يحافظون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يحافظون».

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: (أولئك هم الوارثون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] A mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); «هم» is for separation (faṣl).

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «الذين» is a naʿt (adjective) of {الْوَارِثُونَ}; the clause «هم خالدون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) in «يرثون»; the preposition and its genitive noun «فيها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خالدون».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The wāw in «ولقد» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «من سلالة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خلقنا», and the second preposition and its genitive noun is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «سلالة».

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The clause «ثم جعلناه» is conjoined to the clause {خَلَقْنَا}; the preposition and its genitive noun «في قرار» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «نطفة».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: «علقة» is the second object, by making the verb include the meaning of ṣayyara (to make into); «خلقا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ. The clause «فتبارك» is resumptive; «أحسن» is a naʿt (adjective), which is preferable to a badal (substitute), because the badal is rare among derived words; and it is definite here because the annexation of the elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl) is a true (maḥḍa) annexation.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «ثم إنكم بعد ذلك لميتون» is conjoined to the clause {أَنْشَأْنَاهُ}; «بعد» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ميِّتون».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The clause «ولقد خلقنا» is conjoined to {وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا} in verse (12). «طرائق» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the clause «وما كنا عن الخلق غافلين» is conjoined to the clause «خلقنا».

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «بقدر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ماء»; the clause «وإنا لقادرون» is conjoined to the clause «فأسكنَّاه»; the preposition and its genitive noun «به» is attached to the maṣdar (verbal noun) «ذهاب», and the preposition and its genitive noun «على ذهاب» is attached to the khabar (predicate) «قادرون».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: (فأنشأنا لكم به جنات) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The two preposition and its genitive nouns are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the preposition and its genitive noun «من نخيل» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «جنات». The preposition and its genitive noun «لكم» is attached to the khabar (predicate), and the second preposition and its genitive noun, «فيها», is attached to the "being established" (istiqrār) to which the khabar is attached. The clause «لكم فيها فواكه» is a naʿt of «جنات», and the clause «تأكلون» is conjoined to the clause «لكم فيها فواكه».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: «شجرة» is a noun conjoined to {جَنَّاتٍ}; the clause «تخرج» is a naʿt (adjective) of «شجرة»; the clause «تنبت» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «تخرج»; the preposition and its genitive noun «بالدهن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; «صبغ» is conjoined to «الدهن»; and the preposition and its genitive noun «للآكلين» is attached to a naʿt of «صبغ».

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The clause «وإن لكم ...» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «في الأنعام» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «لعبرة», and the lām is for emphasis (tawkīd). The clause «نسقيكم» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «مما» is attached to the verb; the preposition and its genitive noun «في بطونها» is attached to the implied (muqaddar) ṣila (relative clause). The clause «ولكم فيها منافع» is conjoined to the clause «نسقيكم»; the preposition and its genitive noun «فيها» is attached to a ḥāl of «منافع», the mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause «ومنها تأكلون» is conjoined to the clause «نسقيكم».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The clause «تُحْمَلون» is conjoined to the clause {تَأْكُلُونَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The clause «ولقد أرسلنا» is conjoined to the clause {وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا} in verse (17). The clause «ما لكم من إله غيره» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the name of Majesty; the preposition and its genitive noun «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «إله», and «مِن» is redundant (zāʾida); «غيره» is a naʿt (adjective) following the position of «إله», and the annexation did not give it definiteness because it is vague. The clause «تتقون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «من قومه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «كفروا»; «بشر» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «يريد» is a second naʿt (adjective), and the interpreted maṣdar is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «يريد». The conditional clause is conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb), and the clause «ما سمعنا» is resumptive within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: «إنْ» is negating, and the clause is resumptive within the scope of the speech, as is the clause «فتربصوا». «حتى»: a particle of limit and a preposition; «حين»: a genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تربَّصوا».

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The «bāʾ» is a preposition of causation (sababiyya), «ما» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and the interpreted maṣdar is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the implied form is: because of their denying.

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: «أن» is explicative (tafsīriyya), and the clause «اصنع» is explicative; the preposition and its genitive noun «بأعيننا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «اصنع». The conditional clause is conjoined to the clause «اصنع», and the clause «فاسلك» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). The tanwīn in «كل» is a compensation for a single word; «زوجين» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «أهلك» is a noun conjoined to «زوجين». «إلا» is for exception; «مَنْ» is a relative noun, excepted; the preposition and its genitive noun «منهم» is attached to a ḥāl of the yāʾ in «عليه» [Translator's note: so in the source; «عليه» has a hāʾ, not a yāʾ]. The clause «إنهم مغرقون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The conditional clause is conjoined to the conditional clause before it, {فَإِذَا جَاءَ أَمْرُنَا.....}. «أنت» is tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun tāʾ; «مَن» is a relative noun conjoined to the tāʾ, and conjoining an overt noun to a nominative pronoun is permitted because of the presence of a separator. «معك»: an adverb of place (ẓarf makān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the ṣila (relative clause); the preposition and its genitive noun «على الفلك» is attached to «استويت»; and the relative noun is a naʿt (adjective) of the name of Majesty.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: «منزلا» is the second object, and the clause «وأنت خير المنزلين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) in «أنزلني».

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: (إن في ذلك لآيات) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The lām is for emphasis (tawkīd). «إنْ» is lightened (mukhaffafa) and inoperative (muhmala), with an abrogating verb with its noun and its khabar (predicate); the lām in «لمبتلين» is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); and the clause «وإن كنا لمبتلين» is conjoined to the resumptive one.

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: The clause «ثم أنشأنا» is conjoined to the clause «إن كنا» before it; «قرنًا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and its naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «رسولا». «أن» is explicative (tafsīriyya), and the clause after it is explicative. The clause «ما لكم من إله غيره» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the name of Majesty; «إله» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «مِن» is redundant (zāʾida), and «غيره» is a naʿt; the clause «تتقون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «من قومه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الملأ»; «الذين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «الملأ»; «مثلكم» is a naʿt of «بشر»; the clause «يأكل» is a second naʿt. The referent pronoun of the relative noun in «مما» was omitted, the implied form being: تشربون منه (you drink of it).

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: The clause «ولئن أطعتم» is resumptive; «إذًا» is a particle of response; and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); the clause «إنكم لخاسرون» is the answer to the oath.

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: The clause «أيعدكم» is resumptive within the scope of the speech. «إذا» is a pure adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مخرجون». The interpreted maṣdar formed from «أن» and what follows it is the second object of «يعدكم»; the abrogating particle was repeated because of the length of the separation, and «مخرجون» is the khabar (predicate) of the first «أن».

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: The clause «هيهات» is resumptive within the scope of the speech. «هيهات» is a verbal noun with the force of a past verb (ism fiʿl māḍin) meaning "it is far", and the second is a verbal tawkīd (emphasis). The lām is redundant (zāʾida), «ما» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and a passive imperfect verb; the interpreted maṣdar is the fāʿil (agent) of «هيهات».

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: «إن» is negating; «هي إلا حياتنا» are a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); the clause is resumptive within the scope of the speech, and so is the clause «نموت». The clause «وما نحن بمبعوثين» is conjoined to the clause «نحيا», and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar of the «ما» that operates like laysa.

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: «إنْ» is negating; the clause «افترى» is a naʿt (adjective) of «رجل»; the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) of «ما», which operates like laysa. The clause «إن هو إلا رجل» is resumptive within the scope of the speech, and the clause «وما نحن له بمؤمنين» is conjoined to the clause «افترى».

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: The clause «انصرني» is the response to the vocative, resumptive; the clause «كَذَّبون» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative; «ما» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and the genitive interpreted maṣdar is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «انصرني».

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: His saying «عمَّا قليل»: «عن» is a preposition, «ما» is redundant (zāʾida), «قليل» is a genitive noun, and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نادمين». The lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of like letters; the implied (muqaddar) wāw is its noun, «نادمين» is its khabar (predicate), and the nūn is for emphasis (tawkīd). The clause «ليصبحُنَّ» is the response to the implied oath, and the oath with its response is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb).

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted, {قد أَفْلح}: Warsh read it by throwing the vowel of the hamza onto the dāl and dropping the hamza. The hamza was dropped only because, when its vowel was thrown onto what precedes it, it remained quiescent, while the dāl before it is [considered] quiescent, because the vowel on it is accidental; so there came together what resembles two quiescent letters, and the hamza was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. It had the better claim to be dropped because it had been impaired by the loss of its vowel, because the heaviness occurred through it, and because it is the one that is quiescent in pronunciation.

mekki-muskil:8-8.t:
His saying {لِأَمَانَاتِهِمْ}: أمانة is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and the rule for a maṣdar is that it is not made plural, because it indicates both little and much of its genus. But since the kinds of trust differ, as it applies to prayer, zakāt, purification, pilgrimage and other acts of worship, making it plural is permissible; for, because of the difference of its kinds, it resembled the direct object, so it was made plural as the direct object is made plural. They agreed on the plural in His saying {أَن تُؤَدُّوا الْأَمَانَات إِلَى أَهلهَا}. Ibn Kathīr read it in the singular in {قد أَفْلح} [i.e. in this sūra]; his evidence is their agreement on the singular in وعهدهم — He did not say وعهودهم — and it is a maṣdar like الأمانة; so he read it in the singular like العهد, according to the basic nature of the maṣdar. Likewise is the matter with صلاتهم and صلواتهم.
His saying {وشجرة}: accusative, conjoined to {جنَّات من نخيل}. Al-Farrāʾ permitted the nominative in it on the implied form "and there is a tree" (وَثمّ شَجَرَة). تخرج and what follows it is a naʿt (adjective) of the tree.

mekki-muskil:110-110.t: His saying {سخريا}: whoever reads the sīn with ḍamma makes it from السخرة and التسخير (subjection, forced labour), and whoever reads it with kasra makes it from mockery and play. It is also said that they are two dialectal forms with the meaning of mockery.

mekki-muskil:111-111.t: His saying {أَنهم هم الفائزون}: أَن is in the position of the accusative as the second object of جزيتهم, its implied form being "I have rewarded them today, for their patience, with triumph" (إني جزيتهم الْيَوْم بصبرهم الْفَوْز), and triumph is deliverance. It is also possible that أَن is in the position of the accusative by the omission of the lām, i.e. "I have rewarded them for their patience because they are the triumphant ones in My knowledge and in what was previously decreed for them by My judgement".

mekki-muskil:14-14.t:
His saying {ثمَّ خلقنَا النُّطْفَة علقَة}: two objects of خلق, because it has the meaning of صيرنا ("We turned … into"). When خلق has the meaning of "brought into being / originated" it takes one object, and when it has the meaning of صيّر it takes two objects.
His saying سيناء: whoever reads the sīn with fatḥa makes it like حمراء, so it is a diptote because of the hamza of the feminine and its being an adjective; and it is said: because of the hamza of the feminine and its being inseparable. Its pattern cannot properly be فَعْلال, because فعلال has not come as a noun so that this could be assimilated (mulḥaq) to it; فعلال has come only in maṣdars (verbal nouns) specifically, e.g. الزلزال. Had it been فعلال, it would be fully declined; but it is a diptote both when definite and indefinite, because the two causes, femininity and being an adjective, are inseparable from it [Translator's note: so in the source; it is a place name, and "adjective" (ṣifa) is as written].
As for whoever reads the sīn with kasra, he makes it a noun assimilated to سرداح, like علباء and حرباء; so the hamza is like the yāʾ in درحاية, and it is فِعْلال. It may not be فِعْلاء, since there is no فعلاء in the language and the hamza of the feminine is not found in فعلاء. It ought then to be fully declined, as علباء and حرباء are fully declined; but it is the name of a spot or a land, and it is definite, so it is a diptote because of femininity and definiteness. Al-Akhfash said: it is a foreign definite noun, so it is like a woman whom you have named جعفر.
Like it in being a diptote because of femininity and definiteness is His saying {وطور سينين}: سينين is a diptote because it is definite, the name of a spot or a land, and it is on the pattern فعليل with its third radical repeated, like خنذيذ. Its pattern may not be فِعْلين like غسلين, because al-Akhfash and others reported that the singular of سينين is سينينة; and an interpretation like this is not permissible for غسلين, since غسلينة has not been heard.

mekki-muskil:20-20.t: His saying {تنْبت بالدهن}: whoever reads تنبت with ḍamma on the tāʾ (تُنبِت) makes the bāʾ redundant (zāʾida), because the verb passes to its object without a preposition, as it is a four-letter verb from أنبت الشيء. But it is said that the bāʾ entered to indicate the constancy and continuity of the growing, as in His saying {اقْرَأ باسم رَبك}. It is also said that the bāʾ in {بالدهن} entered only upon a second object which is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), the first being omitted, its implied form being "it produces its fruit with oil" (تنْبت جناها بالدهن), i.e. with oil in it — as you say خرج بثيابه ("he went out in his clothes") and ركب بسلاحه ("he rode with his weapons"), i.e. he went out wearing [them] and rode armed; so the genitive noun is in the position of the ḥāl. As for whoever reads the tāʾ with fatḥa (تَنبُت), the bāʾ is for transitivity, nothing else, because it is an intransitive three-letter verb; and it may be in the position of a ḥāl. They have said أنبت الزرع and نبت ("the crop grew"), so the two readings would have one meaning.

mekki-muskil:29-29.t: His saying منزلا: whoever reads the mīm with ḍamma (مُنزَلا) makes it a maṣdar (verbal noun) from أنزل, since before it is أنزلني, and its meaning is "a blessed landing" (إنزالا مُبَارَكًا). It may also be a noun of place, as though he said "land me in a place or a spot"; so it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), not an adverb (ẓarf), as though he said "make a place for me". Whoever reads the mīm with fatḥa (مَنزِلا) makes it [Translator's note: the source writes حعله for جعله] the maṣdar of a three-letter verb, because أنزل indicates نزل; and it may also be a noun of place.

mekki-muskil:33-33.t: His saying {وَيشْرب مِمَّا تشربون}: مَا with the verb is a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar), so it does not need a resumptive pronoun. It may also have the meaning of الَّذِي, with the resumptive pronoun omitted from {تشربون}, i.e. "of what you drink" (مِمَّا تشربونه). Al-Farrāʾ said: its implied form is "of what you drink from" (مِمَّا تشربون مِنْهُ), then مِنْهُ was omitted.

mekki-muskil:35-35.t:
His saying {أَنكُمْ مخرجون}: أَن is a badal (substitute) from the first أن, which is accusative by يعد, according to Sībawayh. Al-Jarmī and al-Mubarrad said: it is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first, because the substitution from أن can only come after its ṣila is complete. But it is binding on both of them also that emphasis is not permissible, because emphasis can only come after the relative (mawṣūl) is complete with its ṣila; its ṣila is the khabar, and the khabar is complete only at His saying {مخرجون}, which has not yet come. Al-Akhfash said: the second أن is in the position of the nominative by the adverb (ẓarf), which is إذا, its implied form being "Does he promise you that, when you die, your being brought out [will happen]?" (أيعدكم أَنكُمْ إذا متم إخراجكم), i.e. at the time of your death is your being brought out.
His saying {إِذا متم} up to {مخرجون} is in the position [Translator's note: the source has ضع, evidently for موضع] of the nominative as the khabar of the first أن, and the governing word (ʿāmil) of إذا is implied, as though you said "Does he promise you that, when you die, your being brought out will occur?" (أيعدكم أَنكُمْ حَادث إذا متم إخراجكم). إخراجكم may not govern it, because it would then be in the ṣila of الإخراج while placed before it, and placing the ṣila before the mawṣūl is not permissible. Nor is it good for His saying متم to govern إذا, because إذا is annexed to it, and the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern the muḍāf, because it is part of it. This is like your saying الْيَوْم الْقِتَال ("today is the fighting"): اليوم is the khabar of القتال, and the governor of اليوم is implied, as though you said "today the fighting occurs" or "the fighting is occurring today"; القتال may not govern اليوم, because it would be in its ṣila while placed before it, and that is not permissible. This implied [word] that governs adverbs contains a pronoun referring back to the mubtadaʾ; so when you set up the adverb or the preposition with its genitive noun in its place and omit it, that pronoun becomes notionally present in the adverb or the preposition phrase, because it stands in place of the khabar which contained a pronoun referring back to the mubtadaʾ. This question is a foundation in this area, so understand it, for it is difficult (mushkil).

mekki-muskil:36-36.t:
His saying {هَيْهَات هَيْهَات لما توعدون}: whoever reads the tāʾ with fatḥa makes it indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, and the pause on it, for whoever reads the tāʾ with fatḥa, is with hāʾ according to the Basrans. Al-Yazīdī reported from Abū ʿAmr that the pause in both is on tāʾ. Its position is accusative, as though it is put in the place of the maṣdar (verbal noun), as if you said "far, far away with what you are promised" (بعدا بعدا لما توعدون). It is also said that its position is nominative, as though He said "the remoteness, the remoteness of what you are promised" (الْبعد الْبعد لما توعدون). Whoever reads the tāʾ with kasra pauses with tāʾ, because it is a plural like بيضة and بيضات, as though the singular of هيهات were هيهة. Some of the Arabs give it tanwīn to distinguish between definite and indefinite: as though, when it does not have tanwīn, it is definite in the meaning "the remoteness of what you are promised" — between definite and indefinite [Translator's note: these words are repeated thus in the source] — and when it has tanwīn it is indefinite, as though He said "far away with what you are promised" (بعدا لما توعدون). هيهات is repeated for emphasis.
His saying {تترا}: in the position of the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), or as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الرسل, i.e. "We sent Our messengers successively", i.e. following one another. Whoever reads it with tanwīn — and that is Abū ʿAmr — takes it in one of two ways: either its pattern is فَعْل, like بغل, and it is a maṣdar, the tanwīn having entered upon the fatḥa of the rāʾ; or it is assimilated (mulḥaq) to جعفر, the tanwīn having entered upon the alif of ilḥāq, like أرطى. If you pause on it according to this view, imāla (inclining the vowel) is permissible, because you intend to pause on the alif that entered for ilḥāq, not on the alif of tanwīn, so you may incline it if you wish. If you pause according to the first view, imāla is not permissible, because you pause on the alif that is a substitute for the tanwīn, nothing else. Whoever reads it without tanwīn makes its alif for the feminine — and the alif of the feminine often attaches to maṣdars, like الدعوى and الذكرى — so it is a diptote because of femininity and its inseparability. The tāʾ in all views is a substitute [Translator's note: the source has يدل, evidently for بدل] for a wāw, and its origin is وترى, because it is from المواترة, which is one thing following another.

mekki-muskil:52-52.t:
His saying {وَإِن هَذِه أمتكُم}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by the omission of the preposition, i.e. "and because this…" (وبأن هَذِه) or (لأن هَذِه), and the preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) اتقون. Al-Kisāʾī said: it is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to مَا in His saying {بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ}. Al-Fāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source, evidently for al-Farrāʾ] said: it is in the position of the accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "and know that this…" (وَاعْلَمُوا أَن هَذِه). Whoever reads إن with kasra does so as a new beginning (istiʾnāf).
His saying {أمة وَاحِدَة}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The nominative is permissible by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), or as a badal (substitute) from أمتكم, which is the khabar of إن, or as a khabar after a khabar.

mekki-muskil:53-53.t: His saying {زبرا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. like scriptures (mithla zubur).

mekki-muskil:55-56.t: His saying {أيحسبون أَنما نمدهم بِهِ من مَال وبنين نسارع لَهُم}: the khabar of أن is نسارع لَهُم, on the assumption of the omission of بِهِ, i.e. "We hasten for them with it in good things" (نسارع لَهُم بِهِ فِي الْخيرَات), and مَا has the meaning of الَّذِي. Hishām said: its implied form is "We hasten for them in it" (نسارع لَهُم فِيهِ), then the pronoun was made overt, namely الخيرات, and مَا, which is the noun of أن, stands for the good things. Like it, according to him, is your saying إِن زيدا تكلم عَمْرو فِي زيد ("Zayd — ʿAmr spoke about Zayd"), i.e. about him, then the pronoun was made overt. Sībawayh did not permit this except in poetry. And it has been said that the khabar of أن is omitted.

mekki-muskil:57-57.t: His saying {إِن الَّذين هم من خشيَة رَبهم مشفقون}: the khabar of إن is His saying {أُولَئِكَ يُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْخيرَات}, a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the khabar of إن. The meaning of في الخيرات is "in doing good deeds".

mekki-muskil:67-67.t:
His saying {سامرا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial), and like it is {مستكبرين}.
His saying {تهجرون}: whoever reads the tāʾ with fatḥa makes it from الهجران (forsaking), i.e. "being arrogant about the Sacred House, conversing by night" — i.e. you converse by night in amusement and play because of your security in it while people are in fear in their homelands — "you forsake My signs and what is recited to you of My Book". Whoever reads the tāʾ with ḍamma makes it from الهُجْر, which is raving and speech in which there is no good.

mekki-muskil:76-76.t: His saying {فَمَا اسْتَكَانُوا}: it is استفعلوا from الكون, and its origin is استكونوا; then [Translator's note: the source has نم, evidently for ثم] it underwent weakening (iʿlāl). It is also said that it is افتعلوا from السكون, but the fatḥa of the kāf was lengthened so that it became an alif. The first view is more correct in derivation, and the second more correct in meaning.

mekki-muskil:99-99.t: His saying {قَالَ رب ارْجِعُونِ}: the address from the people of the Fire came only in the plural form because the All-Compelling speaks of Himself in the plural form, so He was addressed with the sense with which He speaks of Himself. It is also said that its meaning is repetition: "send me back, send me back, send me back" (ارجعن ارجعن ارجعن), so the plural was used in the address to indicate the meaning of repetition. Likewise al-Māzinī said about His saying {ألقيا فِي جَهَنَّم} that its meaning is "throw, throw" (ألق ألق).

mekki-muskil:112-112.t: His saying {كم لبثتم}: كم is in the position of the accusative by لبثتم, and {عدد سِنِين} is accusative as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz (specification)). سنين is a sound plural with yāʾ and nūn.

muyesser-irab:92-92.t:
﴿عالم الغيب والشهادة﴾: (عالم الغيب) is genitive (majrūr) as a badal (substitute) for the Name of Majesty, or as an adjective (naʿt) of it.
﴿فتعالى عما يشركون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; (تعالى) is a verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿عما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تعالى﴾; the clause (يشركون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾ and has no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:93-93.t: ﴿قل رب إما تريني ما يوعدون﴾: (رب) is the one addressed in the vocative, annexed to the first-person yāʾ, which is omitted; in ﴿إما﴾ the conditional (إن) has been assimilated into the connective (ṣila) (ما); (تريني) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and it is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the nūn is the nūn of protection (al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ما) is the second object; the clause (يوعدون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾ and has no grammatical position, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e.: what they are promised of the punishment.

muyesser-irab:94-94.t: ﴿رب فلا تجعلني في القوم الظالمين﴾: (رب) is the one addressed in the vocative, annexed to the first-person yāʾ, which is omitted; the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ; (لا) is the lā of request; (تجعلني) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by (لا); the nūn is the nūn of protection (al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿في القوم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second object; (الظالمين) is an adjective (naʿt); and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with the fāʾ.

muyesser-irab:95-95.t: ﴿وإنا على أن نريك ما نعدهم لقادرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is an abrogating particle (of inna and its sisters), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; ﴿على أن نريك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قادرون﴾; (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (نري) is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by (أن), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "we" (نحن); the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and (ما) is the second object; ﴿نعدهم﴾ is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun and has no grammatical position; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), which is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ); and (قادرون) is the khabar (predicate) of (إن).

muyesser-irab:96-96.t: ﴿ادفع بالتي هي أحسن السيئة نحن أعلم بما يصفون﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position; (ادفع) is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); ﴿بالتي﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ادفع﴾; (التي) is an adjective (naʿt) of an omitted noun, i.e.: the trait (الخصلة); ﴿هي أحسن﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and the clause ﴿هي أحسن﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿التي﴾ and has no grammatical position. (السيئة) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (نحن) is a mubtadaʾ, and ﴿أعلم﴾ is the khabar of the clause; the clause ﴿نحن أعلم﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause; ﴿بما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أعلم﴾; the clause (يصفون) is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾ and has no grammatical position; or (ما) is maṣdar-forming, i.e.: by their describing you and their speaking ill of you.

muyesser-irab:97-97.t: ﴿وقل رب أعوذ بك من همزات الشياطين﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; or the wāw is a conjunction joining it to what preceded; (رب) is the one addressed in the vocative, annexed to the first-person yāʾ, which is omitted; (أعوذ) is an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "I" (أنا); (بك) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعوذ﴾; ﴿من همزات﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أعوذ﴾; (الشياطين) is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause ﴿رب أعوذ بك﴾ is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

muyesser-irab:98-98.t: ﴿وأعوذ بك رب أن يحضرون﴾: conjoined to what preceded; (أعوذ) is an imperfect verb, with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), its implied form being "I" (أنا); (بك) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعوذ﴾; (رب) is the one addressed in the vocative, annexed to the first-person yāʾ, which is omitted; (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (يحضرون) is in the subjunctive by (أن), the sign of its subjunctive being the dropping of the nūn; the nūn is the nūn of protection (al-wiqāya); the wāw is the fāʿil; and the omitted first-person yāʾ is in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:99-99.t: ﴿حتى إذا جاء أحدهم الموت قال رب ارجعون﴾: (حتى) is a particle of inception (ḥarf ibtidāʾ); (إذا) is an adverb of future time attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قال﴾; the clause ﴿جاء﴾ is in the position of the genitive as the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (أحدهم) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed first, and (الموت) is a fāʿil (agent) placed after; the clause ﴿قال﴾ has no grammatical position; (رب) is the one addressed in the vocative, annexed to the first-person yāʾ, which is omitted; ﴿ارجعون﴾ is a verb of supplication (fiʿl duʿāʾ), indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; the nūn is the nūn of protection (al-wiqāya); and the yāʾ, omitted following the script of the Muṣḥaf, is the direct object.

muyesser-irab:100-100.t:
﴿لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت﴾: (لعل) is an abrogating particle (of inna and its sisters), and the yāʾ is its noun; the clause ﴿أعمل﴾ is its khabar (predicate); (صالحا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿أعمل﴾, or it stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is an adjective of the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e.: he does a righteous deed (عمل عملًا صالحًا). ﴿فيما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of ﴿صالحا﴾, or attached to ﴿أعمل﴾; and the clause (تركت) is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾ and has no grammatical position.
﴿كلا إنها كلمة هو قائلها﴾: (كلا) is a particle of deterrence and rebuke; (إن) is an abrogating particle, and ﴿ها﴾ is its noun; ﴿كلمة﴾ is its khabar; ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (قائلها) is the khabar; and the nominal clause is an adjective (naʿt) of ﴿كلمة﴾.
﴿ومن ورائهم برزخ إلى يوم يبعثون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, or a wāw of ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿من ورائهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar placed first; (برزخ) is the mubtadaʾ; ﴿إلى يوم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of (برزخ); and the clause (يبعثون) is in the position of the genitive as the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:101-101.t: ﴿فإذا نفخ في الصور فلا أنساب بينهم يومئذ ولا يتساءلون﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; (إذا) is an adverb of time for the future; the clause (نفخ) is in the position of the genitive as the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿في الصور﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نفخ﴾; the fāʾ links the answer of (إذا); (لا) is the lā of generic negation; ﴿أنساب﴾ is its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; ﴿بينهم﴾ is an adverb attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of (لا); ﴿يومئذ﴾: (يوم) is an adverb of time attached to the omitted khabar to which ﴿بينهم﴾ is attached, and (إذٍ) is a noun, indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) sukūn because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being: on the day when the Trumpet is blown (يوم إذ ينفخ في الصور). ﴿ولا يتساءلون﴾ is conjoined to what preceded, and (يتساءلون) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent).

muyesser-irab:102-102.t:
﴿فمن ثقلت موازينه﴾: the fāʾ is for branching off (al-tafrīʿ), and the clause is conjoined, or resumptive with no grammatical position; the conditional ﴿من﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (ثقلت) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (موازينه) is the fāʿil (agent); and the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate).
﴿فأولئك هم المفلحون﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis; (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ; ﴿هم﴾ is a second mubtadaʾ; (المفلحون) is the khabar of ﴿هم﴾, and the clause is the khabar of (أولئك); or ﴿هم﴾ is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) and (المفلحون) is the khabar of (أولئك); and the clause ﴿أولئك ...﴾ is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

muyesser-irab:103-103.t:
﴿ومن خفت موازينه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿من﴾ is a conditional mubtadaʾ (subject); (خفت) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (موازينه) is the fāʿil (agent); and the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate).
﴿فأولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم في جهنم خالدون﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis; (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ; (الذين) is the khabar; ﴿خسروا أنفسهم﴾ is a verb, its agent and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (خسروا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين) and has no grammatical position; ﴿في جهنم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خالدون﴾; and (خالدون) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or a khabar after a khabar of (أولئك).

muyesser-irab:104-104.t:
﴿تلفح وجوههم النار﴾: ﴿تلفح﴾ is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ); ﴿وجوههم﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿النار﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in ﴿خالدون﴾.
﴿وهم فيها كالحون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, or a wāw of ḥāl; ﴿هم﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿فيها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كالحون﴾, or to an omitted ḥāl of ﴿هم﴾; and (كالحون) is the khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:105-105.t:
﴿ألم تكن آياتي تتلى عليكم﴾: the hamza is interrogative; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion (to past meaning) and jussive; (تكن) is a defective imperfect verb (of kāna and its sisters) in the jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾; (آياتي) is its noun; the clause (تتلى) is its khabar (predicate); and ﴿عليكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تتلى﴾.
﴿فكنتم بها تكذبون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; (كان) is a defective past verb, and the tāʾ is its noun; ﴿بها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تكذبون﴾; and the clause (تكذبون) is the khabar of (كنتم).

muyesser-irab:106-106.t:
﴿قالوا ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا﴾: (قالوا) is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is attached to the wāw, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿ربنا﴾ is the one addressed in the vocative, annexed (muḍāf); (غلبت) is a past verb, and the tāʾ is for the feminine; ﴿علينا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿غلبت﴾; and (شقوتنا) is the fāʿil of (غلبت).
﴿وكنا قوما ضالين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (كان) is a defective past verb (of kāna and its sisters), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; ﴿قومًا﴾ is its khabar (predicate); and ﴿ضالين﴾ is an adjective (naʿt).

muyesser-irab:107-107.t: ﴿ربنا أخرجنا منها فإن عدنا فإنا ظالمون﴾: ﴿ربنا﴾ is the one addressed in the vocative, annexed (muḍāf); (أخرجنا) is a verb of supplication (fiʿl duʿāʾ); ﴿منها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أخرج﴾; the fāʾ is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (عدنا) is a past verb in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the pronoun is the fāʿil (agent); the fāʾ links the apodosis because it is a nominal clause; (إن) is an abrogating particle (of inna and its sisters), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; (ظالمون) is its khabar (predicate); and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

muyesser-irab:108-108.t:
﴿قال اخسئوا فيها﴾: the clause (اخسئوا) is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); (اخسئوا) is an imperative verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (فيها) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اخسئوا﴾.
﴿ولا تكلمون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is the lā of prohibition; (تكلمون) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by (لا); the nūn is the nūn of protection (al-wiqāya); and the omitted yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:109-109.t:
﴿إنه كان فريق من عبادي يقولون ربنا آمنا﴾: a causal (taʿlīliyya) clause; (إن) is an abrogating particle (of inna and its sisters), and the hāʾ is its noun; the clause (كان) is its khabar (predicate); (فريق) is the noun of (كان); ﴿من عبادي﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of (فريق); the clause (يقولون) is the khabar of (كان); (ربنا) is the one addressed in the vocative, annexed (muḍāf); and the clause (آمنا) is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿فاغفر لنا وارحمنا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; (اغفر) is a verb of supplication (fiʿl duʿāʾ), and (ارحمنا) is conjoined to it.
﴿وأنت خير الراحمين﴾: the wāw is resumptive. (أنت) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (خير) is the khabar; (الراحمين) is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:110-110.t:
﴿فاتخذتموهم سخريا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; (اتخذتموهم) is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural, and the wāw is for lengthening the ḍamma of the mīm; and (سخريًّا) is the second object.
﴿حتى أنسوكم ذكري وكنتم منهم تضحكون﴾: (حتى) is a particle of limit and of the genitive; (أنسوكم) is a past verb, its agent and its first object; (ذكري) is the second object; ﴿كنتم﴾: (كان) is a defective past verb (of kāna and its sisters), and the tāʾ is its noun; (منهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تضحكون﴾; and the clause (تضحكون) is the khabar (predicate) of (كان).

muyesser-irab:111-111.t: ﴿إني جزيتهم اليوم بما صبروا أنهم هم الفائزون﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position; (إن) is an abrogating particle (of inna and its sisters), and the yāʾ is its noun; the clause (جزيتهم) is the khabar (predicate) of (إن); (جزيتهم) is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (اليوم) is an adverb of ﴿جزيتهم﴾; (بما) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جزيتهم﴾, the bāʾ being causal, i.e.: because of their patience; (ما) is maṣdar-forming; (أن) and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), the second object of (جزيتهم), i.e.: I have rewarded them with their triumph; (أن) is an abrogating particle, and ﴿هم﴾ is its noun; (هم) is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); and (الفائزون) is the khabar of (أن). [Translator's note: the noun of (أنّ) is the attached pronoun (ـهم) in (أنهم); the detached (هم) after it is the separating pronoun.]

muyesser-irab:112-112.t: ﴿قال كم لبثتم في الأرض عدد سنين﴾: (كم) is interrogative, in the position of the accusative as an adverb of time, and it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿لبث﴾; (في الأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿لبث﴾; (عدد) is the tamyīz (specification) of (كم); (سنين) is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause (كم لبثتم) is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

muyesser-irab:113-113.t:
﴿قالوا لبثنا يوما أو بعض يوم﴾: the clause (لبثنا) is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿يومًا﴾ is an adverb, a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿لبث﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; (يومًا) is an accusative adverb of time (mafʿūl fīhi), not a prepositional phrase — the words "a preposition and its genitive noun" appear to be a slip]; (أو) is a conjunction; and (بعض يوم) is conjoined to ﴿يومًا﴾.
﴿فاسأل العادين﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the "disclosing" fāʾ); (اسأل) is a verb of supplication (fiʿl duʿāʾ), with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), its implied form being "you" (أنت); and (العادين) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:114-114.t: ﴿قال إن لبثتم إلا قليلا لو أنكم كنتم تعلمون﴾: (قال) is a past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), referring to Allah, glorified is He; (إن) is negative; (لبثتم) is a verb and its agent; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (قليلا) is an adjective of an omitted adverb, i.e.: a little time (زمنا قليلا), or (قليلا) is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e.: a little staying (لبثا قليلا); (لو) is a particle of impossibility due to impossibility. ﴿أنكم﴾: (أن) is an abrogating particle (of inna and its sisters), and the kāf is its noun; the clause (كنتم) is its khabar (predicate); the clause (تعلمون) is the khabar of (كنتم); and the object of (تعلمون) is omitted, i.e.: the length of your stay (مقدار لبثتكم).

muyesser-irab:115-115.t:
﴿أفحسبتم أنما خلقناكم عبثا﴾: the hamza is interrogative, and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position; (حسبتم) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (أنما) is a restraining particle and the one it restrains (kāffa wa-makfūfa), and it, together with what follows it, is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that stands in place of the two objects of (حسبتم); (خلقناكم) is a verb, its agent and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (عبثا) is accusative (manṣūb) as a maṣdar standing in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: acting in vain (عابثين), or as an absolute object (maṣdariyya), or as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e.: for the sake of vanity.
﴿وأنكم إلينا لا ترجعون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (أن) is an abrogating particle (of inna and its sisters), and the kāf is its noun; (إلينا) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ترجعون﴾; (لا) is negative; (ترجعون) is an imperfect verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and the clause (ترجعون) is the khabar (predicate) of (أن).

muyesser-irab:116-116.t:
﴿فتعالى الله الملك الحق﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; (تعالى) is a past verb; the Name of Majesty is the fāʿil (agent); and (الملك الحق) are two adjectives (naʿt) of it.
﴿لا﴾: the lā of generic negation.
