This is indicated by what Abū Ḥāzim related from Abū Hurayra from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Allah is good and accepts only what is good, and Allah has commanded the prophets with what He commanded the believers." He said: (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُلُوا مِنْ طَيِّباتِ ما رَزَقْناكُمْ) [al-Baqara: 172], and He said: «يا أيّها الرّسل كلوا من الطّيّبات».

nahhas-irab:52-52.t:
(وَإِنَّ هذِهِ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً): there are three readings on this. The Medinans and Abū ʿAmr read «وَأَنَّ هذه أمّتكم أمّةً واحدةً» with fatḥa on the hamza and «أمّةً واحدةً» in the accusative; the Kufans read with kasra on the hamza and «أمّةً واحدةً» in the accusative as well; and al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «وإنّ هذه أمّتُكم أمّةٌ واحدةٌ» with everything in the nominative. «[Translator's note: the printed text vowels all three like the standard reading; they are given here as the descriptions specify.]» On the fatḥa of the hamza there are three views. The view of the Basrans is that the meaning is:
«ولأنّ», with the lām omitted, and «أنّ» is in the position of accusative. The view of al-Kisāʾī, which is one of al-Farrāʾ's two views, is that «أنّ» is in the position of genitive, coordinated with «ما تعملون», that is: "I am Knowing of what you do, and of [the fact] that this is your community". The third view is that of al-Farrāʾ: it is in the position of accusative by an implied verb, the implied form being:
«واعلموا أنّ هذه أمّتكم» (and know that this is your community). The kasra of the hamza is, according to him, resumptive, and according to al-Kisāʾī it is coordinated with «إنّي بما تعملون عليم». (أُمَّةً واحِدَةً) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The nominative is on three bases:
by an implied mubtadaʾ, as a badal (substitute), and as a khabar after a khabar.

nahhas-irab:53-53.t: (فَتَقَطَّعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ زُبُراً): [«زبراً»] is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the meaning is "like zubur (separate writings)". (كُلُّ حِزْبٍ بِما لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ), that is, every party thinks it is on the truth, so it rejoices in what it holds; and it is incumbent on it to make the truth clear, because it is evident. It has also been said: «كلّ حزب بما لديهم فرحون», that is, in the pleasures and pursuit of leadership they are in.

nahhas-irab:54-54.t: (فَذَرْهُمْ فِي غَمْرَتِهِمْ), that is, in what has covered them of love of this world and heedlessness of death and of the affair of the Hereafter. It has been said: «في غمرتهم», that is, in the ignorance that has overwhelmed them. Abū Isḥāq said: (حَتَّى حِينٍ): until the time when what they were promised of punishment comes to them.

nahhas-irab:55-56.t:
(أَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّما نُمِدُّهُمْ بِهِ): «ما» is in the sense of «الذي». On the khabar (predicate) of «أنّ» there are three views. One is that it is omitted. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is «نسارع لهم به», and «به» was omitted. Hishām stated a subtle view; he said: «ما» is the good things, and there is no omission in the speech, because the meaning of «في الخيرات» is «فيه». This is a far-fetched view; its like is «إنّ زيداً تكلّم عمروٌ في زيد», whereas the better is «تكلّم عمروٌ فيه». Sībawayh allowed the like of it, and recited: [al-Khafīf] 305-
لا أرى الموت يسبق الموت شيء ... نغّص الموت ذا الغنى والفقيرا
(I do not see death — does anything outstrip death? Death has spoiled life for the rich man and the poor alike.)
Whoever reads «يُسارِعُ لهم في الخيرات» has three analyses for his reading: one is with «به» omitted; the implied form may be «يُسارِعُ الإمدادُ» (the provision hastens); and «لهم» may be the noun of the verb whose agent is not named (the nāʾib fāʿil).

nahhas-irab:57-57.t: The khabar (predicate) of «إنّ». «[Translator's note: the entry consists only of these words in the source; the predicate of (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ هُمْ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ رَبِّهِمْ مُشْفِقُونَ) is (أُولئِكَ يُسارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْراتِ) in verse 61.]»

nahhas-irab:61-61.t:
(أُولئِكَ يُسارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْراتِ), that is, in doing good works, that is, acts of obedience. Abū Isḥāq said:
«يسارعون» is more emphatic than «يسرعون». (وَهُمْ لَها سابِقُونَ): the best that has been said about it is that they race to their [appointed] times; and it indicates that prayer at the beginning of its time is better. Everyone who goes ahead in something has raced to it, and everyone who lags behind it has been outstripped by it and has missed it.

nahhas-irab:62-62.t: (وَلَدَيْنا كِتابٌ يَنْطِقُ بِالْحَقِّ): it has been said: He means by it the book in which the deeds of creatures are written, kept preserved with the angels.

nahhas-irab:63-63.t: (بَلْ قُلُوبُهُمْ فِي غَمْرَةٍ مِنْ هذا وَلَهُمْ أَعْمالٌ مِنْ دُونِ ذلِكَ هُمْ لَها عامِلُونَ) (63): (بَلْ قُلُوبُهُمْ فِي غَمْرَةٍ مِنْ هذا): Abū Isḥāq said: that is, rather their hearts are in blindness concerning this. It has also been said: rather their hearts are in heedlessness concerning this Book, which speaks with the truth and in which their deeds are counted.

nahhas-irab:67-67.t:
This is a good reading «[Translator's note: the reading meant is not named in the printed text; from the context it is «تُهْجِرُونَ» (you talk obscenely/rave), as against the standard (تَهْجُرُونَ).]», matching the beginning of the story, because in the story there is mention of their turning back on their heels; so this resembles [the sense] that they abandoned the Prophet ﷺ and the Book. Al-Kisāʾī said: (تَهْجُرُونَ) means "you rave" (تهذون). Abū Jaʿfar said: one says «هَجَرَ المحمومُ» when the fevered person is overcome in his mind and raves. So the meaning of the verse — and Allah knows best — would be: you speak about the Prophet ﷺ with what does not harm him and what is not in him, so you are like someone raving.
And one says «ما زال ذاك إهجيراه وهجيراه», that is, his habit, as if he raves about it until it has become a habit for him.

nahhas-irab:69-69.t: (أَمْ لَمْ يَعْرِفُوا): the Arabs use this in the sense of making [someone] acknowledge [something] and of reproach; they say: "Is good dearer to you, or evil?", that is, you have chosen evil.

nahhas-irab:71-71.t: The people of tafsīr, Mujāhid, Abū Ṣāliḥ and others, say: «الحقّ» here is Allah, Majestic and Mighty. Its implied form in Arabic is «ولو اتّبع صاحبُ الحقّ» (were the Possessor of the Truth to follow). It has also been said: it is figurative (majāz), that is, were the truth to agree with their desires; so He made its agreeing a "following", figuratively; that is, if they disbelieved in the messengers and disobeyed Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and then were not punished or requited for that, whether out of incapacity or out of ignorance, the heavens and the earth would be corrupted. It has also been said: the meaning is, were the truth to lie in what they say about taking gods besides Allah, the gods would vie with one another and some of them would will what others do not will, so the governance would be thrown into disorder and the heavens and the earth would be corrupted; and when the two are corrupted, those in them are corrupted.

nahhas-irab:72-72.t:
Al-Akhfash said: «الخَرْج» [and «الخَراج»] are one, but varying the wording is better. Abū Ḥātim said:
«الخرج» is the fee and «الخراج» is the gift. And the view of Muḥammad ibn Yazīd: «الخرج» is the maṣdar (verbal noun) and «الخراج» is the noun. The meaning is: or do you ask them for provision? For the provision of your Lord is better, and He is the best of providers, that is, no one provides as He provides, nor bestows blessing as He bestows it.

nahhas-irab:73-73.t: That is, to an upright religion. «الصراط» in the language is the road; the religion was called a road because it leads to Paradise, that is, it is a road to it.

nahhas-irab:74-74.t: It has been said: [this] is like the first, that is, [they deviate] from the religion; and it has been said: they deviate from the road to Paradise, until they end up in the Fire.

nahhas-irab:75-75.t: (وَلَوْ رَحِمْناهُمْ وَكَشَفْنا ما بِهِمْ مِنْ ضُرٍّ), that is, if We returned them to this world, did not put them into the Fire, and tested them, (لَلَجُّوا فِي طُغْيانِهِمْ): al-Suddī said: that is, in their disobedience. (يَعْمَهُونَ): al-Akhfash said: they waver.

nahhas-irab:76-76.t: (وَلَقَدْ أَخَذْناهُمْ بِالْعَذابِ): al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, with hunger.

nahhas-irab:77-77.t:
(حَتَّى إِذا فَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ باباً ذا عَذابٍ شَدِيدٍ): ʿIkrima said: it is one of the gates of Hell, over which are four hundred thousand of the keepers, their faces black, their fangs like kites, mercy plucked out of their hearts; when they reach it, Allah opens it upon them.
«قل ... لله» and «قل ... الله» «[Translator's note: thus abbreviated in the printed text, referring to the phrases (سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ قُلْ …) in verses 85–89.]»: we have already discussed them in a way that needs nothing more.

nahhas-irab:91-92.t: «عالِمُ الغيب» «[Translator's note: the printed text vowels it as the genitive (عالِمِ الْغَيْبِ) here; the description shows the nominative is meant.]» is the reading of the people of Medina and the people of Kufa, by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject); the reading of Abū ʿAmr is (عالِمِ الْغَيْبِ) in the genitive, as a naʿt (adjective) of Allah, Majestic and Mighty. Most of the grammarians, Kufan and Basran, hold that the nominative is preferable. The argument of the Basrans is that before it is the end of a verse and the speech is complete, so beginning anew is better. The argument of the Kufans, among them al-Farrāʾ, that the nominative is preferable: he said: because had it been genitive, it would have been with the wāw, so it would be «عالمِ الغيب وتعالى»; since it is «فتعالى», the nominative is preferable.

nahhas-irab:93-94.t:
Abū Isḥāq said: «ربُّ» with ḍamma on the bāʾ is permissible, and «ربّي» with the yāʾ given sukūn or fatḥa is permissible.
«إنْ» here is for the condition and «ما» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis; since «ما» was added, the entry of the nūn of emphasis became good. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is (فَلا تَجْعَلْنِي فِي الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ), that is, if You intend a punishment for them, take me out from among them.

nahhas-irab:96-96.t: (ادْفَعْ بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ): al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said: By Allah, no one attains it until he swallows his anger and endures what is disliked.

nahhas-irab:97-97.t: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said — and some trace it back [to the Prophet ﷺ] — : its «همز» is «الموتة»; and «الموتة» is a kind of madness. «همزة», though it has a vowelless [middle letter], is pluralized as «همزات» [with a vowel], to distinguish between the noun and the adjective.

nahhas-irab:99-99.t: Speech may be within the soul; He, Majestic and Mighty, said: (وَيَقُولُونَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ لَوْلا يُعَذِّبُنَا اللَّهُ) [al-Mujādila: 8]. As for His saying (ارْجِعُونِ), while he is addressing his Lord, Majestic and Mighty, and he did not say «ارجعني», the grammarians have two views on it. One of them is that the Arabs commonly recognize that a mighty one, when speaking of himself, says «لنفعلنّ» and «لنرجعنّ» (We shall surely do, We shall surely return), and when he is addressed, the address to him is the address to a group, so it is said to him «برّونا» and «أرجعونا»; and this verse came in this manner. The other view is that the meaning of «ارجعون» is by way of repetition: «ارجعنِ ارجعنِ ارجعنِ» (return me, return me, return me). Al-Māzinī said likewise about His saying, Majestic and Mighty, (أَلْقِيا فِي جَهَنَّمَ) [Qāf: 24]: he said: its meaning is «ألقِ ألقِ» (throw, throw).

nahhas-irab:100-100.t: (وَمِنْ وَرائِهِمْ بَرْزَخٌ): «البرزخ» in the language is every barrier between two things; so the barzakh is between this world and the Hereafter. As is related, a man said in the presence of al-Shaʿbī: "May Allah have mercy on so-and-so; he has become one of the people of the Hereafter." He said: "He has not become one of the people of the Hereafter, but he has become one of the people of the barzakh; he is neither of this world nor of the Hereafter." You annexed «يوم» to «يبعثون» because it is an adverb of time, and what is meant by the annexation is the maṣdar (verbal noun). Abū Isḥāq said: its reality is that of quotation (ḥikāya).

nahhas-irab:101-101.t: There are two views on its meaning. One of them is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās: that they are at a time when they do not question one another; and «يوم» in the language means a known time. The other view is clearer than this: the meaning of (فَلا أَنْسابَ بَيْنَهُمْ) is that they do not boast of lineages on the Day of Resurrection, nor ask one another about them, as they used to do in this world.

nahhas-irab:104-104.t: (تَلْفَحُ وُجُوهَهُمُ النَّارُ): one also says «تنفح» in [a similar] sense, except that «تلفح» is more severe. (وَهُمْ فِيها كالِحُونَ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); outside the Qurʾān the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) would be permissible. «الكالح» in the speech of the Arabs is the one whose lips have drawn back and whose teeth show, as you see with the heads of [roasted] sheep. A transmitted text from the Prophet ﷺ has come with this meaning; he said: "The Fire burns one of them, so his upper lip contracts until it reaches the middle of his head, and his lower lip hangs down until it reaches his navel."

nahhas-irab:106-107.t: (قالُوا رَبَّنا غَلَبَتْ عَلَيْنا شِقْوَتُنا) is the reading of the people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim; the Kufans except ʿĀṣim read «شَقاوتُنا», and this reading is related from Ibn Masʿūd and al-Ḥasan. One also says «شَقاً» and «شَقاء», with the short and the long [final alif]. The best of what has been said about its meaning: "... and the desires" are [called] wretchedness «[Translator's note: some words appear to have dropped out of the printed text here; the sense is presumably that their pleasures and desires overcame them and are called «شقوة» (wretchedness).]», because they lead to it, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوالَ الْيَتامى ظُلْماً إِنَّما يَأْكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ ناراً) [al-Nisāʾ: 10], because that leads them to the Fire. (وَكُنَّا قَوْماً ضالِّينَ), that is, in our actions we were astray from guidance. This is not an excuse from them; it is only a confession, and this is indicated by (رَبَّنا أَخْرِجْنا مِنْها فَإِنْ عُدْنا فَإِنَّا ظالِمُونَ).

nahhas-irab:108-108.t: (قالَ اخْسَؤُا فِيها): the maṣdar (verbal noun) is «خَسْء», in both the intransitive and the transitive, on the pattern «فَعْل».

nahhas-irab:109-109.t: (إِنَّهُ كانَ فَرِيقٌ مِنْ عِبادِي يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنا آمَنَّا): Mujāhid said: they are Bilāl, Khabbāb, Ṣuhayb, and so-and-so and so-and-so of the weak among the Muslims; Abū Jahl and his companions used to mock them.

nahhas-irab:110-110.t: (فَاتَّخَذْتُمُوهُمْ سِخْرِيًّا), with kasra and with ḍamma. Abū ʿAmr distinguished between them, making the one with kasra from the sense of mockery and the one with ḍamma from the sense of forced labour. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, may Allah have mercy on them both, do not know this distinction, nor do al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ. Al-Kisāʾī said: they are two dialectal forms with one meaning, as one says «عُصِيّ» and «عِصِيّ» (sticks). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: distinctions between meanings are taken only from the Arabs; as for [mere] interpretation, it does not count. The kasra in «سخريّ» in both meanings, and in «عصيّ», is more common, because the ḍamma is felt to be heavy in such a case.

nahhas-irab:112-112.t: (قالَ كَمْ لَبِثْتُمْ) and «قُلْ كم لبثتم» are two different meanings; it may not be said that one of them is better than the other. (عَدَدَ سِنِينَ), with fatḥa on the nūn, on the basis that it is a sound plural; and some of the Arabs put it in the genitive and give it tanwīn.

nahhas-irab:113-113.t: (قالُوا لَبِثْنا يَوْماً أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ): there is nothing in this that denies the punishment of the grave, because there must be a dormancy before the Resurrection.

nahhas-irab:116-116.t: (رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْكَرِيمِ): «كمن نعت العرش» «[Translator's note: thus in the printed text, which appears corrupt; the sense is presumably that «الكريم» is a naʿt (adjective) of «العرش»,]» because of its elevation and because hands cannot reach it.

nahhas-irab:118-118.t:
(وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الرَّاحِمِينَ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). The noun [in «أنت»], according to the Basrans, is «أن», and the tāʾ is for address.
The argument for Abū ʿAmr in his distinction between «سِخريّ» and «سُخريّ» is that he was reporting his own position in reading, nothing more. As for «لبتّم» with assimilation, it is because of the closeness of the tāʾ to the thāʾ; and likewise «فاتّختّموهم» is assimilated because of the closeness of the dhāl to the tāʾ. Whoever does not assimilate in either does so because the tāʾ is a noun [pronoun], so it is as if separate, and the two points of articulation are different. Mujāhid said: (الْعادِّينَ) are the angels, because they count that. Al-Aʿmash read «عدداً سنين», and «عدداً» is accusative as clarification (bayān) in both readings; «كم» is in the position of accusative by «لبثتم».

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلرُّسُلُ كُلُواْ مِنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَاتِ وَٱعْمَلُواْ صَالِحاً﴾.
 Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: This is an address to the Prophet ﷺ, and the plural indicates that all the messengers were commanded likewise, that is: eat of what is lawful.

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّ هَـٰذِهِ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾.
 The meaning is "and because" (ولأنَّ), that is: and because your religion is one religion, namely Islam, so fear Me.

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
Then He reported that a people split up their religions, and said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَتَقَطَّعُوۤاْ أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ زُبُراً﴾.
 Qatāda said: That is, books.
 Al-Farrāʾ said: That is, they became Jews and Christians.
 Al-Aʿmash read it: ﴿فتقطَّعُوا أمرَهُمْ بينَهُمْ زُبَرَاً﴾, which is the plural of "زُبَرَة", that is: pieces and factions.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كُلُّ حِزْبٍ بِمَا لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ﴾.
That is, pleased with themselves (admiring).

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿فَذَرْهُمْ فِي غَمْرَتِهِمْ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍٍ﴾.
 Qatāda said: ﴿فِي غَمْرتِهِمْ﴾ means: in their ignorance.
﴿حَتَّىٰ حِينٍٍ﴾: Mujāhid said: until death.

nahhas-meani:55-56.t:
Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿أَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّمَا نُمِدُّهُمْ بِهِ مِن مَّالٍ وَبَنِينَ. نُسَارِعُ لَهُمْ فِي ٱلْخَيْرَاتِ﴾ [verses 55, 56].
The khabar (predicate) is omitted, and the meaning is: "We hasten for them with it (نسارع لهم به)"; this is the view of Abū Isḥāq.
Hishām al-Ḍarīr has a view on it, namely that "ما" is the good things (الخيرات), so the meaning becomes: "We hasten for them in it", without any omission: ﴿أَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّ مَا نُمِدُّهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ مَالٍ وَبَنِينَ﴾ is a recompense for them and a good.
 ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakra read ﴿يُسَارِعُ لَهُمْ فِي الخَيْراتِ﴾ with yāʾ and kasra on the rāʾ.
 This may be without any omission, that is: the provision (الإِمداد) hastens for them.
 And it may contain an omission, the meaning being: Allah hastens for them with it in good things.

nahhas-meani:57-60.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ هُم مِّنْ خَشْيةِ رَبِّهِمْ مُّشْفِقُونََ﴾ up to His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْتُونَ مَآ آتَواْ وَّقُلُوبُهُمْ وَجِلَةٌ﴾ [verses 57-60].
 ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿīd al-Hamadānī related from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْتُونَ مَآ آتَواْ وَّقُلُوبُهُمْ وَجِلَةٌ﴾: is it the man who commits adultery, or steals, or drinks wine? He said: No, O daughter of al-Ṣiddīq; rather it is the man who prays, fasts and gives charity, and fears that it will not be accepted from him."
 Ibn Mujāhid related from his father from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْتُونَ مَآ آتَواْ﴾: he said: they give what they give.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: This is how it has been related, and that is indeed the meaning of ﴿يُؤْتون﴾: they give; but what is well known as the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās is ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يَأْتُونَ مَا أَتَوْا﴾, and it is the reading related from the Prophet ﷺ and from ʿĀʾisha.
 Its meaning is: they do what they do, as was related in the ḥadīth.
 And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَنَّهُمْ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ رَاجِعُونَ﴾.
 Al-Farrāʾ said: The meaning is: "of [the fact] that they" (من أنهم).
 And Abū Ḥātim said: The meaning is: "because they (لأنهم) are returning to their Lord."

nahhas-meani:61-61.t:
Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ يُسَارِعُونَ فِي ٱلْخَيْرَاتِِ﴾.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: سَارَع and أَسْرَع have one and the same meaning.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهُمْ لَهَا سَابِقُونَ﴾.
 There are three views on it:
1- The meaning is: "and they are foremost towards it (إليها)", just as He said ﴿بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ أَوْحَى لَهَا﴾, that is, He inspired to it (إليها); and Sībawayh cited:
تَجَانَفُ عن جَوِّ اليمَامَةِ نَاقَتِي * وَمَا قَصَدتْ من أَهْلِها لِسَوَائِكا.
(My she-camel veers away from the plain of al-Yamāma, and she did not head, of its people, for anyone but you.)
2- It was also said: the meaning of ﴿وَهُمْ لَهَا﴾ is: for its sake, that is, for the sake of earning it, as you say: "I honour so-and-so for you (لك)", that is, for your sake.
3- It was also said: when He said ﴿وَهُمْ لَهَا سَابِقُونَ﴾ it indicated the act of preceding, as if He had said: their preceding to it.

nahhas-meani:63-63.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلْ قُلُوبُهُمْ فِي غَمْرَةٍ مِّنْ هَـٰذَا﴾.
That is, in heedlessness and a covering, bewildered.
 One says: غَمَره الماءُ when the water covers him; and a غَمْر river is one that covers whoever enters it; and a غُمْر man is one whom people's opinions overwhelm (تَغْمُره).
It was also said: غُمْرة, because it covers the face; and from it: "he entered into the غُمار of the people".
- in the view of whoever held it — its meaning is: into what covers him of the crowd.
 And His saying ﴿مِنْ هَذَا﴾: there are two views on it:
1- The first: Mujāhid said: rather, their hearts are in blindness concerning the Qurʾān.
So according to Mujāhid's view ﴿هَذَا﴾ points to the Qurʾān.
 And Qatāda said: He described the people of righteousness, saying ﴿وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ رَبِّهِمْ مُشْفِقُونَ﴾, "and those who…", "and those who…".
 Then He described the people of disbelief, saying ﴿بَلْ قُلُوبُهُمْ فِي غَمْرَةٍ مِّنْ هَـٰذَا﴾.
So the meaning according to Qatāda's view is: from this righteousness.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَلَهُمْ أَعْمَالٌ مِّن دُونِ ذٰلِكَ هُمْ لَهَا عَامِلُونَ﴾.
 There are two views on it:
 The first: al-Ḥasan said: and they have evil deeds which they have not yet done and will do.
 Mujāhid said: That is, they have sins which they must inevitably commit.
b- And Qatāda said: He returned to the people of righteousness, saying ﴿وَلَهُمْ أَعْمَالٌ مِّن دُونِ ذٰلِكَ﴾; he said: that is, other than what He has enumerated.

nahhas-meani:64-64.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَآ أَخَذْنَا مُتْرَفِيهِمْ بِٱلْعَذَابِ إِذَا هُمْ يَجْأَرُونَ﴾.
 Qatāda said: That is, they cry out in distress.
 And the lexicographers report: جَأَر، يَجْأَرُ when one raises one's voice.
 Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: The punishment with which they were seized was the sword.
 Mujāhid said: On the day of Badr.

nahhas-meani:66-66.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَدْ كَانَتْ آيَاتِي تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْْ﴾.
 Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Before you were punished by being killed.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿فَكُنتُمْ عَلَىٰ أَعْقَابِكُمْ تَنكِصُونَ﴾.
 Mujāhid said: You draw back.

nahhas-meani:67-67.t:
Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿مُسْتَكْبِرِينَ بِهِ﴾.
 Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Ḥasan and Abū Mālik said: Being arrogant on account of the Sanctuary (الحَرَم).
 Abū Mālik said: Because of their security, while people were being snatched away all around them.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: It was also said: being arrogant towards the Qurʾān, that is, arrogance seizes them when it is recited.
The first view is more fitting.
 The meaning is: they boast of the Sanctuary, saying: "We are the people of Allah's Sanctuary, Mighty and Majestic is He."
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿سَامِراً تَهْجُرُونَ﴾.
 Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad] said: A group who gather to converse is called سَامِر and سُمَّار; سَامِر is like saying بَاقِر for a herd of cattle (البَقَر) and جَامِل for a herd of camels (الجِمَال).
That is, they gather for night conversation (السَّمَر); and سَامِر is mostly used for those who converse at night.
 Abū al-ʿAbbās said: The origin of this is their saying: "I will not speak to him as long as there are السَّمَر and القَمَر", that is, night and day.
 And al-Thawrī said: The shadow of the moon is called السَّمَر.
 Abū Isḥāq said: From it comes السُّمْرة (brownness) in colour; and it is also called الفَخْت, from which comes فاخته.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: Regarding His saying ﴿تَهْجُرُوْنَ﴾ there are two views:
1- Al-Ḥasan said: You abandon My Prophet and My Book.
2- And others said: ﴿تَهْجُرُوْنَ﴾ means you rave; one says هَجَر المريضُ، يَهْجُرُ، هُجْراً when the sick person raves.
 Ibn ʿAbbās read ﴿تُهْجِروْنَ﴾ with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the jīm.
 And he said: They held night conversations about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and spoke obscenity (الهُجْر).
 And ʿIkrima said: ﴿تُهْجِروْنَ﴾ means you associate partners [with Allah].
 And al-Ḥasan said: You revile the Prophet ﷺ.
 And Mujāhid said: You say evil things about the Qurʾān.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are close to one another; one says أَهْجَر، يُهْجِر when someone utters obscenity and speaks foully, and the noun from it is الهُجْر; its meaning is that he overstepped bounds; and from it was said الهَاجِرة (the midday heat), which is simply the sun's passing over from east to west.
 And Abū Rajāʾ read "سُمَّارا", which is the plural of سَامِر, as the poet said:
فقالتْ سَبَاكَ اللَّهُ إنكَ فَاضِحي * أَلَسْتَ تَرَى السُّمَّارَ والنَّاسَ أَحوالي
(She said: May Allah carry you off, you will disgrace me! Do you not see the night-talkers and the people around me?)

nahhas-meani:68-68.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَدَّبَّرُواْ ٱلْقَوْلَ﴾.
That is, the Qurʾān.

nahhas-meani:71-71.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلْحَقُّ أَهْوَآءَهُمْْ﴾.
 Sufyān related from Ismāʿīl from Abū Ṣāliḥ regarding ﴿وَلَوِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلْحَقُّ﴾: he said: [The Truth is] Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
 It was also said: The meaning is: rather He brought them the Qurʾān; and if the Qurʾān had followed their desires, that is, if it had come down with what they love, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿بَلْ أَتَيْنَاهُمْ بِذِكْرِهِمْ فَهُمْ عَن ذِكْرِهِمْ مُّعْرِضُونَ﴾.
 Maʿmar related from Qatāda: ﴿بِذِكْرِهِمْ﴾: he said: with the Qurʾān.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning according to his view is: rather We brought them that in which there is for them mention of what would earn them Paradise if they followed it.
 It was also said: الذِّكْر here means honour.

nahhas-meani:72-72.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْ تَسْأَلُهُمْ خَرْجاً فَخَرَاجُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌٌ﴾.
 Al-Ḥasan said: "خَرْجا" means a wage.
 Abū Ḥātim said: الخَرَاج is a payment for a service (الجُعْل), and الخَرَاج is a gift, if Allah wills, or something like that.

nahhas-meani:74-74.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ عَنِ ٱلصِّرَاطِ لَنَاكِبُونَ﴾.
 ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: He says ﴿عَنِ ٱلصِّرَاطِ لَنَاكِبُونَ﴾: they are deviating from the truth.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: الصِّراط in the language is the straight road, and one says نَكَبَ عن الحَقِّ when someone deviates from it.
 The meaning is: they are indeed deviating from the right course.

nahhas-meani:76-76.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَخَذْنَاهُمْ بِٱلْعَذَابِ فَمَا ٱسْتَكَانُواْ لِرَبِّهِمْ وَمَا يَتَضَرَّعُونَ﴾.
 ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَخَذْنَاهُمْ بِٱلْعَذَابِ﴾ means: with fear, and loss of wealth and lives.
 ﴿فَمَا ٱسْتَكَانُواْ لِرَبِّهِمْ﴾ means: they did not humble themselves.

nahhas-meani:77-77.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا فَتَحْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ بَاباً ذَا عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍٍ﴾.
 It was said: He means hunger; and it was said: the sword.
 ﴿إِذَا هُمْ فِيهِ مُبْلِسُونَ﴾ means: bewildered, despairing of any good.

nahhas-meani:80-80.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَلَهُ ٱخْتِلاَفُ ٱللَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِِ﴾.
 Al-Farrāʾ said: The meaning of ﴿وَلَهُ ٱخْتِلاَفُ ٱللَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ﴾ is: He is their Creator, as you say: "To you belong the reward and the gift."

nahhas-meani:100-100.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَلاَّ إِنَّهَا كَلِمَةٌ هُوَ قَآئِلُهَا﴾.
 ﴿كَلاَّ﴾ is a word of rebuff, rebuke and alerting.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِن وَرَآئِهِمْ بَرْزَخٌ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾.
 Abū ʿUbayda said: That is, in front of them.
 Mujāhid said: البَرْزَخ is a barrier between death and returning to the world.
 Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: It is what lies between this world and the Hereafter.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: The Arabs call every barrier between two things a barzakh, as He, Glorified is He, said: ﴿بَيْنَهُما بَرْزَخٌ لاَ يَبْغِيَانِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:101-101.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ فَلاَ أَنسَابَ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَلاَ يَتَسَآءَلُونََ﴾.
 Abū ʿUbayd said: It is the plural of صُوْرة (form).
 Abū Jaʿfar said: He holds that the meaning is: when the spirits are blown into the forms of people; and this is an error according to the scholars of exegesis and of the language.
 Abū al-Zaʿrāʾ related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd regarding ﴿فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ﴾: he said: into the horn.
 And ʿAṭiyya related from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "How can I enjoy comfort when the one with the horn has put the horn to his mouth, bent his forehead and inclined his ear, waiting for when he will be commanded? The Muslims said: O Messenger of Allah, what shall we say? He said: Say: Allah is sufficient for us and an excellent Guardian is He; upon Him we rely."
 The lexicographers know no plural of "صورة" other than "صُوَر"; and if it were the plural of صورة, it would have been "ثم نُفِخَ فيها" [with a feminine pronoun], except by a far-fetched construction.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: This verse is problematic, because He said, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿فَلاَ أَنسَابَ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَلاَ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ﴾, while He said in another place ﴿وَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ﴾?!
 The answer to this — and it is the meaning of what ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said, even if it differs from some of his wording, the meaning being one — is that when the Trumpet is blown the first blast, the ties of kinship are cut, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth swoons, and people are preoccupied with themselves from one another; at that point there are no lineages between them that day, nor do they ask one another.
 Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning of ﴿يَوْمَئِذِ﴾ in His saying ﴿فَلاَ أَنسَابَ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ is as when you say "Today I am such-and-such", that is, at this time, not intending a specific time.

nahhas-meani:104-104.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَلْفَحُ وُجُوهَهُمُ ٱلنَّارُ وَهُمْ فِيهَا كَالِحُونََ﴾.
 Abū al-Aḥwaṣ related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he said: الكَالِح is one whose teeth have become exposed and whose lip has shrunk back, like a head singed by fire.

nahhas-meani:106-106.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ رَبَّنَا غَلَبَتْ عَلَيْنَا شِقْوَتُنَا﴾.
 Mujāhid said: That is, that which was written against us.

nahhas-meani:108-108.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ ٱخْسَئُواْ فِيهَا وَلاَ تُكَلِّمُونِ﴾.
One says خسأتُه when you drive him away with a harsh rebuke.

nahhas-meani:110-110.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱتَّخَذْتُمُوهُمْ سِخْرِيّاً حَتَّىٰ أَنسَوْكُمْ ذِكْرِي﴾.
 Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda and Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said — and this is the meaning of what they said —: السُّخْرِيّ with ḍamma is what pertains to forced labour (السُّخْرة), and السِّخْرِيّ with kasra is what pertains to mockery.

nahhas-meani:111-111.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنِّي جَزَيْتُهُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ بِمَا صَبَرُوۤاْ أَنَّهُمْ هُمُ ٱلْفَآئِزُونَ﴾.
That is, because they (لأنهم).
And the meaning may be: I have rewarded them with triumph.

nahhas-meani:113-113.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ لَبِثْنَا يَوْماً أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ فَسْئَلِ ٱلْعَآدِّينَ﴾.
 Mujāhid said: ﴿فَسْئَلِ ٱلْعَآدِّينَ﴾: the angels.
 And Qatāda said: That is, those who keep count.

nahhas-meani:117-117.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن يَدْعُ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَـهَا آخَرَ لاَ بُرْهَانَ لَهُ بِهِ﴾.
 Mujāhid said: That is, he has no clear proof for it.

nahhas-meani:84-84.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُل لِّمَنِ ٱلأَرْضُ وَمَن فِيهَآ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ. سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ﴾.
There is no disagreement about this verse; as for the two after it, Abū ʿAmr reads them ﴿سَيَقُولُونَ اللَّهُ﴾.
Most of the Qurʾān readers read ﴿سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ﴾.
 Whoever reads ﴿سَيَقُولُونَ اللَّهُ﴾ gives the answer according to the wording [of the question].
 And whoever reads ﴿سَيَقُولونَ لِلَّهِ﴾ gives it according to the meaning, just as it is said: "Whose is this house?" and one answers: "Zayd's (لزيدٍ)", according to the wording, or "Its owner is Zayd", according to the meaning.
And: "Who is the owner of this house?" and one answers: "Zayd (زيدٌ)", according to the wording, or "Zayd's (لزيد)", and that suffices you for it.
 And in the first one, ﴿سَيَقُولُونَ اللَّهُ﴾ is permissible in Arabic.

nahhas-meani:88-88.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهُوَ يُجْيِرُ وَلاَ يُجَارُ عَلَيْهِ﴾.
That is, He grants protection from His punishment and from His creation, and none of His creation grants protection against Him.

nahhas-meani:89-89.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ فَأَنَّىٰ تُسْحَرُونَ﴾.
 The meaning of ﴿فَأَنَّىٰ تُسْحَرُونَ﴾ is: how then are you turned away from the truth?

nahhas-meani:91-91.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَا ٱتَّخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِن وَلَدٍ وَمَا كَانَ مَعَهُ مِنْ إِلَـهٍ إِذاً لَّذَهَبَ كُلُّ إِلَـٰهٍ بِمَا خَلَقَ﴾.
 There is an omission in the statement, that is: if there were gods with Him, each god would have kept its creation to itself.
﴿وَلَعَلاَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ﴾ means: some of them would have overpowered others.

nahhas-meani:93-94.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ قُل رَّبِّ إِمَّا تُرِيَنِّي مَا يُوعَدُونَ. رَبِّ فَلاَ تَجْعَلْنِي فِي ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّالِمِينََ﴾ [verses 93, 94].
The vocative (النِّداء) is parenthetical (muʿtariḍ).
 The meaning is: if You show me what they are promised, then do not place me among the wrongdoing people.

nahhas-meani:96-96.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱدْفَعْ بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ ٱلسَّيِّئَةَ﴾.
 Mujāhid, ʿAṭāʾ and Qatāda said: He means the greeting of peace: when you meet him, greet him with peace.

nahhas-meani:97-97.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُلْ رَّبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ هَمَزَاتِ ٱلشَّياطِينِ﴾.
The root meaning of الهَمْز is prodding and pushing; and it is said "so-and-so is a هُمَزَة", as if he prods whomever he finds fault with; so the همز of Satan is his touch and his whispering.

nahhas-meani:99-99.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَآءَ أَحَدَهُمُ ٱلْمَوْتُ قَالَ رَبِّ ٱرْجِعُونِ﴾.
He means those mentioned who do not believe in the resurrection.
 ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ ٱرْجِعُونِ﴾, and he did not say "ارجعْنِ" [in the singular]; he addressed Him in the way Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, speaks of Himself, as He said ﴿إِنَّا نَحْنَ نُحْي المَوْتَى﴾; and it carries the sense of emphasis and repetition.

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Of that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَدْ أَفْلَحَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾.
That is, they have attained success (falāḥ), which is everlasting abiding in Paradise.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْوَارِثُونََ﴾.
It may be asked: An heir is only one who inherits what belonged to someone else, so how is one who enters Paradise called an heir?
There are several answers to this,
which need not be mentioned because of what is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ.
Al-Aʿmash narrated from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ concerning His saying, exalted is He, ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْوَارِثُونَ﴾; he said: "There is no one but has two dwellings: a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in the Fire. If he is admitted to the Fire, the people of Paradise inherit his dwelling; and that is His saying, exalted is He, ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْوَارِثُونَ﴾."

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ ٱلْفِرْدَوْسَ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾.
In the ḥadīth of Saʿīd, from Qatāda, from Anas, traced back to the Prophet (marfūʿ): "And al-Firdaws is the height of Paradise, its middle and its best."
Then He said ﴿هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾, making [the pronoun] feminine according to the sense of "al-janna" (Paradise).

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلإِنْسَانَ مِن سُلاَلَةٍ مِّن طِينٍٍ﴾.
Qatāda said: Adam ﷺ was drawn out (ustulla) from clay.
And someone else said: Adam was called «سلالة» only because he was drawn out from every kind of soil.
And a child is called: the «سلالة» of his father.
It is of the pattern "fuʿāla" from insalla (to slip out), and fuʿāla comes for a small amount of a thing, such as al-qulāma (nail-parings) and al-nukhāla (bran).
And it has been said that «السلالة» is only the sperm-drop of Adam ﷺ; so said Mujāhid.
And this is the soundest of what has been said about it: We created the son of Adam from the «سلالة» of Adam, and Adam is the clay, because he was created from it.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
And this is indicated by His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَاهُ نُطْفَةً فِي قَرَارٍ مَّكِينٍٍ﴾.
And he came to be in a firm lodging only after being created in the loins of the male.
* And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَاهُ نُطْفَةً فِي قَرَارٍ مَّكِينٍ﴾ — his offspring is meant.
﴿ثُمَّ خَلَقْنَا النُّطْفَةَ عَلَقَةً﴾ — and it is the singular of ʿalaq, which is blood before it dries.
﴿فَخَلَقْنَا العَلَقَةَ مُضْغَةً﴾ — the muḍgha is the small piece of flesh, the amount of what is chewed, just as one says "ghurfa" for the amount of what is scooped up, and "ḥuswa" [for the amount of what is sipped].

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَخَلَقْنَا ٱلْمُضْغَةَ عِظَاماً﴾.
And it is also read «عَظْماً» (bone), which is a singular indicating a plural, because it is known that a human being has bones.
﴿فَكَسَوْنَا ٱلْعِظَامَ لَحْماً﴾ — and al-ʿaẓm is permissible on the same basis.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ أَنشَأْنَاهُ خَلْقاً آخَرَ﴾.
ʿAṭāʾ narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas from Abū al-ʿĀliya, Saʿīd from Qatāda from al-Ḥasan, and ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, concerning His saying ﴿ثُمَّ أَنشَأْنَاهُ خَلْقاً آخَرَ﴾: they said: He breathed the spirit into him.
And Hushaym narrated from Manṣūr, from al-Ḥasan: ﴿ثُمَّ أَنشَأْنَاهُ خَلْقاً آخَرَ﴾ — he said: male and female.
And it is narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: the teeth and the growth of hair.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The most fitting of what has been said about it is that it is the breathing of the spirit into him, because he changes from those states until he becomes a human being.
And the hāʾ (pronoun) in ﴿أَنشَأْنَاهُ﴾ refers back to the human being, or to the mention of the bones, the muḍgha and the nuṭfa, i.e.: We produced that.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ لَمَيِّتُونََ﴾.
And in this sense we [may] say: la-māʾitūna.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعَ طَرَآئِقَ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: That is, seven heavens.
And someone else reported that it is said: ṭāraqtu al-shayʾa, i.e. I placed parts of it one above another; so the heavens were called ṭarāʾiq because they are one above another.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً بِقَدَرٍ فَأَسْكَنَّاهُ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
The meaning of ﴿فَأَسْكَنَّاهُ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ is: We made it settled firmly in it.
As it is narrated: "Four rivers of Paradise are in this world: the Euphrates, the Tigris, Sayḥān and Jayḥān."
It was read out to "Abū Yaʿqūb" Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Yūnus, from Jāmiʿ ibn Sawāda, who said: Saʿīd ibn Sābiq narrated to us: Maslama ibn ʿAlī narrated to us from Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down five rivers from Paradise: "Sayḥūn", which is the river of India; "Jayḥūn", which is the river of Balkh; "the Tigris and the Euphrates", which are the two rivers of Iraq; and "the Nile", which is the river of Egypt. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent them down from one of the springs of Paradise, in the lowest of its degrees, on the two wings of Gabriel ﷺ, and He deposited them in the mountains and made them flow in the earth, and placed in them benefits for people in the various kinds of their livelihoods; and that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً بِقَدَرٍ فَأَسْكَنَّاهُ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾. Then when the time of the emergence of "Gog and Magog" comes, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, will send Gabriel, upon him be peace, and he will take up from the earth the Qurʾān, knowledge and these five rivers, and raise that up to heaven; and that is His saying, exalted is He, ﴿وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰ ذَهَابٍ بِهِ لَقَادِرُونَ﴾. So when these things are raised from the earth to heaven, its people will lose the good of religion, of this world and of the Hereafter." «[Translator's note: the source reads «أنزلهما» (dual, "sent the two of them down") although five rivers are listed; translated as "them".]»

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي صَلاَتِهِمْ خَاشِعُونََ﴾.
Ibrāhīm and Qatāda said: Humility (khushūʿ) is in the heart. Ibrāhīm said: and it is stillness.
And Qatāda said: and it is fear, and lowering the gaze in prayer.
Mujāhid said: It is stillness.
And khushūʿ according to some of the people of the language is in the heart and the gaze, as though it were emptying the heart for the prayer, and humbleness in tongue and deed.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of Mujāhid and Ibrāhīm on this is good; when a person is still he is humbled, does not raise his gaze, and does not move his hands. As for placing the gaze on the place of prostration, that is a strict specification.
And it is narrated from ʿAlī, upon him be peace: Khushūʿ is that one does not turn aside in prayer.
And its true nature: one whose heart is broken out of reverence for Allah and awe of Him, so that he may perform what is obligatory on him.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَشَجَرَةً تَخْرُجُ مِن طُورِ سَيْنَآءَ﴾.
The meaning is: and We produced a tree.
Abū ʿUbayda said: al-ṭūr is the mountain, and Saynāʾ is a name.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿سَيْنَاءَ﴾ means the beautiful.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What is well known is that "Saynā" is the name of the place.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَنبُتُ بِٱلدُّهْنِ﴾.
And it is also read "tunbitu bi-l-duhn".
And there are three views on it:
One of them: that the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); this is the position of Abū ʿUbayda, as the poet said:
هُنَّ الحَرَائرُ لا رَبَّاتُ أَحْمِرةٍ * سُوْدُ المحاجِرِ لا يَقْرأنَ بالسُّورِ
(They are free-born women, not owners of donkeys, dark round the eyes, who do not recite the sūras — with a redundant bāʾ in «بالسور».)
And it is said: the bāʾ is attached to the maṣdar (verbal noun) indicated by the verb; and it is said that nabata and anbata have one meaning, as the poet said:
رَأَيْتَ ذَوِي الحَاجَاتِ حَوْل بُيوتِهمْ * قَطِيناً لَهُمْ حتَّى إذا أَنْبتَ البَقْلُ
(You saw those in need settled around their houses as their dependants, until the herbage sprouted (anbata).)
And this view is the position of al-Farrāʾ and Abū Isḥāq; the meaning of ﴿تُنْبِتُ بالدُّهْنِ﴾ and ﴿تَنْبُتُ بالدُّهْنِ﴾ is the same according to them.
And the meaning is: it grows, and with it is the oil, as you say: so-and-so came with the sword, i.e. and with him was the sword.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَصِبْغٍ لِّلآكِلِيِنَ﴾.
Ṣibgh and ṣibāgh have one meaning (a relish).
Qatāda said: He means the olive.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنْ هُوَ إِلاَّ رَجُلٌ بِهِ جِنَّةٌ﴾.
"Jinna", i.e. madness.
﴿فَتَرَبَّصُواْ بِهِ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ﴾ — al-Farrāʾ said: No specific time is meant by "ḥīn"; it is only as you say: leave him until some day.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُل رَّبِّ أَنزِلْنِي مُنزَلاً مُّبَارَكاً﴾.
"Munzal" and "inzāl" are one [in meaning]; and al-manzil is the place of alighting, while al-manzal is in the sense of alighting (al-nuzūl), as you say: jalasa majlasan (he sat a sitting), whereas al-majlis is the place in which one sits.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنِ ٱللَّغْوِ مُّعْرِضُونَ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: from acts of disobedience.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And al-laghw, according to the people of the language, is what ought to be cancelled (yulghā), i.e. discarded and left aside, of play, jesting and acts of disobedience.
That is, earnestness has occupied them away from this.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَتْرَفْنَاهُمْ فِي ٱلْحَيـاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾.
Its meaning: We granted them ample provision until they came to be brought turfa (delicacies), which is like tuḥfa (a choice gift).

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتٌّمْ وَكُنتُمْ تُرَاباً وَعِظاماً أَنَّكُمْ مُّخْرَجُونَ﴾.
Sībawayh said: And among what has come as a substitute (mubdal) in this chapter is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتٌّمْ وَكُنتُمْ تُرَاباً وَعِظاماً أَنَّكُمْ مُّخْرَجُونَ﴾?
He holds that the second "anna" is a badal (substitute) for the first, and that the meaning is: Does he promise you that you will be brought out when you have died?
Sībawayh said: And that is what is intended by it; and the first "anna" was brought to indicate the time of the bringing out.
And al-Farrāʾ, al-Jarmī and Abū al-ʿAbbās hold that the second "anna" is repeated for tawkīd (emphasis); since the speech had become long, its repetition was good.
And al-Akhfash holds that the second "anna" is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ) by an implied verb indicated by "idhā"; the meaning according to him is: Does he promise you that when you have died and become dust and bones, your being brought out will take place? — just as you say: al-yawma al-qitālu (today is the fighting), the meaning according to him being: today the fighting takes place, the fighting occurs.
Al-Farrāʾ said: And in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: ﴿أَيَعِدُكُمْ إذَا مِتُّمْ وكُنْتُم تُرَاباً وَعِظَامَاً إنَّكُمْ مُخْرَجُونَ﴾?
Abū Isḥāq said: And "a-yaʿidukum innakum idhā mittum wa-kuntum turāban wa-ʿiẓāman innakum mukhrajūn" (with kasra) is permissible, because the meaning of "a-yaʿidukum" is "does he say to you".

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَيْهَاتَ هَيْهَاتَ لِمَا تُوعَدُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, for the resurrection.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The Arabs say: «هيهات», «هيهات لما قلت», and «هيهات ما قلت».
Whoever says "«هيهات لما قلت»", its implied form (taqdīr) is: remoteness for what you said; and whoever says "«هيهات ما قلت»", its implied form is: remote is what you said.
And there are dialectal forms of «هيهات» which this is not the place to mention.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنْ هِيَ إِلاَّ حَيَاتُنَا ٱلدُّنْيَا نَمُوتُ وَنَحْيَا﴾.
It may be asked: How did they say ﴿نَمُوتُ وَنَحْيَا﴾ when they do not acknowledge the resurrection?
There are several answers to this:
a- [Among them: in the verse there is a placing forward and a placing back, and the meaning is: it is nothing but our worldly life; we live in it and die,] as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿وَاسْجُدِي وَارْكَعِي﴾.
b- And among them: that the meaning is: we die, and our children live.
c- And a third answer: that the meaning is: we are lifeless, i.e. sperm-drops, then we live in this world.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِلزَّكَـاةِ فَاعِلُونََ﴾.
That is, they pay it.
[And Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, praised whoever pays the zakāt from his wealth, even if he pays nothing else from it.]

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ عَمَّا قَلِيلٍ لَّيُصْبِحُنَّ نَادِمِينَ﴾.
And the meaning is: in a little while; and "mā" is redundant (zāʾida) for tawkīd (emphasis).

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ غُثَآءً﴾.
And the meaning is: We destroyed them and scattered them.
And al-ghuthāʾ is the leaves of trees and rubbish that float on top of the water, because it is scattered and of no use.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ أَرْسَلْنَا رُسُلَنَا تَتْرَى﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: That is, one after another.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the view of most of the people of the language, except al-Aṣmaʿī, who said: ﴿تَتْرَى﴾ is from wātartu ʿalayhi al-kutub (I sent him the letters successively), i.e. with an interval between them.
And the origin of "tatrā" is from al-watr, which is the single one. Whoever says ﴿تَتْرَىً﴾ with nunation, the origin according to him is "watran", then the wāw was replaced by a tāʾ, as one says "tallāhi" in the sense of "wallāhi".
And whoever reads ﴿تَتْرى﴾ without nunation, the meaning according to him is like this, except that he made it [the alif] an alif of the feminine.
And one says titr just as one says witr.
And the meaning is: We sent them one by one; except that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿ثُمَّ أَرْسَلْنَا رُسُلَنَا تَتْرَى﴾ — he said, saying: they follow one another.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ أَحَادِيثَ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: That is, We made an example of them; and one does not say of good, "I made it a tale".

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حَافِظُونَ. إِلاَّ عَلَىٰ أَزْوَاجِهِمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ﴾ [verses 5–6].
[Al-Farrāʾ said: That is, except from those whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has made lawful for them — the four, which he does not exceed.
﴿أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُمْ﴾ is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ), conjoined (maʿṭūf) to "azwājihim", and "mā" is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), i.e. they marry whatever slave-women they wish; they guard their private parts except from these two.]

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ وَأُمَّهُ آيَةً﴾.
Qatāda said: She bore him without a father.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And He did not say "two signs" (āyatayn), because the sign in the two of them is one.
And it is possible that it is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿وَاللَّهُ وَرَسُوْلُهُ أَحَقُّ أَنْ يُرْضُوْهُ﴾.
And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿وَآوَيْنَاهُمَآ إِلَىٰ رَبْوَةٍ﴾.
Isrāʾīl narrated from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وَآوَيْنَاهُمَآ إِلَىٰ رَبْوَةٍ﴾: he said: I have been told that it is Damascus.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And so the well-known reading of Ibn ʿAbbās is ﴿إلَى رِبْوَةٍ﴾. And one says "rabwa" with a fatḥa on the rāʾ; and one says "rabāwa" with a fatḥa on the rāʾ and with alif — al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī read it so; and one says "rubāwa" with alif and a ḍamma on the rāʾ; and one says "ribāwa" with a kasra on the rāʾ; and its meaning is the elevated part of anything.
And the meaning of al-rabwa is the elevated part of the ground; it is said rabā when it rises and increases; and from it is ribā (usury) in selling.
And there has been disagreement about the meaning of this word:
Ibn ʿAbbās said what we have mentioned.
And likewise Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab: ﴿وَآوَيْنَاهُمَا إلَى رَبْوَةٍ﴾ — he said: Damascus.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis).
And Kaʿb al-Aḥbār said: Jerusalem is eighteen miles nearer to heaven.
And Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Egypt.
And Sālim al-Afṭas narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: ﴿وَآوَيْنَاهُمَا إِلَى رِبْوَةٍ﴾ — he said: the raised ground of the earth.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: what is elevated of the ground.
And it has been narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that al-rabwa here is al-Ramla.
As for Ibn Zayd, he said: to a hill among the hills of Egypt; he said: and there are no such hills (rubā) except in Egypt; when the water is let loose, the hills have villages on them, and were it not for the hills those villages would be drowned.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What is correct is to say that it is an elevated place, level, with water on the surface.
* Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿ذَاتِ قَرَارٍ وَمَعِينٍ﴾.
Qatāda said: having water and fruits.
And Sālim narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: ﴿ذَاتِ قَرَارٍ﴾ — level; and ﴿مَعَينٍ﴾ — water on the surface.
And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿وَمَعِيِنٍ﴾ — he said: flowing water.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning of ﴿ذات قرارٍ﴾ in the language is: one settles in it; and what Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said is good.
And ﴿مَعِينٌ﴾ has three analyses (taqdīrāt):
The first of them: that it is a passive participle (mafʿūl).
Abū Isḥāq said: It is the water flowing in the springs (ʿuyūn).
So the mīm on this view is augmentative, like its augmentation in "mabīʿ".
And likewise the mīm is augmentative in the view of whoever said: it is water that is seen with the eye (ʿayn).
2- And it is said that it is "faʿīl" in the sense of "mafʿūl".
ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: One says maʿana al-māʾu when water flows and is abundant, so it is maʿīn and mamʿūn. He said: And Muḥammad ibn Yazīd recited to me a verse of which he had memorized only his saying:
*" وماءٍ مَمْعُون" *
(and water flowing abundantly (mamʿūn))
He said: And one says maʿīn and muʿun, as one says raghīf and rughuf.
And the third view: Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd narrated to us from Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ibn al-Aʿrābī, who said: maʿana al-māʾu yamʿanu muʿūnan, it flowed and ran easily; and also amʿana, and I made it flow (amʿantuhu); and waters that are muʿnān.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَنِ ٱبْتَغَىٰ وَرَآءَ ذٰلِكَ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْعَادُونَ﴾.
That is: whoever seeks other than four wives and what his right hand possesses — ﴿فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْعَادُونَ﴾, i.e. those who deviate to what is not lawful, who have transgressed.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ لأَمَانَاتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ رَاعُونََ﴾.
That is, they guard [them].
It is said: raʿaytu al-shayʾa, i.e. I took care of its proper state; and from it: so-and-so looks after (yarʿā) what is between him and so-and-so.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلَىٰ صَلَوَاتِهِمْ يُحَافِظُونَ﴾.
Masrūq said: That is, they pray them at their proper times.
And it is not in the sense of abandoning, because abandoning [prayer] is disbelief.

safi-cedvel:1-11.t:
* I'rab:
(قد) is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); (الذين) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative, a naʿt (adjective) of (المؤمنون); (هم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is (خاشعون); (في صلاتهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar; (الواو) is a conjunction in the six places, and the five relative nouns (الذين) are in the position of the nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first relative noun; (عن اللغو) is attached to (معرضون), the khabar; (الزكاة) is genitive (majrūr) in form and accusative in position, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle فاعلون, and (اللام) is the lām of strengthening (lām al-taqwiya) [Note: The lām may be original (aṣliyya), and so attached to (فاعلون).]; (لفروجهم) is like للزكاة; (إلّا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (على أزواجهم) is attached to (حافظين) by its being made to include (taḍmīn) the meaning of ممسكين ("withholding") [Note: In the speech there is the meaning of negation which must precede (إلّا), because withholding is the absence of giving freely..
The preposition phrase may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "except as being in charge of their wives".. and al-Zamakhsharī permitted its attachment to an omitted verb, its implied form being يلامون ("they are blamed").]; (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive, conjoined to أزواجهم, and (الفاء) in (فإنّهم) is causal (taʿlīliyya), and the (الفاء) after it is a conjunction; (من) is a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ; (ابتغى) is a past verb, indeclinable on the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (وراء) is an adverb (ẓarf), accusative (manṣūb), attached to (ابتغى); (الفاء) links (rābiṭa) the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (هم) is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position [Note: Or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is العادون.]; (لأماناتهم) is like للزكاة, so الأمانات is an object of (راعون); (على صلواتهم) is attached to (يحافظون); (أولئك هم الوارثون) is like أولئك هم العادون; the last (الذين) is in the position of the nominative, a naʿt of (الوارثون); (فيها) is attached to the khabar (خالدون).
The clause «قد أفلح المؤمنون ...» has no grammatical position, initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «هم.. خاشعون» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (الذين).
The clause «هم.. معرضون» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «هم.. فاعلون» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the third relative noun (الذين).
The clause «هم.. حافظون» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the fourth relative noun (الذين).
The clause «ملكت أيمانهم» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the fourth relative noun (الذين) [Translator's note: so in the source; the relative noun here is ما].
The clause «إنّهم غير ملومين» has no grammatical position, causal.
The clause «من ابتغى ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إنّهم غير ...
The clause «ابتغى وراء ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «أولئك هم العادون» is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «هم العادون» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
The clause «هم.. راعون» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the fifth relative noun (الذين).
The clause «هم.. يحافظون» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the sixth relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يحافظون» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
The clause «أولئك.. الوارثون» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يرثون ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the seventh relative noun (الذين).
The clause «هم.. خالدون» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) or of the object.

* Morphology:
(8) راعون: plural of راع, the active participle of the triliteral رعى; it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion: the yāʾ was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; its pattern is فاعون.

* Rhetoric:
Antithesis (al-ṭibāq):
That is in the saying of Allah the Exalted «الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي صَلاتِهِمْ خاشِعُونَ، وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنِ اللَّغْوِ مُعْرِضُونَ»: an affirmative antithesis (ṭibāq ījāb), for He, glorified is He, combined for the believers in this description doing and abstaining, since He described them by humility in prayer and abstention from idle talk; all of this is semantic affirmative antithesis (ṭibāq al-ījāb al-maʿnawī).

safi-cedvel:12-16.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya) — or a conjunction; (اللام) is the lām of the oath, for an implied (muqaddar) oath; (من سلالة) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خلقنا); (من طين) is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (سلالة); (ثمّ) is a conjunction of delay (tarākhī) in the five places; (نطفة) is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) whose governor (ʿāmil) is جعلناه, accusative (manṣūb); (في قرار) is attached to a naʿt of (نطفة) [Note: Or attached to (جعلناه).]; (علقة) is a second mafʿūl bihi whose governor is خلقنا, by its being made to include (taḍmīn) the meaning of صيّرنا ("We made into"), and likewise (مضغة وعظاما); (الفاء) is a conjunction; (لحما) is a second mafʿūl bihi whose governor is (كسونا), accusative; (خلقا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the absent (third-person) pronoun, in the sense of مخلوقا ("created"); (آخر) is a naʿt of (خلقا), accusative, and it is prevented from tanwīn because it is an adjective on the pattern أفعل; (الفاء) is for linking the effect to the cause; (أحسن) is a badal (substitute) of the word of majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla), nominative (marfūʿ) [Note: It was not parsed as a naʿt of the word of majesty because it has the status of an indefinite, even though it is annexed to الخالقين, for the latter is in the sense of من, i.e. "better than whoever created".. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject)..]; (بعد) is an adverb (ẓarf), accusative, attached to (ميّتون); (يوم) is an adverb, accusative, attached to (تبعثون).
The clause «خلقنا ...» has no grammatical position, the response to the implied oath.. and the implied oath clause is resumptive — or conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the initial (ibtidāʾiyya) clause — and the clause «جعلناه ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause خلقنا..
The clause «خلقنا النطفة ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause جعلناه.
The clause «خلقنا العلقة ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause خلقنا النطفة.
The clause «خلقنا المضغة ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause خلقنا العلقة.
The clause «كسونا العظام ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause خلقنا المضغة.
The clause «أنشأناه ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause كسونا..
The clause «تبارك الله ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أنشأناه.. [Note: Or resumptive, of supplication (duʿāʾiyya).].
The clause «إنّكم ... لميّتون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أنشأناه.
The clause «إنّكم.. تبعثون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إنكم لميّتون.
The clause «تبعثون» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of inna.

* Morphology:
(2) سلالة: a noun for what is drawn out (ustulla) of a thing, or in the sense of the extract (khulāṣa) of a thing; it is in the sense of "the thing drawn out" (al-shayʾ al-maslūl); its pattern is فعلة with ḍamma on the fāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the word is on the pattern فُعالة].

* Rhetoric:
Figurative usage (al-majāz):
In the saying of Allah the Exalted «فِي قَرارٍ مَكِينٍ», His saying «فِي قَرارٍ» means "a place of settling" (mustaqarr); it is so called by way of hyperbole, and what is meant by it is the womb; and He described it by His saying «مكين», i.e. "firmly settled", which here is the sperm-drop (al-nuṭfa), by way of figurative usage, as one says طريق سائر ("a travelling road"). It was also permitted to say that the womb itself is firmly settled, and the meaning of its being firmly settled is that it does not detach, because of the weight of what it carries, or does not expel what is in it; so it is an allusion (kināya) to making the sperm-drop guarded and protected.

* Benefits:
- The disparity of the conjunctions:
All of us know that each of the conjunctions has a meaning; for example, «ثمّ» is for delay (tarākhī), «الفاء» for immediate succession (taʿqīb), and «أو» for equivalence, etc. But there are other considerations which we must grasp and give their role in establishing those differences between the particles; among them is the close connection between the two periods of the conjoined (al-maʿṭūf) and that to which it is conjoined (al-maʿṭūf ʿalayhi), even if the duration of each of them is long.
And among them is the rational distance between the two members of the conjunction, even if their durations are close; for rational unlikelihood makes the period of conjunction take the place of delay in time, and the conjunction الفاء was replaced by the conjunction «ثم». This subject has subtleties and fine considerations worthy of study, if the plan of the book allowed it.

safi-cedvel:17-22.t:
* I'rab:
(لقد خلقنا): its i'rab has already been given [Note: In verse (12) of this sūra.]; (فوقكم) is an adverb (ẓarf), accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خلقنا); (طرائق) is a diptote, because it is a plural on the pattern of the ultimate plurals (ṣīghat muntahā al-jumūʿ); (الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) — or a conjunction; (ما) is negating, inoperative (muhmala); (عن الخلق) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar (predicate) (غافلين).
The clause «خلقنا ...» has no grammatical position, the response to the implied (muqaddar) oath.. and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position, resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya) — or conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding implied oath clause [Note: In verse (12) of this sūra.].
The clause «ما كنّا.. غافلين» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of خلقنا [Note: Or conjoined to the response to the oath.].
18- (الواو) is a conjunction; (من السماء) is attached to (أنزلنا); (بقدر) is attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil [Note: Or attached to a naʿt (adjective) of ماء, i.e. "being in measure", i.e. measured out.]; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (في الأرض) is attached to (أسكنّاه); (الواو) is a conjunction — or circumstantial; (على ذهاب) is attached to the khabar (قادرون); (به) is attached to (ذهاب), and (الباء) is for transitivity (taʿdiya); (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis.
The clause «أنزلنا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause of the response to the oath.
The clause «أسكنّاه ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أنزلنا.
The clause «إنّا.. لقادرون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أسكنّاه [Note: Or parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya); and it may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil or of the object in (أسكنّاه).].
19- (الفاء) is a conjunction; (لكم) is attached to (أنشأنا); (به) is attached to (أنشأنا), and (الباء) is causal (sababiyya); (من نخيل) is attached to a naʿt of (جنّات); the second (لكم) is attached to a fronted khabar; (فيها) is attached to the "being settled" (al-istiqrār) which is the khabar [Note: It may be attached to a ḥāl of فواكه — a naʿt placed before what it qualifies.], and the mubtadaʾ (subject) is (فواكه); (الواو) is a conjunction; (منها) is attached to (تأكلون).
The clause «أنشأنا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أسكنّاه.
The clause «لكم فيها فواكه ...» is in the position of the accusative, a naʿt of جنّات [Note: Or it is a ḥāl of جنّات, because it has been qualified by the preposition and its genitive noun (من نخيل).].
The clause «تأكلون» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause لكم فيها فواكه.
20- (الواو) is a conjunction; (شجرة) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being أنشأنا; (من طور) is attached to (تخرج); (سيناء) is a diptote because of being a proper name and feminine — or a feminine ending in the extended alif of femininity (alif al-taʾnīth al-mamdūda); (بالدهن) is attached to (تنبت), and (الباء) is for transitivity; (صبغ) is conjoined to الدهن by the wāw, genitive (majrūr); (للآكلين) is attached to a naʿt of (صبغ), and the sign of its genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «(أنشأنا) شجرة ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the mentioned clause أنشأنا.
The clause «تخرج ...» is in the position of the accusative, a naʿt of شجرة.
The clause «تنبت ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl of the fāʿil of تخرج.
21- 22- (الواو) is a conjunction; (لكم) is attached to the khabar of inna; (في الأنعام) is attached to a ḥāl of (عبرة) [Note: Or attached to the "being settled" which is the khabar.], and (اللام) is the lām of the inchoative (lām al-ibtidāʾ), for emphasis; (عبرة) is the postponed ism of inna, accusative; (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by (من), attached to (نسقيكم); (في بطونها) is attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما; (الواو) is a conjunction; (لكم فيها ... تأكلون) is like the previous one; (الواو) is a conjunction; (عليها) is attached to the passive تحملون, and likewise (على الفلك).
The clause «إنّ لكم.. لعبرة» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the implied oath clause.
The clause «نسقيكم ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لكم فيها منافع ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نسقيكم.
The clause «منها تأكلون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نسقيكم.
The clause «عليها.. تحملون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نسقيكم.

* Morphology:
(17) طرائق: plural of طريقة.. see verse (63) of Sūrat Ṭā Hā.
(18) ذهاب: an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the triliteral verb ذهب; its pattern is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ; there is another maṣdar, ذهوب, with ḍamma on the dhāl.
(20) سيناء: a noun of place for the well-known desert; its pattern is فيعال; it contains the substitution (ibdāl) of its lām — which is the yāʾ — into hamza, because it comes at the end after a quiescent extra alif.
(20) الدهن: a noun for the pressed juice of anything containing fat; its pattern is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn.
(20) صبغ: a noun for that with which a thing is dyed; its plural is أصباغ; its pattern is فعل with kasra then sukūn.
(آكلين): plural of آكل, the active participle of the triliteral أكل; its pattern is فاعل and the plural فاعلين; the hamza was merged with the quiescent alif of فاعل and a madda was placed over it.

* Rhetoric:
Explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya):
In the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَصِبْغٍ لِلْآكِلِينَ», where liquid condiment is likened to dye; then the thing likened (al-mushabbah) was omitted and the thing likened to (al-mushabbah bihi) was retained, the common ground being taking on its colour when dipped in it.

* Benefits:
1- Emphasis (al-tawkīd):
The discerning observer of the styles of the Qur'an notices that emphasis is a basic sinew in the style of the Noble Qur'an. Look at verse 18 (وَإِنَّا عَلى ذَهابٍ بِهِ لَقادِرُونَ): this passage contains a number of devices of emphasis, the first of them: (أنّ) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has إنّا]; the second: the fronting of the khabar «عَلى ذَهابٍ» before the mubtadaʾ; the third: the redundant preposition «به» [Translator's note: so in the source, although the i'rab above makes this bāʾ one of transitivity, and عَلى ذَهابٍ is attached to the khabar قادرون rather than being a fronted khabar]; the fourth: «the shifted lām of قادرون». We can say the like of that about the saying of Allah the Exalted «إِنَّ لَكُمْ فِي الْأَنْعامِ لَعِبْرَةً», which contains three emphasisers. The like of that is abundant in the Noble Qur'an, for whoever observes its outward form. Its explanation differs with the difference of the sūras and their subjects. Perhaps among the first of these reasons is the obstinacy of the polytheists, the hypocrites and the People of the Book who were the subject of these addresses; and among them too is the strength of the proof against them, and its establishment before them, on His part, exalted is He. So is there anyone who will take heed?!
2- طور سيناء is the very same as طور سينين:
Either it is an annexational compound (murakkab iḍāfī), like امرئ القيس and بعلبك, and it is a diptote.
Or «طور» is the name of the mountain, and it has been annexed to a region named «سيناء», which is known as «the Sinai Desert»; it is an extension of Palestine up to the Suez Canal, and it is the desert of wandering (al-tīh) in which the people of Mūsā wandered for forty years. As for the tree, it is the olive tree, because its cultivation became famous in this region of the lands of al-Shām.

safi-cedvel:23-23.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); (لقد أرسلنا نوحا): the i'rab of its parallel has already been given [Note: In verse (12) of this sūra.]; (إلى قومه) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أرسلنا); (الفاء) is a conjunction; (يا قوم) is a vocative particle and the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the letter before the yāʾ, which is deleted for lightness (takhfīf).. and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (ما) is negating, inoperative (muhmala); (لكم) is attached to a fronted khabar (predicate); (إله) is genitive (majrūr) in form and nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); (غيره) is a naʿt (adjective) of إله, following its position, and so nominative; (الهمزة) is for the interrogative of rebuke (tawbīkhī); (الفاء) is a conjunction..
The clause «أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position, the response to the implied (muqaddar) oath.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the response clause.
The clause «the vocative and its response ...» is in the position of the accusative, the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «اعبدوا ...» has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative.
The clause «ما لكم من إله ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) — or causal (taʿlīliyya) — and the clause «تتّقون ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.:
"Have you disobeyed, so that you do not fear (Allah)?"

safi-cedvel:24-25.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative, a naʿt (adjective) of الملأ; (من قومه) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of كفروا; (ما) is negating, inoperative (muhmala); (إلّا) is for restriction (ḥaṣr); (بشر) is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هذا); (مثلكم) is a naʿt of بشر, nominative (marfūʿ); (عليكم) is attached to (يتفضّل).
The interpreted maṣdar (al-maṣdar al-muʾawwal) (أن يتفضّل) is in the position of the accusative, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) whose governor (ʿāmil) is يريد..
(الواو) is a conjunction; (اللام) occurs in the response of لو; (بهذا) is attached to (سمعنا); (في آبائنا) is attached to (سمعنا) with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "in the reports of our fathers" [Note: Or attached to an omitted ḥāl of the demonstrative.].
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «ما هذا إلّا بشر ...» is in the position of the accusative, the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «يريد ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl of بشر [Note: Because the indefinite here has been qualified; and the clause may be a naʿt of بشر, in the position of the nominative.].
The clause «يتفضّل ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «لو شاء الله ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the object of the saying.
The clause «أنزل ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition (jawāb sharṭ ghayr jāzim).
The clause «ما سمعنا ...» has no grammatical position, a resumption within the scope of the saying.
25- (إن) is negating; (إلّا) is for restriction; (رجل) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو); (به) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (جنّة); (الفاء) links (rābiṭa) the apodosis of an implied condition; (به) is attached to (تربّصوا), and likewise (حتّى حين).
The clause «إن هو إلّا رجل ...» has no grammatical position, a resumption within the scope of the saying.
The clause «به جنّة ...» is in the position of the nominative, a naʿt of رجل.
The clause «تربّصوا ...» is in the position of the jussive (majzūm), the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you want to know his reality, then wait".

safi-cedvel:26-26.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّ) is the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the letter before the yāʾ, which is deleted for lightness (takhfīf), and the deleted (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle (ḥarf maṣdarī), and (النون) is for protection (al-wiqāya).. and the deleted (الياء) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
The interpreted maṣdar (al-maṣdar al-muʾawwal) (ما كذّبون..) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (انصرني), and (الباء) is causal (sababiyya).
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya).
The clause «ربّ انصرني ...» is in the position of the accusative, the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «انصرني ...» has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative.
The clause «كذّبون ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (ما).

safi-cedvel:27-27.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is a conjunction; (إليه) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أوحينا); (أن) is explicative (tafsīriyya); (بأعيننا) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of اصنع, and (الباء) is for accompaniment (mulābasa); and (الفاء) in (فاسلك) links (rābiṭa) the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (فيها) is attached to (اسلك) by its being made to include (taḍmīn) the meaning of أدخل ("bring in"); (من كلّ) is attached to (اسلك); (اثنين) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ; (إلّا) is for exception; (من) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative, excepted (mustathnā) by إلّا; (عليه) is attached to (سبق); (منهم) is a ḥāl of the pronoun in (عليه); (لا) is prohibitive, making jussive (nāhiya jāzima); (في الذين) is attached to (تخاطبني) with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "concerning the matter of those who"..
The clause «أوحينا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause قال [Note: In the previous verse (26).].
The clause «اصنع ...» has no grammatical position, explicative.
The clause «جاء أمرنا ...» is in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «فار التنّور ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause جاء أمرنا.
The clause «اسلك ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition (jawāb sharṭ ghayr jāzim).
The clause «سبق عليه القول» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من).
The clause «لا تخاطبني ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «ظلموا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إنّهم مغرقون» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Benefits:
- «فَأَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْهِ أَنِ اصْنَعِ الْفُلْكَ»:
