Al-Zamakhsharī said: «He put the singular in the place of the plural because the confusion is removed, since the human being has many bones.» The Shaykh said: «According to Sībawayh and his companions this is not permissible except out of necessity, and they recited:
3405 - كُلوا في بَعْضِ بطنِكُم تَعِفُّوا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Eat in part of your belly, you will be chaste …)
even though it is known that each one has a belly.» I say: and like it:
3406 - لا تُنْكِروا القَتْلَ وقد سُبِيْنا ... في حَلْقِكم عَظْمٌ وقد شُجينا
(Do not deny the killing, for we have been taken captive; in your throats is a bone, and we have been choked)
he means: "in your throats". And like it the saying of another:
3407 - به جِيَفُ الحَسْرى فأمَّا عِظامُها ... فبِيْضٌ وأمَّا جِلْدُها فصَلِيْبُ
(In it are the carcasses of worn-out camels; as for their bones, they are white, and as for their hide, it is hard)
he means: "their hides". And of it is {وعلى سَمْعِهِمْ} [al-Baqara: 7]; a part of this has already been given.
His saying: {أَحْسَنَ الخالقين}: there are three views on it. One: that it is a badal (substitute) for the Majestic Name. The second: that it is an adjective (naʿt) of the Majestic Name, and it is preferable to the previous, because a badal with a derived word is rare. The third: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: "He is the best". The default is that there is no implication. Abū l-Baqāʾ forbade that it be a description, saying: «because it is indefinite even if annexed to a definite, because the muḍāf ilayhi is a replacement for «من», and so are all forms of afʿal followed by "than you".» I say: he built this on one of two views about the elative afʿal when it is annexed: is its annexation genuine (maḥḍa) or not? The sound one is the first.
And «الخالقين», that is, "those who measure out", as in the saying of Zuhayr:
3408 - ولأنتَ تَفْرِيْ ما خَلَقْتَ وبَعْ ... ضُ القومِ يَخْلُقُ ثم لا يَفْرِي
(You cut what you have measured out, while some of the people measure out and then do not cut)
The specification (mumayyiz) of afʿal is omitted because the muḍāf ilayhi indicates it, that is: "the best of the creators in creation", that is, "of those who measure out, in measuring", like His saying {أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقَاتَلُونَ} [al-Ḥajj: 39], that is: "to fight"; what permission was given for is omitted because the ṣila indicates it.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {بَعْدَ ذلك}: that is, after what has been mentioned, and for that reason the demonstrative is singular. The majority read «لَمَيِّتُون». Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Ibn Muḥayṣin read «لَمائِتون». The difference between them is that mayyit indicates permanence and settledness, and māʾit indicates occurrence, like ḍayyiq and ḍāʾiq, and farih and fārih. So of one who will die one says mayyit and māʾit, and of one who has died, mayyit only and not māʾit, because the quality is settled and permanent; the like of it will come in al-Zumar, if Allah the Exalted wills. If it is asked: no two people differ over death, while how many differ over the resurrection, so why did He strengthen what is agreed upon with the strongest emphasis and omit that degree of emphasis for what is disputed? The answer: because the evidences for the resurrection are abundant and mutually supporting, it was brought out in the form of what is agreed upon and needs no such emphasis; and because they did not work for death and did not care about its affairs, they were placed in the position of one who denies it, so He brought them out in the form of the denier who thinks it utterly improbable.
The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) was asked about that. He answered that the lām mostly makes the imperfect purely present, and it cannot enter «تُبْعثون» because that is made purely future by its governing a future adverbial. He objected to himself with His saying {وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَيَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ القيامة} [al-Naḥl: 124], for the lām entered the imperfect which governs a future adverbial, namely the Day of Resurrection. He answered that this is excluded by his word "mostly", or that the governor of «يوم القيامة» is implied. There is something to consider in this which is not hidden, since in it the governor is prepared to govern and then cut off from it.
And «بعد ذلك» is attached to «مَيِّتون», and the lām of inceptive (lām al-ibtidāʾ) does not prevent that.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {على ذَهَابٍ بِهِ}: «على ذَهابٍ» is attached to «لَقادرون», and the lām, as already stated, does not prevent that; and «به» is attached to «ذَهاب», and the bāʾ is equivalent to the hamza (of transitivization), like it in {لَذَهَبَ بِسَمْعِهِمْ} [al-Baqara: 20], that is, "to cause it to go away".

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {وَشَجَرَةً}: conjoined to «جناتٍ». Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «سِيناء» with kasra on the sīn; the rest read it with fatḥa. Al-Aʿmash likewise, except that he shortened it. As for the first reading, the hamza in it is not for the feminine, since in the language there is no fiʿlāʾ with kasra on the first whose hamza is feminine; rather it is for attachment (ilḥāq), like «sirdāḥ» and «qirṭās», so it is like «ʿilbāʾ», and the hamza is converted from a yāʾ or wāw, because attachment is done with them; when the weak letter occurred at the end after an extra alif it was converted to a hamza, like ridāʾ and kisāʾ. Al-Fārisī said: «It is the yāʾ that appeared in "dirḥāya".» The dirḥāya is the short, fat man.
Abū l-Baqāʾ made this hamza radical (original), saying: «The hamza on this is a root, like "ḥimlāq", and is not feminine since in the language there is nothing like [ḥamrāʾ, and the yāʾ is a root, since in the language there is no "sanaʾ"]», meaning the root sīn-nūn-hamza. This contradicts what was said earlier, that it is substituted for an extra letter attached to the root. Although his words admit being interpreted as the earlier, on this the prohibition of full declension (manʿ al-ṣarf) is for definiteness and femininity, because it is the name of a particular place; it was also said: for definiteness and foreignness. Some said: the sound view is that «سِيْناء» is a foreign name which the Arabs pronounced, and their dialects differed in it, so they said saynāʾ like ḥamrāʾ and ṣafrāʾ, and sīnāʾ like ʿilbāʾ and ḥirbāʾ, and sīnīn like khindhīdh and ziḥlīl. The khindhīdh is the stallion and also the eunuch, so it is among the contraries (aḍdād), and it is also the high mountain peak; and the ziḥlīl is one who withdraws, from zaḥala when he withdrew.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «"Ṭūr Sīnāʾ" and "Ṭūr Sīnīn": either Ṭūr is annexed to a place whose name is Sīnāʾ and Sīnūn, or it is a name for the mountain compounded of a muḍāf and muḍāf ilayhi like Imruʾ al-Qays and Baʿlabakk, for those who annexed. As for the one who put kasra on the sīn of «سيناء», he prevented full declension for definiteness and foreignness, or femininity, because it is a place, and a fiʿlāʾ does not have its alif for the feminine, like ʿilbāʾ and ḥirbāʾ.» I say: that the alif of fiʿlāʾ with kasra is not feminine is the view of the people of Basra. As for the Kufans, according to them its alif is feminine, so it is prevented from full declension for necessary femininity, like ḥamrāʾ and its kind. The kasra on the sīn of «سِيْناء» is the dialect of Kināna.
As for the second reading, its alif is feminine, so the prohibition of full declension is clear. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: «Its hamza is feminine, since there is no faʿlāl with fatḥa in the language. And what al-Farrāʾ reported, their saying "a she-camel with khazʿāl in her", is not established, and if it is established it is anomalous and is not to be built upon.»
Some have erred by deriving «سيناء» from sanā (light), and that is not sound for two reasons. One: that it is not Arabic in its coinage; they stated that explicitly, as was said. The second: that even if we grant it is Arabic in its coinage, the two roots differ, for the middle radical of «sanā» is nūn and of «sīnāʾ» is yāʾ. So some said. There is something to consider in it, since someone could say: we do not grant that the middle radical of «سيناء» is yāʾ; rather its middle radical is nūn, and its yāʾ is extra and its hamza is converted from a wāw as sanāʾ was converted, and its pattern then is fīʿāl, and fīʿāl exists in their speech, like mīlāʿ and qītāl, the maṣdar of qātala.
His saying «تنبُتُ»: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «تُنْبِتُ» with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the bāʾ; the rest read it with fatḥa on the tāʾ and ḍamma on the bāʾ. As for the first, there are three views on it. One: that «أنبت» has the meaning of «نَبَتَ», so it is among the cases where faʿala and afʿala agree, and they recited from Zuhayr:
3409 - رأيتُ ذوي الحاجات عند بيوتهِم ... قَطِيْناً لها حتى إذا أَنْبَتَ البقلُ
(I saw the people of needs at their homes, residing there until the herbage grew)
that is: "grew"; al-Aṣmaʿī denied it. The second: that the hamza is for transitivization and the object is omitted for the understanding of the meaning, that is: "it brings forth its fruit or its pickings"; and «بالدهن» means "accompanied by the oil". The third: that the bāʾ is redundant on the direct object, as in {وَلاَ تُلْقُواْ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 195] and the saying of the poet:
3410 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
سُوْدُ المَحاجرِ لا يَقْرَأْنَ بالسُّوَرِ
(… black around the eyes, they do not recite the sūras)
and the saying of another:
3411 - نَضْربُ بالسَّيْفِ ونرْجُو بالفَرَجْ ...
(We strike with the sword and hope for relief …)
As for the other reading, it is clear, and the bāʾ is a ḥāl from the agent, that is: "accompanied by the oil", meaning "and in it is the oil".
Al-Ḥasan, al-Zuhrī and Ibn Hurmuz read «تُنْبِتُ» in the passive, from "Allah made it grow"; and «بالدهن» is a ḥāl from the one standing in the place of the agent, that is, "accompanied by the oil".
Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh read «تُنْبِتُ الدُّهْنَ» from anbata; the dropping of the bāʾ here indicates its redundancy in the reading of those who kept it. Al-Ashhab and Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Malik read «بالدِّهان», which is the plural of duhn, like rumḥ and rimāḥ. As for the reading of Ubayy, «تُثْمر», and of ʿAbd Allāh, «تَخْرج», it is commentary and not a reading, for its opposition to the written copy (al-sawād).
Al-duhn is the extract of what contains fat. Al-dahn with fatḥa is anointing with oil, a maṣdar of dahana yadhunu, and mudāhana (flattery) is from that, as though he anoints his companion so that his mind is settled.
His saying: {وَصِبْغٍ}: the majority read it in the genitive in sequence with «بالدُّهْن». Al-Aʿmash read «وصبغاً» in the accusative in sequence with the position of «بالدُّهْن», like the reading of «وأَرْجلَكم» in one of its possibilities. ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh read «وصِباغ» with an alif, and this reading was fitting with the reading of those who read «بالدِّهان». Ṣibgh and ṣibāgh are like dabgh and dibāgh, a noun for what is used for the action. And «للآكلين» is an adjective.
[Translator's note: the source text of Abū l-Baqāʾ's quotation is damaged («مثل [حِمْراء والياءُ أصلٌ إذ ليس في الكلام «سنأ»]»); the bracketed portion is in the source. The poetic fragments 3410 and 3411 are incomplete in the source, and the glosses are mine and only approximate.]

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {نُّسْقِيكُمْ}: what is in al-Naḥl has been mentioned. It was also read «تَسْقيكم» with the tāʾ, that is: the cattle (al-anʿām).

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {مُنزَلاً مُّبَارَكاً}: Abū Bakr read it with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the zāy; the rest read it with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the zāy. Both manzil and munzal may be a noun of the maṣdar, namely the sending down (inzāl) and the alighting (nuzūl), and may be a noun of place for alighting and sending down; however, the analogy is «مُنْزَلاً» with ḍamma and fatḥa because of «أَنْزِلْني». As for the fatḥa and kasra, it is on the substitution of the maṣdar of the triliteral for the maṣdar of the quadriliteral, as in {أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ الأرض نَبَاتاً} [Nūḥ: 17]; its like has already been given for madkhal and mudkhal in sūrat al-Nisāʾ.
And «إنْ» in His saying {وَإِن كُنَّا} is the lightened «inna», and the lām is the distinguishing lām (fāriqa). It was also said: «إنْ» is negative and the lām has the meaning of «إلاَّ»; that has been given more than once.

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {فَأَرْسَلْنَا فِيهِمْ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you ask: arsala ought to be made transitive with «ilā» like its sisters, which are wajjaha, anfadha and baʿatha; so why is it made transitive in the Quran at times with «ilā» and at times with «fī», as in His saying {كَذَلِكَ أَرْسَلْنَاكَ في أُمَّةٍ} [al-Raʿd: 30]? I say: it was not made transitive with «fī» as it is with «ilā», and He did not make it its complement as that is, but the nation or the town was made a location for the sending, as in the saying of Ruʾba:
3412 - أرسلْتَ فيها مُصْعباً ذا إقحامِ
(You sent into it Muṣʿab, the plunger)
and baʿatha has come in that way, as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَوْ شِئْنَا لَبَعَثْنَا فِي كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ نَّذِيراً} [al-Furqān: 51].»
His saying: {أَنِ اعبدوا}: it may be the maṣdarī «an», that is: "We sent him with 'worship'", that is, with the saying "worship"; and it may be explicative.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you ask: the saying of Hūd in his answer is mentioned in sūrat al-Aʿrāf and sūrat Hūd without a wāw: {قَالَ الملأ الذين كَفَرُواْ مِن قَوْمِهِ إِنَّا لَنَرَاكَ فِي سَفَاهَةٍ} [al-Aʿrāf: 66], {قَالُواْ ياهود مَا جِئْتَنَا بِبَيِّنَةٍ} [Hūd: 53], and here with the wāw; what is the difference between them? I say: the one without a wāw is on the implication of a questioner asking: "so what was said to him?", and it was said: they said such-and-such. As for the one with the wāw, it is a conjoining of what they said to what he said, and its meaning is that there came together in occurring this truth and this falsehood, and how far apart they are.»
I say: someone could say: this is an answer by the very fact, and the question remains, since it would be good to say: why is their saying here not also made an answer to a questioner, as in its two counterparts, if the matter were reversed?

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {مِمَّا تَشْرَبُونَ}: that is, "from it"; the returning pronoun was omitted because its conditions are fulfilled, namely sameness of the preposition and of what it is attached to, its not standing in the place of a nominative, and the absence of another pronoun. This is if we make it mean "that which" (alladhī); if you make it a maṣdar it needs no returning pronoun, and the maṣdar occurs in the place of the object, that is: "from your drink". He said in «al-Taḥrīr»: «Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the meaning of «mā tashrabūn» is with an omission, that is: you drink from it.
This is not permissible according to the Basrans, and it needs no omission at all, because when «mā» is maṣdarī it needs no returning pronoun, and if you make it mean "that which" you omit the returning pronoun and there is no need to imply «min».» He means that it is implied as "you drink it" without a preposition, and then the conditions of omission are also present; but the correspondence is lost, since His saying {تَأْكُلُونَ مِنْهُ} has partitive sense, so if you implied this as "you drink it" without «min», the correspondence would be lost. Then his saying "this is not permissible according to the Basrans" is disputed; rather it is permissible for the presence of the conditions of omission.

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His saying: {إِذَنْ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: «It occurs in the apodosis of a condition and is an answer to those of their people who spoke back to them.» The Shaykh said: ««Idhan» does not occur in the apodosis of a condition; it occurs between «innakum» and the khabar, and «innakum» with the khabar is not an apodosis of the condition, but that is the sentence that answers the oath omitted before the conditional «in». Had «innakum» and the khabar been the answer to the condition, the fāʾ would have been necessary on «innakum»; indeed, had it been with the fāʾ in a construction other than the Quran, that construction would not be permitted except according to al-Farrāʾ. The Basrans do not allow it, and it is a mistake according to them.»
I say: he means that when a condition and an oath follow one another, the earlier of the two is answered, and the oath here is earlier, so it ought to be answered and the condition not answered; and had the condition been answered, the rule would be disturbed, except according to some of the Kufans, who answer the condition even if it comes later. And it exists in poetry.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying: {أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ}: the i'rab of the verse has six views. One: that the noun of the first «أنَّ» is annexed to the pronoun of address, which was omitted and its muḍāf ilayhi put in its place, and the khabar is His saying {إِذَا مِتٌّمْ}, and {أَنَّكُمْ مُّخْرَجُونَ} is a repetition of the first «أنَّ» for emphasis and as an indication of the omitted; the meaning: "that your being brought forth, when you have died and become…".
The second: that the khabar of the first «أنَّ» is «مُخْرَجُون», and it is the governor of «إذا», and the second was repeated for emphasis when the separation became long. Al-Jarmī, al-Mubarrad and al-Farrāʾ held this.
The third: that {أَنَّكُمْ مُّخْرَجُونَ} is interpreted as a maṣdar nominative by an omitted verb, that omitted verb being the apodosis of the conditional «إذا», and the conditional «إذا» with its implied apodosis is the khabar of the first «أنَّكم»; its implied form: "it will happen that you will be brought forth".
The fourth: like the third in being nominative by an implied verb, except that this implied verb is the khabar of the first «أنَّ», and it is the governor of «إذا».
The fifth: that the khabar of the first is omitted because the khabar of the second indicates it, its implied form being: "that you will be resurrected", and it is the governor of the adverbial, and that the second «أنَّ» and what is in its scope is a badal from the first; this is the school of Sībawayh.
The sixth: that {أَنَّكُمْ مُّخْرَجُونَ} is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar is the adverbial fronted before it, and the sentence is a khabar for the first «أنكم», the implication being: "Does he promise you that your being brought forth will be, or is established, at the time of your death?" It is not permissible, on any view, that the governor of «إذا» be «مُخْرَجُون», because what is in the scope of «أنَّ» does not govern what is before it, and «مِتُّم» does not govern it because it is a muḍāf ilayhi; and «أنَّكم» and what is in its scope is in the position of accusative or genitive after omitting the preposition, since the original is "does he promise you with the fact that you". It is also permissible not to imply a preposition, so that it is in the position of accusative only, as in waʿadtu Zaydan khayran.

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying: {هَيْهَاتَ هَيْهَاتَ}: a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) whose meaning is "it is far", repeated for emphasis, so the case is not one of competing governors (tanāzuʿ). Jarīr said:
3413 - فهيهاتَ هيهاتَ العَقيقُ وأهلُه ... وهيهاتَ خِلٌّ بالعقيقِ نُواصِلُهْ
(How far, how far is al-ʿAqīq and its people; and how far is a friend at al-ʿAqīq with whom we keep ties)
Al-Zajjāj, in the apparent sense of his wording, explained it with a maṣdar, saying: «Remoteness (al-buʿd) for what you are promised, or it is remote for what you are promised.» The apparent sense is that it is a maṣdar, by the evidence of his conjoining the verb to it. It is possible that he explained only the meaning. And «هيهاتَ» is a verbal noun of an intransitive verb that takes an agent, and here what has the appearance of the agent has come in the genitive with the lām. Some made it as it appears and said: «ما توعدون» is the agent of it, and the lām was added to it; the implication: "far, far is what you are promised". That is weak, since the addition of the lām to the agent is not known. Others made the agent an implied pronoun because the speech indicates it; Abū l-Baqāʾ estimated: «Far, far is the confirmation, or the validity, of what you are promised.» Another estimated: "your being brought forth is far", and «لِما تُوعدون» is for clarification. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is to clarify the one regarded as remote, what is it, after the declaration by the word of remoteness? As the lām came in {هَيْتَ لَكَ} [Yūsuf: 23] to clarify the one to whom "come" is addressed.» Al-Zajjāj said: «Remoteness is for what you are promised», making it a mubtadaʾ and the prepositional phrase after it the khabar. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you ask: what you are promised is the one regarded as remote, and its right is to be nominative by «hayhāta» as it was nominative in the saying:
فهيهاتَ هيهاتَ العَقيقُ وأهلُه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
then what is this lām? I say: al-Zajjāj said in his commentary: «Remoteness for what you are promised, or a remoteness for what you are promised, according to the one who gives it tanwīn, placing it in the position of the maṣdar.»» The Shaykh said: «Al-Zamakhsharī's saying "whoever gives it tanwīn places it in the position of the maṣdar" is not clear, because they have given tanwīn to verbal nouns and we do not say that when given tanwīn they are placed in the position of maṣdars.» I say: al-Zamakhsharī did not say that; he said only that for one who gives tanwīn, it is placed in the position of the maṣdar because of his saying "or a remoteness (buʿdun)"; so the tanwīn is the reason for his implying it as indefinite, not for its being placed in the position of the maṣdar; for among verbal nouns, those given tanwīn are indefinite, and those not given tanwīn are definite, such as ṣah and ṣahin, the first implying "the silence" and the second "some silence".
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «Sometimes it is followed by the agent without a lām; you say hayhāta majīʾu Zaydin, that is, "far"; and sometimes the agent is omitted where there is a lām, as in this verse. The implication: far is the existence for what you are promised.» The Shaykh did not allow it, both because of his saying the agent was omitted, and the agent is not omitted, and because it involves omitting the maṣdar, which is the existence, and keeping its dependent, «لِما تُوعدون». And the second «هيهاتَ» is a verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī) for the first. It has also come unemphasized, as in the saying:
3414 - هيهات مَنْزِلُنا بنَعْفِ سُوَيْقَةٍ ... كانت مباركةً على الأيام
(How far is our abode at the slope of Suwayqa, which was blessed through the days)
and another said:
3415 - هيهاتَ ناسٌ مِنْ أُناسٍ ديارُهُمْ ... دُقاقٌ ودارُ الآخرين الأوانسُ
(How far apart are some people from others: their abodes are slight, and the abode of the others is the congenial one)
and Ruʾba said:
3416 - هيهاتَ مِنْ مُنْخَرِقٍ هَيْهاؤه
(How far from one whose far-reaching distance is torn open …)
Al-Qaysī, the commentator on «Abyāt al-Īḍāḥ», said: «This is like your saying "his remoteness is remote"; for he built from this word a faʿlāl, so it came as qalqāl and zilzāl. The alif in «hayhāt» is not the alif in «hayhāʾuhu»; in «hayhāt» it is the second lām of the verb, like the second qāf of ḥaqḥaqa, and in «hayhāʾuhu» it is the extra alif of faʿlāl.»
In this word there are many dialects, exceeding forty, and I mention here the famous ones and those read: the famous is hayhāta with fatḥa on the tāʾ without tanwīn, indeclinable (mabnī) because it occurs in the place of an indeclinable or for its resemblance to a particle, and the verification of that has already been given. The majority read it, and it is the dialect of the Hijazis. And «هَيْهاتاً» with fatḥa and tanwīn, which Abū ʿAmr read in the transmission of Hārūn from him; Ibn ʿAṭiyya ascribed it to Khālid ibn Ilyās. And «هَيْهاتٌ» with ḍamma and tanwīn, which al-Aḥmar and Abū Ḥaywa read. And with ḍamma without tanwīn, transmitted from Abū Ḥaywa also, so from him there are two ways in it; Abū l-Sammāl agreed with him in the first and not the second.
And «هَيْهاتٍ» with kasra and tanwīn, which ʿĪsā and Khālid ibn Ilyās read; and with kasra without tanwīn, the reading of Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba, also transmitted from ʿĪsā, and it is the dialect of Tamīm and Asad. And hayhāt with sukūn on the tāʾ, which ʿĪsā also read, and Khārija from Abū ʿAmr, and al-Aʿraj. And «هَيْهاهْ» with a hāʾ at the end in connection and pause. And «أَيْهاتَ» with the hāʾ replaced by hamza with fatḥa on the tāʾ; some of the readers read these two, as Abū l-Baqāʾ reported. These are nine dialects that have been read, and none but the first is mutawātir.
Replacing the hamza for the first hāʾ is permissible in all of the above, which completes sixteen dialects. And «إيهان» with a nūn at the end, and «أيهى» with an alif at the end. Whoever puts fatḥa on the tāʾ says it is a singular noun in his view; whoever puts kasra says it is a feminine plural in his view, like Zaynabāt and Hindāt. This is ascribed to Sībawayh, because he said, «It is like bayḍāt»; so it was ascribed to him that it is a plural of that, until some grammarians said: its singular is hayha, like bayḍa. That is nothing; rather its singular is hayhāt. They said: and on his principle one ought to say hayhayāt, turning the alif of hayhāt into a yāʾ because it exceeds four letters, like malhayāt, maghwayāt and marmayāt; because it is among the doubled quadriliterals of the yāʾ, of the type ḥāḥaytu and ṣīṣiya. Its root is on the pattern of qalqala and ḥaqḥaqa, then the yāʾ turned into alif because it is vowelled and what precedes it has fatḥa, so it became hayhāt like salqāt and jaʿbāt, even though the yāʾ from which the alif of «salqāt» and «jaʿbāt» was turned is extra, while the yāʾ of hayhaya is radical. When it was pluralized its analogy, on the saying of arṭayāt and ʿalqayāt, would be to say hayhayāt, except that they dropped the alif for the meeting of two silent letters, since it is at the end of an indeclinable noun, as they dropped it in dhān, allatān and tān, to distinguish the alifs at the ends of indeclinables from the alifs at the ends of declinables; on this they dropped it in ulāt and dhawāt, so as to differ from the yāʾ of ḥaṣayāt and nawayāt.
They said: whoever puts fatḥa on the tāʾ of «hayhāt» should write it with a hāʾ, because it is in a singular like tamra and nawāt; and whoever puts kasra should write it with a tāʾ because it is in a plural like Hindāt. The ruling of pause is likewise equal. No heed is paid to the dialect of «kayfa l-ikhwatu wa-l-akhawāh» nor «hādhihi thamaratʻ», for their rarity. It was written in the muṣḥaf with a hāʾ.
The readers differed in pausing on it: some followed the writing and paused with the hāʾ, namely al-Kisāʾī and al-Bazzī from Ibn Kathīr. Some paused with the tāʾ, namely the rest. It ought to have been that most pause with the hāʾ for two reasons. One: conformity with the writing. The second: that they said the one with fatḥa is a singular noun whose root is hayhaya, like zalzala and qalqala, from the doubled quadriliterals. It has been said earlier that a singular is paused on at its feminine tāʾ with a hāʾ.
As for the tanwīn, it is on the principle of tanwīn of verbal nouns: its entering indicates indefiniteness, and its leaving indicates definiteness. Al-Qaysī said: «Whoever gives tanwīn holds it indefinite and conceives the meaning of an indefinite maṣdar, as though he said "remoteness, remoteness"; whoever does not give tanwīn holds it definite and conceives the meaning of a definite maṣdar, as though he said "the remoteness, the remoteness", making tanwīn the sign of indefiniteness and its absence the sign of definiteness.» End. Tanwīn of indefiniteness is found only in two kinds: verbal nouns and nouns of sounds, such as Sībawayhi and Sībawayhin, and it is not analogical, meaning you may not give tanwīn to whatever you like of them, but what is heard with tanwīn is held to be indefinite. What is said about the readings above is: whoever gives tanwīn makes it for indefiniteness as stated, and whoever does not give tanwīn makes its absence for definiteness. Whoever puts fatḥa does so for lightness and for conformity; whoever puts kasra, on the original of the meeting of two silent letters; whoever puts ḍamma, by likening it to qablu and baʿdu; whoever makes sukūn, because the original of indeclinability is sukūn; whoever pauses with the hāʾ, for conformity with the writing; whoever pauses with the tāʾ, on the original, whether the tāʾ has kasra or fatḥa, because the apparent is that they are the same, and that is only from the variation of dialects, even if what is transmitted of Sībawayh's school is what was stated earlier. This is how the above readings ought to be explained.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said regarding one who gave ḍamma and tanwīn: «It is an independent declinable noun, nominative by inceptive, its khabar being «لِما تُوْعَدون», that is: remoteness for your promise, as you say: success for your effort.» Al-Rāzī said in «al-Lawāmiḥ»: «As for one who read it nominative with tanwīn, it is possible that they are two declinable nouns nominative [by the inceptive], their khabar being from the prepositions, meaning: remoteness for what you are promised. The repetition is for emphasis. It is also possible that they are a verbal noun, and the ḍamma is for indeclinability like ḥawb in driving camels, but he gave it tanwīn as indefinite.» I say: Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū l-Faḍl ought also to have made it a noun in the accusative case with tanwīn, as a maṣdar occurring in the place of the verb.
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «هَيْهات هَيْهات ما تُوْعدون» without the genitive lām. It is clear and supports the one who claims its redundancy in the reading of the majority.
And «ما» in «لِما تُوْعدون» may be maṣdarī, that is: "for your promise", and may mean "that which", and the returning pronoun is omitted, that is: "you are promised it".
[Translator's note: the glosses for the verses (especially 3415 and 3416) are tentative since the verse texts are partial or obscure; the phrase «ذان واللتان وتان» and «كيف الإخوة والأخواه» are quoted as in the source.]

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {إِنْ هِيَ}: «هي» is a pronoun explained by the context of the speech, that is: "Your life is nothing but our life". Al-Zamakhsharī said: «This is a pronoun whose referent is not known except through the explanation that follows it. Its original is "there is nothing but our worldly life", so he put «hiya» in the place of "our life" because the khabar indicates it and explains it. From it are «hiya l-nafs tataḥammalu mā ḥummilat» ("it is the soul, it bears what it is made to bear") and «hiya l-ʿarab taqūlu mā shāʾat» ("it is the Arabs, they say what they wish").» Some have made this category among those explained by what follows, in form and order, and ascribed it to al-Zamakhsharī in connection with these words which I quoted from him; it has no connection with that.
His saying: {نَمُوتُ وَنَحْيَا}: an explicative sentence for what they claimed, that their life is nothing but this. Some claimed that in it is evidence that the wāw does not imply order, since the meaning is "we live and we die", as that is what happens. But there is no evidence in it, because the apparent sense is: some of us die and others live, and so on; they are alluding to the passing of a generation and its succession by another in its place. It was also said: we die and our sons live. And it was said: the people believe in return (rajʿa), that is: we die and then live after that death.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ (١)).
His saying, the Exalted: (قَدْ أَفْلَحَ): whoever casts the vowel of the hamza onto the dāl and drops it (قَدَ فْلَحَ), his reasoning is that the hamza, after its vowel was removed, was turned into an alif, and then dropped because it was quiescent and the dāl before it was originally quiescent; and the vowel of the dāl is not taken into account, because it is incidental.

ukberi-tibyan:101-101.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ فَلَا أَنْسَابَ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَلَا يَتَسَاءَلُونَ (١٠١)).
His saying, the Exalted: (يَوْمَئِذٍ): what governs the adverb of time is what governs «بَيْنَهُمْ», namely the omitted element; أَنْسَابَ may not govern it, because the noun of «لَا», when made indeclinable (mabnī), does not govern.

ukberi-tibyan:106-106.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا رَبَّنَا غَلَبَتْ عَلَيْنَا شِقْوَتُنَا وَكُنَّا قَوْمًا ضَالِّينَ (١٠٦)).
His saying, the Exalted: (شِقْوَتُنَا): it is read with kasra without an alif, and with fatḥa with an alif (شَقَاوَتُنَا); and they have one meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ الْفِرْدَوْسَ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ (١١)).
His saying, the Exalted: (هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ): the clause is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara, circumstantial), either from the agent or from the object.

ukberi-tibyan:110-110.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَاتَّخَذْتُمُوهُمْ سِخْرِيًّا حَتَّى أَنْسَوْكُمْ ذِكْرِي وَكُنْتُمْ مِنْهُمْ تَضْحَكُونَ (١١٠)).
His saying, the Exalted: (سِخْرِيًّا): it is a second object. Kasra and ḍamma (سُخْرِيًّا) are two dialectal forms. It is also said: kasra has the meaning of jesting, and ḍamma the meaning of subjugation, from التَّسْخِير; and it is also said: the reverse of that.

ukberi-tibyan:111-111.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنِّي جَزَيْتُهُمُ الْيَوْمَ بِمَا صَبَرُوا أَنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْفَائِزُونَ (١١١)).
His saying, the Exalted: (أَنَّهُمْ): it is read with fatḥa, the clause being in the position of a second object, because «جَزَى» takes two objects, as Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَزَاهُمْ بِمَا صَبَرُوا جَنَّةً).
There is another view on it, namely that it is with the implied form "because they…" (لِأَنَّهُمْ) or "with the fact that they…" (بِأَنَّهُمْ); i.e. He rewarded them with triumph for their patience. It is also read with kasra (إِنَّهُمْ), as a resumption.

ukberi-tibyan:112-115.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ كَمْ لَبِثْتُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ عَدَدَ سِنِينَ (١١٢) قَالُوا لَبِثْنَا يَوْمًا أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ فَاسْأَلِ الْعَادِّينَ (١١٣) قَالَ إِنْ لَبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ (١١٤) أَفَحَسِبْتُمْ أَنَّمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ عَبَثًا وَأَنَّكُمْ إِلَيْنَا لَا تُرْجَعُونَ (١١٥))
His saying, the Exalted: (قَالَ كَمْ لَبِثْتُمْ): it is read in the form of the past, i.e. the questioner said to them;
and in the form of the imperative (قُلْ), i.e. Allah says to the questioner: say to them.
(كَمْ): an adverb (ẓarf) for لَبِثْتُمْ; i.e. how many years, or the like.
(عَدَدَ): a badal (substitute) from «كَمْ»; it is read anomalously (shādhdh) عَدَدًا, with nunation.
(سِنِينَ): a badal from it.
(الْعَادِّينَ) with doubling, from الْعَدَد ("counting"); and undoubled (الْعَادِينَ) with the meaning of الْعَادِيِّين, i.e. the ancients, as you say "this is an ancient (عَادِيَة) well"; i.e. "ask those who preceded us". One of the two yāʾs of relation (nisba) was dropped, as they said الْأَشْعَرُونَ, and the other was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. (إِلَّا قَلِيلًا): i.e. a short time, or a short stay.
The apodosis (jawāb) of «لَوْ» is omitted; i.e. "if you had known how long your stay was, you would not have answered with this duration". (عَبَثًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

ukberi-tibyan:116-116.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَتَعَالَى اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ الْحَقُّ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْكَرِيمِ (١١٦)).
His saying, the Exalted: (رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْكَرِيمِ): like His saying, the Exalted, in al-Baqara: (لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الرَّحْمَنُ الرَّحِيمُ), and it has been mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:117-117.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَنْ يَدْعُ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ لَا بُرْهَانَ لَهُ بِهِ فَإِنَّمَا حِسَابُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ إِنَّهُ لَا يُفْلِحُ الْكَافِرُونَ (١١٧)).
His saying, the Exalted: (لَا بُرْهَانَ لَهُ بِهِ): an adjective (ṣifa) of إِلَه, and the apodosis (jawāb) is «فَإِنَّمَا حِسَابُهُ».
His saying: (إِنَّهُ لَا يُفْلِحُ) is with kasra, as a resumption; and with fatḥa (أَنَّهُ), with the implied form "with the fact that he…" (بِأَنَّهُ); i.e. he is requited with not succeeding. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ مِنْ سُلَالَةٍ مِنْ طِينٍ (١٢)).
His saying, the Exalted: (مِنْ سُلَالَةٍ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to خَلَقْنَا. (مِنْ طِينٍ): attached to something omitted, because it is an adjective (ṣifa) of سُلَالَة; and it may be attached to the meaning of سُلَالَة, because it has the meaning of مَسْلُولَة ("drawn out").

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَاهُ نُطْفَةً فِي قَرَارٍ مَكِينٍ ثُمَّ خَلَقْنَا النُّطْفَةَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقْنَا الْعَلَقَةَ مُضْغَةً فَخَلَقْنَا الْمُضْغَةَ عِظَامًا فَكَسَوْنَا الْعِظَامَ لَحْمًا ثُمَّ أَنْشَأْنَاهُ خَلْقًا آخَرَ فَتَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ أَحْسَنُ الْخَالِقِينَ (١٤)).
His saying, the Exalted: (خَلَقْنَا النُّطْفَةَ عَلَقَةً): «خَلَقْنَا» has the meaning of "We made into" (صَيَّرْنَا); that is why it takes two objects in the accusative.
(الْعِظَامَ): in the plural, according to the original, and in the singular (الْعَظْمَ), because it is a genus.
(أَحْسَنُ الْخَالِقِينَ): a badal (substitute), or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); it is not an adjective (ṣifa), because it is indefinite even though it is put in construct, since the muḍāf ilayhi stands in place of «مِنْ»; and so it is with the whole category of «أَفْعَلُ مِنْكَ» (the comparative).

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ لَمَيِّتُونَ (١٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ): what governs it is «مَيِّتُونَ», and the lām here does not prevent the governing.

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَنْزَلْنَا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً بِقَدَرٍ فَأَسْكَنَّاهُ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَإِنَّا عَلَى ذَهَابٍ بِهِ لَقَادِرُونَ (١٨)).
His saying, the Exalted: (بِهِ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to ذَهَاب. And «عَلَى» is attached to «قَادِرُونَ».

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَشَجَرَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ طُورِ سَيْنَاءَ تَنْبُتُ بِالدُّهْنِ وَصِبْغٍ لِلْآكِلِينَ (٢٠)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَشَجَرَةً): i.e. "and We produced a tree"; so it is conjoined to «جَنَّاتٍ».
(سَيْنَاءَ): it is read with kasra on the sīn (سِينَاءَ); on this reading the hamza is a radical, like حِمْلَاق, and it is not for the feminine, since there is nothing in the language like سَنَا - سَيَا [Translator's note: so in the source; the point is that no root exists from which a feminine pattern fiʿlāʾ could be formed here]. It is a diptote because it is the name of a tract of land, so it has definiteness and femininity; and it may also have foreignness (ʿujma).
It is also read with fatḥa on the sīn; on this reading the hamza is for the feminine, since there is no faʿlāl pattern with fatḥa in the language. What al-Farrāʾ reported of their saying "a she-camel in which there is خَزْعَال (lameness)" is not established, and if it were established it would be anomalous (shādhdh) and nothing would be based on it.
His saying, the Exalted: (تَنْبُتُ): it is read with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the bāʾ (تُنْبِتُ), and there are two views on it. First: it is transitive, and the object is omitted, its implied form being "it produces its fruit" or "its harvest"; on this view the bāʾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from what is omitted, i.e. "with oil in it", as you say "Zayd went out with his clothes". It is also said: the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), so there is then no omission; rather, the object is الدُّهْن. The second view: it is intransitive; one says نَبَتَ الْبَقْلُ and أَنْبَتَ with the same meaning; on this view the bāʾ is a ḥāl. It is also said: it is an object; i.e. it grows because of the oil.
It is also read with ḍamma on the tāʾ and fatḥa on the bāʾ (تُنْبَتُ), and that is clear.
It is also read with fatḥa on the tāʾ and ḍamma on the bāʾ (تَنْبُتُ), and it is like the second view mentioned.
(وَصِبْغٍ): conjoined to الدُّهْن.
It has been read, among the anomalous readings, in the accusative (وَصِبْغًا), conjoined to the position of بِالدُّهْنِ.

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنَّ لَكُمْ فِي الْأَنْعَامِ لَعِبْرَةً نُسْقِيكُمْ مِمَّا فِي بُطُونِهَا وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَنَافِعُ كَثِيرَةٌ وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ (٢١)).
His saying, the Exalted: (نُسْقِيكُمْ): it is read with nūn, and this has been mentioned in al-Naḥl; and with tāʾ (تُسْقِيكُمْ), in which case it contains the pronoun of the livestock, and it is resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْهِ أَنِ اصْنَعِ الْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا فَإِذَا جَاءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ التَّنُّورُ فَاسْلُكْ فِيهَا مِنْ كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَنْ سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ الْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَا تُخَاطِبْنِي فِي الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا إِنَّهُمْ مُغْرَقُونَ (٢٧)).
His saying, the Exalted: (بِأَعْيُنِنَا): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); i.e. guarded.
(مِنْ كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ): has been mentioned in Hūd.

ukberi-tibyan:29-30.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقُلْ رَبِّ أَنْزِلْنِي مُنْزَلًا مُبَارَكًا وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الْمُنْزِلِينَ (٢٩) إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ وَإِنْ كُنَّا لَمُبْتَلِينَ (٣٠)).
His saying, the Exalted: (مُنْزَلًا): it is read with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the zāy (مَنْزِلًا); it is a place, or the maṣdar (verbal noun) of نَزَلَ [Translator's note: the source prints نَزَّلَ], which is the reflexive-compliant (muṭāwiʿ) of أَنْزَلْتُهُ.
It is also read with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the zāy (مُنْزَلًا), and it is a maṣdar with the meaning of الْإِنْزَال; it may also be a place, as you say "I set down at the place", so it is مُنْزَل.
(وَإِنْ كُنَّا): i.e. "indeed we were"; so it is lightened from the heavy (inna), and this has been mentioned in more than one place.

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مُتُّمْ وَكُنْتُمْ تُرَابًا وَعِظَامًا أَنَّكُمْ مُخْرَجُونَ (٣٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتُّمْ): concerning the iʿrāb of this verse there are several views:
The first: that the noun of the first «أَنَّ» is omitted (a muḍāf), with the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place, its implied form being "that your being brought out…" (أَنَّ إِخْرَاجَكُمْ); and «إِذَا» is the khabar (predicate); and «أَنَّكُمْ مُخْرَجُونَ» is a repetition, because «أَنَّ» with what it governs is for emphasis, or to indicate what is omitted. The second: that the noun of «أَنَّ» is the kāf and mīm, and «إِذَا» is conditional, its apodosis (jawāb) being omitted, its implied form being "that you, when you die, it will come about that you are brought out"; so the second أَنَّكُمْ with what it governs is the fāʿil (agent) of the apodosis of إِذَا, and the whole clause is the khabar of the first أَنَّ. The third: that the khabar of the first is مُخْرَجُونَ, and the second أَنَّ is repeated alone for emphasis; that is permissible when the speech has become long, just as it is permissible with the kasra form in His saying, the Exalted: (ثُمَّ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لِلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا) and (ثُمَّ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لِلَّذِينَ عَمِلُوا السُّوءَ); this has been mentioned in al-Naḥl. The fourth: that the khabar of the first «أَنَّ» is omitted because the khabar of the second indicates it. «إِذَا» cannot be the khabar of the first (on this view), because it is an adverb of time and its noun denotes a concrete entity (juththa). As for what governs «إِذَا», it is omitted: on the first view the implied element is (a word) of settledness (al-istiqrār); on the second view it is governed by its omitted apodosis; and on the third and fourth it is governed by what the khabar of the second indicates. «مُتُّمْ» does not govern it, because it (إِذَا) is put in construct with it.

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هَيْهَاتَ هَيْهَاتَ لِمَا تُوعَدُونَ (٣٦)).
His saying, the Exalted: (هَيْهَاتَ): it is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl), a statement standing in the place of بَعُدَ ("it is far"). Concerning its fāʿil (agent) there are two views. First: it is latent, its implied form being "far is the belief in what you are promised", or "its truth", or "its occurrence", and the like. Second: its fāʿil is «مَا», and the lām is redundant (zāʾida); i.e. "far is what you are promised of the resurrection".
Some said: «هَيْهَاتَ» has the meaning of الْبُعْد ("farness"), so its position is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «لِمَا تُوعَدُونَ» is the khabar (predicate); this is weak. On the first view «هَيْهَاتَ» has no grammatical position. There are several readings of it: fatḥa without nunation, as being singular; with nunation, intending intensification; kasra without nunation, and with nunation, as being a feminine plural; and ḍamma in both ways, likened to قَبْلُ and بَعْدُ.
It is also read هَيْهَاهْ, with hāʾ, both in pause and in connected speech.
It is also read أَيْهَاهْ, with hamza substituted for the first hāʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:40-40.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ عَمَّا قَلِيلٍ لَيُصْبِحُنَّ نَادِمِينَ (٤٠)).
His saying, the Exalted: (عَمَّا قَلِيلٍ): «مَا» is redundant (zāʾida).
It is also said: it has the meaning of "a thing" or "a time". It is also said: (قَلِيلٍ is) a badal (substitute) from it.
In the speech there is an omitted oath, whose answer is «لَيُصْبِحُنَّ».
«عَنْ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يُصْبِحُنَّ; the lām did not prevent this as the lām of the mubtadaʾ (lām al-ibtidāʾ) prevents it. They permitted زَيْدٌ لَأَضْرِبَنَّ ("Zayd, I shall surely strike"), because the lām is for emphasis, so it is like قَدْ, and like the lām of emphasis in the khabar of إِنَّ, as in His saying: (بِلِقَاءِ رَبِّهِمْ لَكَافِرُونَ).
It is also said: the lām here prevents fronting except with adverbs, for latitude is allowed with them.

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ أَرْسَلْنَا رُسُلَنَا تَتْرَى كُلَّمَا جَاءَ أُمَّةً رَسُولُهَا كَذَّبُوهُ فَأَتْبَعْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ بَعْضًا وَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ أَحَادِيثَ فَبُعْدًا لِقَوْمٍ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ (٤٤)).
His saying, the Exalted: (تَتْرَى): the tāʾ is a substitute for wāw, because it is from الْمُوَاتَرَة, which is succession; that is from their saying "they came in one وَتِيرَة", i.e. in one manner. It is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. in succession; strictly speaking it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl. It is also said: it is an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a successive sending".
Concerning its alif there are three views. First: it is for attachment (ilḥāq) to the pattern of جَعْفَر, like the alif in أَرْطَى; that is why it takes nunation [Translator's note: the printed text has تُؤَنَّثُ ("is made feminine"); تُنَوَّنُ ("takes nunation") is evidently intended, matching the third view] according to those who treat it as fully declinable. Second: it is a substitute for nunation. Third: it is for the feminine, like سَكْرَى; that is why it does not take nunation according to those who treat it as a diptote.

ukberi-tibyan:45-45.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ أَرْسَلْنَا مُوسَى وَأَخَاهُ هَارُونَ بِآيَاتِنَا وَسُلْطَانٍ مُبِينٍ (٤٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (هَارُونَ): it is a badal (substitute) from «أَخَاهُ».

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَقَالُوا أَنُؤْمِنُ لِبَشَرَيْنِ مِثْلِنَا وَقَوْمُهُمَا لَنَا عَابِدُونَ (٤٧)).
His saying, the Exalted: (مِثْلِنَا): it was not put in the dual only because «مِثْل» has the status of a maṣdar (verbal noun); its dual and plural do occur, in His saying (يَرَوْنَهُمْ مِثْلَيْهِمْ) and in His saying, the Exalted: (ثُمَّ لَا يَكُونُوا أَمْثَالَكُمْ).
It is also said: it was kept singular only because what is meant is likeness in humanity, not quantity.
It is also said: the singular sufficed in place of the dual.

ukberi-tibyan:5-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حَافِظُونَ (٥) إِلَّا عَلَى أَزْوَاجِهِمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ (٦)).
His saying, the Exalted: (إِلَّا عَلَى أَزْوَاجِهِمْ): in the position of the accusative, governed by «حَافِظُونَ» according to the meaning, because the meaning is: they guarded them from every private part except from the private parts of their spouses.
It is also said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial); i.e. they guarded them in every state except in this state.
It may not be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «مَلُومِينَ», for two reasons: first, what comes after «إِنَّ» does not govern what precedes it; second, the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern what precedes it.
«عَلَى» is attached to حَافِظُونَ only according to the meaning; and it may be attached to a verb indicated by «مَلُومِينَ», i.e. "except with their spouses they are not blamed".

ukberi-tibyan:50-50.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَعَلْنَا ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ وَأُمَّهُ آيَةً وَآوَيْنَاهُمَا إِلَى رَبْوَةٍ ذَاتِ قَرَارٍ وَمَعِينٍ (٥٠)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَأُمَّهُ آيَةً): has been mentioned in al-Anbiyāʾ.
His saying, the Exalted: (وَمَعِينٍ): there are two views on it. First: it is of the pattern faʿīl from الْمَعْن, which is a small thing; and from it is الْمَاعُون. It is also said: الْمَاعُون is water; so the mīm is a radical. Second: the mīm is augmentative, and it is from عِنْتُهُ, "I saw it with my eye"; its original form is مَعْيُون.

ukberi-tibyan:52-53.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنَّ هَذِهِ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً وَأَنَا رَبُّكُمْ فَاتَّقُونِ (٥٢) فَتَقَطَّعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ زُبُرًا كُلُّ حِزْبٍ بِمَا لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ (٥٣))
His saying, the Exalted: (وَإِنَّ هَذِهِ): it is read with fatḥa on the hamza (وَأَنَّ), and there are three views on it. First: its implied form is "and because…", the implied lām being attached (mutaʿalliq) to «فَاتَّقُونِ», i.e. "so fear Me, because this…". The position of أَنَّ is accusative, or genitive, according to the disagreement we have reported in more than one place. Second: it is conjoined to what precedes it, its implied form being "I am Knowing of what you do, and of the fact that this…". Third: there is an omission in the speech, i.e. "and know that this…".
It is also read with the nūn undoubled (وَأَنْ), and it is lightened from the heavy (anna).
It is also read with kasra, as a resumption.
(أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً): has been mentioned in al-Anbiyāʾ, as has «فَتَقَطَّعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ». (زُبُرًا), with two ḍammas, is the plural of زَبُور, like رَسُول and رُسُل.
It is also read with the bāʾ quiescent (زُبْرًا), with this meaning.
It is also read with fatḥa on the bāʾ (زُبَرًا), and it is the plural of زُبْرَة, which is a piece or a party. The accusative on the first view is as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أَمْرَهُمْ», i.e. like books. It is also said: from the agent pronoun. It is also said: it is a second object of تَقَطَّعُوا. On the second view, it is a ḥāl from the agent.

ukberi-tibyan:55-56.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّمَا نُمِدُّهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ مَالٍ وَبَنِينَ (٥٥) نُسَارِعُ لَهُمْ فِي الْخَيْرَاتِ بَل لَا يَشْعُرُونَ (٥٦))
His saying, the Exalted: (أَنَّمَا): (مَا) has the meaning of الَّذِي, and the khabar (predicate) of أَنَّ is «نُسَارِعُ لَهُمْ», with the returning pronoun omitted; i.e. "We hasten for them in it". The khabar may not be «مِنْ مَالٍ», because if it were «مِنْ مَالٍ», that would not be held against them; what is held against them is only their belief that those riches are good for them.
نُسَارِعُ is also read with yāʾ and with nūn, and with the agent unnamed, and نُسْرِعُ without an alif.

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْتُونَ مَا آتَوْا وَقُلُوبُهُمْ وَجِلَةٌ أَنَّهُمْ إِلَى رَبِّهِمْ رَاجِعُونَ (٦٠)).
His saying, the Exalted: (مَا آتَوْا): «مَا» has the meaning of الَّذِي, and the returning pronoun is omitted; i.e. "they give what they give".
It is also read: أَتَوْا, without prolongation; i.e. "what they came to (do)".
(أَنَّهُمْ…): i.e. "fearful of their returning to their Lord"; so the preposition was dropped.

ukberi-tibyan:61-61.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أُولَئِكَ يُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْرَاتِ وَهُمْ لَهَا سَابِقُونَ (٦١)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَهُمْ لَهَا): i.e. "for their sake". It is also said: the implied form is "and they race them", i.e. they hasten to them; so it is in the position of the object. The like of it is (هُمْ لَهَا عَامِلُونَ), i.e. for its sake, and it is what they do.

ukberi-tibyan:64-64.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (حَتَّى إِذَا أَخَذْنَا مُتْرَفِيهِمْ بِالْعَذَابِ إِذَا هُمْ يَجْأَرُونَ (٦٤)).
His saying, the Exalted: (إِذَا): it is of surprise (mufājaʾa), and its rule has been mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:66-67.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَدْ كَانَتْ آيَاتِي تُتْلَى عَلَيْكُمْ فَكُنْتُمْ عَلَى أَعْقَابِكُمْ تَنْكِصُونَ (٦٦) مُسْتَكْبِرِينَ بِهِ سَامِرًا تَهْجُرُونَ (٦٧)).
His saying, the Exalted: (عَلَى أَعْقَابِكُمْ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent in «تَنْكِصُونَ»; and His saying, the Exalted, «مُسْتَكْبِرِينَ» is another ḥāl.
The hāʾ in «بِهِ» refers to the Mighty Qurʾān. It is also said: to the Prophet, upon him be blessing and peace. It is also said: to the command of Allah the Exalted. It is also said: to the House; on this view it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «سَامِرًا», i.e. "you hold night talk around the House".
It is also said: (attached) to the Qurʾān. سَامِرًا is also a ḥāl, and it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), as in their saying قُمْ قَائِمًا ("stand up standing"); maṣdars do occur in the form of the active participle, such as الْعَاقِبَة and الْعَافِيَة. It is also said: it is a singular in the place of a plural.
It has also been read: (سُمَّرًا), the plural of سَامِر, like شَاهِد and شُهَّد.
(تَهْجُرُونَ): in the position of a ḥāl from the pronoun in سَامِرًا. It is read with fatḥa on the tāʾ, from your saying هَجَرَ يَهْجُرُ, when one talks nonsense. It is also said: they forsake the Qurʾān.
It is also read with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the jīm (تُهْجِرُونَ), from أَهْجَرَ, when one utters الْهُجْر, which is obscenity. It is also read with doubling (تُهَجِّرُونَ), and it has the meaning of the undoubled form. Allah the Exalted said: (أَمْ تَسْأَلُهُمْ خَرْجًا فَخَرَاجُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الرَّازِقِينَ (٧٢)).
His saying, the Exalted: (خَرْجًا): it is read without an alif in the first and with an alif in the second.
It is also read without an alif in both, and with an alif in both; and they have the same meaning.
It is also said: الْخَرْج is the wage, and الْخَرَاج is what is levied on land and on persons.

ukberi-tibyan:74-74.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ عَنِ الصِّرَاطِ لَنَاكِبُونَ (٧٤)).
His saying, the Exalted: (عَنِ الصِّرَاطِ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to «نَاكِبُونَ», and the lām does not prevent that.

ukberi-tibyan:76-76.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ أَخَذْنَاهُمْ بِالْعَذَابِ فَمَا اسْتَكَانُوا لِرَبِّهِمْ وَمَا يَتَضَرَّعُونَ (٧٦)).
His saying, the Exalted: (فَمَا اسْتَكَانُوا): has been mentioned in Āl ʿImrān, together with the disagreement about it.

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَنْشَأَ لَكُمُ السَّمْعَ وَالْأَبْصَارَ وَالْأَفْئِدَةَ قَلِيلًا مَا تَشْكُرُونَ (٧٨)).
His saying, the Exalted: (قَلِيلًا مَا تَشْكُرُونَ): has been mentioned at the beginning of al-Aʿrāf.

ukberi-tibyan:84-85.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ لِمَنِ الْأَرْضُ وَمَنْ فِيهَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ (٨٤) سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ قُلْ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ (٨٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ): the first occurrence is with the lām in the reading of the majority; it is the answer to what contains the lām, namely His saying, the Exalted: (لِمَنِ الْأَرْضُ), and it matches both wording and meaning.
It has also been read without the lām (اللَّهُ), construed according to the meaning, because the meaning of «لِمَنِ الْأَرْضُ» is "who is the Lord of the earth?", so the answer is "Allah", i.e. "He is Allah".
As for the other two occurrences, they are read without the lām, construed according to the wording, being the answer to His saying, the Exalted: (مَنْ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ); and «مَنْ بِيَدِهِ مَلَكُوتُ» (is answered) with the lām according to the meaning, because the meaning of His saying «مَنْ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ» is "to whom do the heavens belong?". [Translator's note: the passage is compressed in the source; it describes the reading without lām in the last two answers (vv. 87, 89) and the majority reading with lām (لِلَّهِ) construed by meaning.]

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِأَمَانَاتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ رَاعُونَ (٨) وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلَى صَلَوَاتِهِمْ يُحَافِظُونَ (٩)).
His saying, the Exalted: (لِأَمَانَاتِهِمْ): it is read in the plural, because they are many, as in His saying, the Exalted: (أَنْ تُؤَدُّوا الْأَمَانَاتِ إِلَى أَهْلِهَا); and in the singular (لِأَمَانَتِهِمْ), because it is a genus, so in being singular it is like عَهْدِهِمْ. The like of it is (صَلَوَاتِهِمْ), in the singular and the plural.

ukberi-tibyan:92-92.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (عَالِمِ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ فَتَعَالَى عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ (٩٢)).
His saying, the Exalted: (عَالِمِ الْغَيْبِ): it is read in the genitive as an adjective (ṣifa) or a badal (substitute) of the name of Allah the Exalted before it; and in the nominative (عَالِمُ), i.e. "He is the Knower".

ukberi-tibyan:94-95.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رَبِّ فَلَا تَجْعَلْنِي فِي الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ (٩٤) وَإِنَّا عَلَى أَنْ نُرِيَكَ مَا نَعِدُهُمْ لَقَادِرُونَ (٩٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (فَلَا تَجْعَلْنِي): the fāʾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition, namely His saying, the Exalted: (إِمَّا تُرِيَنِّي), and the vocative is parenthetical between them. (عَلَى): attached (mutaʿalliq) to «قَادِرُونَ».

ukberi-tibyan:99-99.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (حَتَّى إِذَا جَاءَ أَحَدَهُمُ الْمَوْتُ قَالَ رَبِّ ارْجِعُونِ (٩٩)).
His saying, the Exalted: (ارْجِعُونِ): there are three views on it. First: it is put in the plural for majesty, as Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ), and as in His saying, the Exalted: (أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَخْرَجْنَا). Second: he meant "O angels of my Lord, send me back". Third: by the plural form he indicated repetition of the saying, as though he said "send me back, send me back".

zajjaj:111-111.t: His saying: ﴿إنِّي جَزَيْتُهُمُ اليَوْمَ بِما صَبَرُوا أنَّهم هُمُ الفائِزُونَ﴾ — the kasra (reading «إنَّهم») is better, because the kasra carries the meaning "إنِّي جَزَيْتُهم بِما صَبَرُوا" (I have rewarded them for their patience); then He gave a fresh statement and said: "إنَّهم هُمُ الفائِزُونَ" (truly they are the triumphant). The fatḥa is good and sound, with the meaning: "إنِّي جَزَيْتُهم لِأنَّهم هُمُ الفائِزُونَ" (I have rewarded them because they are the triumphant). There is another possibility in it: the meaning is "جَزَيْتُهُمُ الفَوْزَ" (I have rewarded them with triumph), because the meaning of "أنَّهم هُمُ الفائِزُونَ" is "فَوْزَهم" (their triumph), so the meaning becomes: "جَزَيْتُهم فَوْزَهم" (I have rewarded them with their triumph).

zajjaj:112-112.t: His saying: ﴿قالَ كَمْ لَبِثْتُمْ في الأرْضِ عَدَدَ سِنِينَ﴾ — "كَمْ" is in the position of the accusative (naṣb), governed by His saying "لَبِثْتُمْ", and "عَدَدَ سِنِينَ" is accusative (manṣūb) by "كَمْ". It is also permissible to say "كَمْ لَبِتُّمْ في الأرْضِ", with the tāʾ doubled, and the same is permissible in the reply.

zajjaj:113-113.t:
﴿قالُوا لَبِثْنا يَوْمًا أوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ﴾, and "لُبِثْنا" [is also said]. [Translator's note: the source records the form «لُبِثْنا» without further comment.]
His saying: ﴿فاسْألِ العادِّينَ﴾, that is: ask the angels who keep count of how long we remained.

zajjaj:114-114.t: ﴿قالَ إنْ لَبِثْتُمْ إلا قَلِيلا لَوْ أنَّكم كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — its meaning is: "ما لَبِثْتُمْ إلّا قَلِيلًا" (you remained only a little while).

zajjaj:115-115.t: His saying: ﴿وَأنَّكم إلَيْنا لا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾, and "تَرْجِعُونَ" [is also read].

zajjaj:117-117.t: His saying: ﴿فَإنَّما حِسابُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ إنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ الكافِرُونَ﴾ — the interpretation is: his reckoning is with his Lord, for indeed the disbelievers will not prosper. The meaning is: "اَلَّذِي لَهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ أنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ" (what is due to him with his Lord is that he will not prosper). It is permissible to read "أنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ الكافِرُونَ" with fatḥa on "أنَّ". It is also possible that it means "فَأنَّما حِسابُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ فَيُجازِيهِ عَلَيْهِ" (his reckoning is with his Lord, and He will requite him for it), as He said: ﴿ثُمَّ إنَّ عَلَيْنا حِسابَهُمْ﴾ [al-Ghāshiya: 26].

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat "al-Muʾminūn" (The Believers)
Meccan
﷽
From the sura in which the believers are mentioned, His saying, the Exalted: ﴿قَدْ أفْلَحَ المُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, i.e. they have attained everlasting continuance in good. Whoever reads "قَدْ أُفْلِحَ المُؤْمِنُونَ" (passive), its meaning is "they have been brought to success". It is narrated from Kaʿb al-Ḥabr that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, created only three things with His hand: He created Ādam ﷺ with His hand, He created the Garden of ʿAdn with His hand, and He wrote the Torah with His hand. Then He said to the Garden of ʿAdn: (Speak), and it said: ﴿قَدْ أفْلَحَ المُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, because of the honour it saw in it for its people. "المُؤْمِنُون" are those who affirm the truth of what came from Allah, and that He is One, without partner, and that Muhammad ﷺ is His Prophet.

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الوارِثُونَ﴾, i.e. whoever is described by what has preceded — faith and acting upon what is binding on the believer — those are the inheritors.

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ الفِرْدَوْسَ﴾: it is narrated that Allah, exalted be His praise, appointed for every person a house in Paradise and a house in the Fire. Whoever does the deeds of the people of the Fire, his house in Paradise is inherited by one who did the deeds of the people of Paradise; and whoever does the deeds of the people of Paradise, his house in the Fire is inherited by one who did the deeds of the people of the Fire. "الفِرْدَوْس": its origin is Greek (Rūmī), Arabicised, and it is "the garden (البُسْتان)"; thus it came in the exegesis. It has also been said that the Arabs know (the word) firdaws, and a place with grapevines is called a "firdaws". Abū Isḥāq (al-Zajjāj) said: We have related from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, in his book "Kitāb al-Tafsīr" — which his son ʿAbd Allāh licensed me (to relate) from him — that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, built the Garden of Firdaws with one brick of gold and one brick of silver, and made its mountains of pungent musk. And we have related from someone else that Allah, exalted be His praise, swept the Garden of Firdaws with His hand, and built it with one brick of refined gold and one brick of scattered musk, and planted in it the finest fruit and the finest fragrant plants.

zajjaj:12-12.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنا الإنْسانَ مِن سُلالَةٍ مِن طِينٍ﴾: "سُلالَة" is on the pattern "فُعالَة". So Allah created Ādam, peace be upon him, from clay.

zajjaj:13-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلْناهُ نُطْفَةً﴾: on this view it means the offspring of Ādam. It has also been said: "مِن سُلالَةٍ مِن طِينٍ" means from the semen of Ādam ﷺ. "سُلالَة" is the small amount of what slips out (يَنْسَلّ); everything built on the pattern "فُعالَة" denotes a small amount, such as "الفُضالَة" (leftover), "النُّخالَة" (bran) and "القُلامَة" (nail-parings); its analogy is on this basis.
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ خَلَقْنا النُّطْفَةَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقْنا العَلَقَةَ مُضْغَةً فَخَلَقْنا المُضْغَةَ عِظامًا فَكَسَوْنا العِظامَ لَحْمًا﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 14] is read in four ways. One of them is what we have mentioned; it is also read "فَخَلَقْنا المُضْغَةَ عَظْمًا فَكَسَوْنا العَظْمَ لَحْمًا"; and it is read "فَخَلَقْنا المُضْغَةَ عِظامًا فَكَسَوْنا العَظْمَ لَحْمًا"; and it is read "فَخَلَقْنا المُضْغَةَ عَظْمًا فَكَسَوْنا العِظامَ لَحْمًا". The singular and the plural are both permissible here, because it is known that a human being has bones. When it is mentioned in the singular, that is because it indicates the plural, and because the flesh is with it while its form is singular; so it is known that "العَظْم" is meant as "العِظام". Even stronger than this is permissible in the singular when there is in the speech an indication of the plural. The poet said:
؎فِي حَلْقِكم عَظْمٌ وقَدْ شَجِينا
(In your throat is a bone, and we have choked.)
He means: in your throats are bones.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ أنْشَأْناهُ خَلْقًا آخَرَ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 14]: there are three views on it. It has been said: he was made male or female; it has been said: the spirit was breathed into him; and it has been said: hair was made to grow on him. It is narrated «that ʿUmar was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when this verse was revealed, and ʿUmar said: "فَتَبارَكَ اللَّهُ أحْسَنُ الخالِقِينَ" (So blessed is Allah, the best of creators), and he ﷺ said to ʿUmar: Allah has sealed the verse with it».

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ إنَّكم بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ لَمَيِّتُونَ﴾: "لَمائِتُونَ" is possible and "لَمَيْتُونَ" is possible, but the best of them is "لَمَيِّتُونَ", and the reading is on it. "مائِتُونَ" occurs because it is for what is in the future.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنا فَوْقَكم سَبْعَ طَرائِقَ﴾ means seven heavens; each one of them is a ṭarīqa (layer). ﴿وَما كُنّا عَنِ الخَلْقِ غافِلِينَ﴾, i.e. We were not such as to neglect guarding them, as He said: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا السَّماءَ سَقْفًا مَحْفُوظًا﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 32]. It is also possible that "وَما كُنّا عَنِ الخَلْقِ غافِلِينَ" means: "it is for Our guarding of them that We created this creation."
﴿وَأنْـزَلْنا مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً بِقَدَرٍ فَأسْكَنّاهُ في الأرْضِ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 18]: it is narrated that four rivers are from Paradise: the Tigris and the Euphrates, Sayḥān and Jayḥān. The meaning of ﴿فَأسْكَنّاهُ في الأرْضِ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 18] is: We made it settled in it, not ceasing.

zajjaj:2-2.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الَّذِينَ هم في صَلاتِهِمْ خاشِعُونَ﴾: the basic meaning of "الخُشُوع" in the language is submissiveness and humility, and the proof of that is His saying: ﴿وَخَشَعَتِ الأصْواتُ لِلرَّحْمَنِ فَلا تَسْمَعُ إلا هَمْسًا﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 108]. Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: "خاشِعُونَ" means fearful. It is narrated «from the Prophet ﷺ that when he stood in his prayer he would raise his gaze towards the sky; then when ﴿الَّذِينَ هم في صَلاتِهِمْ خاشِعُونَ﴾ was revealed», he placed his gaze on the place of his prostration.

zajjaj:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿وَشَجَرَةً تَخْرُجُ مِن طُورِ سَيْناءَ﴾: "شَجَرَةً" is accusative, conjoined to His saying: ﴿فَأنْشَأْنا لَكم بِهِ جَنّاتٍ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 19], i.e. "and We produced for you by it a tree". It is read "مِن طُورِ سِيناءَ" with fatḥa on the sīn and with kasra on the sīn. "الطُّور" is the mountain. It has been said that "سَيْناء" means stones; and it is — Allah knows best — the name of a place. Whoever says "سَيْناءَ" (with fatḥa) treats it on the pattern of "صَحْراء": it is a diptote. Whoever says "سِيناءَ" with kasra on the sīn — there is nothing in the language on the pattern "فِعْلاء" with the alif being for the feminine, because there is nothing in the language with the feminine alif on the pattern "فِعْلاء"; there are in the language words like "عِلْباء", which is fully declinable (munṣarif). But "سِيناء" here is the name of the area (البُقْعَة), so it is a diptote. His saying: ﴿تَنْبُتُ بِالدُّهْنِ﴾: one says "نَبَتَ الشَّجَرُ" and "أنْبَتَ" with one meaning. Zuhayr said:
؎رَأيْتُ ذَوِي الحاجاتِ حَوْلَ بُيُوتِهِمْ .. قَطِينًا لَهم حَتّى إذا أنْبَتَ البَقْلُ
(I saw the needy around their tents, dwelling with them, until when the herbage sprang up.)
The meaning of "تَنْبُتُ بِالدُّهْنِ" is: it grows with oil in it and oil along with it, as you say "جاءَنِي زَيْدٌ بِالسَّيْفِ", meaning "Zayd came to me with the sword with him". His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَصِبْغٍ لِلآكِلِينَ﴾: by it the olive is meant.

zajjaj:25-25.t: His saying: ﴿إنْ هو إلا رَجُلٌ بِهِ جِنَّةٌ﴾: "جِنَّة" has the meaning of "جُنُون" (madness); and "الجِنَّة" is also a name for the jinn.

zajjaj:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿وَقُلْ رَبِّ أنْـزِلْنِي مُنْـزَلا مُبارَكًا﴾: it is read both "مُنْزَلًا" and "مَنزِلًا". "المَنزِل" is a name for every place you alight in, and "المُنْزَل" is the maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of "الإنْزال": one says "أنْزَلْتُهُ إنْزالًا، ومُنْزَلًا" (I lodged him, a lodging). "مَنزَلًا" is grammatically possible but has not been read, so do not read it — in the sense of "نَزَلَتْ نُزُولًا، ومَنزَلًا" (I alighted, an alighting).

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿والَّذِينَ هم عَنِ اللَّغْوِ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾: "اللَّغْو" is all play and jest; and every act of disobedience is cast aside and void (مُلْغاة). They are the ones whom earnestness in what Allah commanded them has kept occupied away from idle talk.

zajjaj:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ هم لِلزَّكاةِ فاعِلُونَ﴾: the meaning of "فاعِلُونَ" is "giving (it)".

zajjaj:5-5.t: ﴿والَّذِينَ هم لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حافِظُونَ﴾, i.e. they guard their private parts from acts of disobedience.

zajjaj:6-6.t: ﴿إلا عَلى أزْواجِهِمْ أوْ ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُهُمْ﴾: the position of "ما" is genitive (khafḍ). "عَلى" enters here because the meaning is: "they are blamed for giving free rein to what has been forbidden to them, except with respect to their wives, for they are not blamed for what has been made lawful to them: marrying four, and those whom the right hand possesses." The meaning is: "they are blamed for anything other than their wives and what their right hands possess."

zajjaj:7-7.t: ﴿فَمَنِ ابْتَغى وراءَ ذَلِكَ﴾, i.e. whoever seeks what is beyond that, ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ العادُونَ﴾: the meaning of "العادُونَ" is the unjust, the wrongdoers, those who have transgressed in wrongdoing.

zajjaj:8-8.t: ﴿والَّذِينَ هم لأماناتِهِمْ﴾ — it is also read "لِأمانَتِهِمْ", singular and plural — ﴿وَعَهْدِهِمْ راعُونَ﴾, i.e. they take care to keep their trust and their covenant; they tend (يَرْعَوْنَ) that. The basic meaning of "الرَّعْي" in the language is taking charge of setting right whatever the shepherd (الرّاعِي) is in charge of, in everything. You say: "the imam tends his subjects (رَعِيَّتَهُ)", "the one in charge of the sheep tends his sheep", and "so-and-so tends what is between him and so-and-so", i.e. he takes care to keep right what is between him and the other.

zajjaj:9-9.t: ﴿والَّذِينَ هم عَلى صَلَواتِهِمْ﴾ — "صَلاتِهِمْ" also; both are read — ﴿يُحافِظُونَ﴾: its meaning is that they perform it at its time. Guarding the prayers is that they are prayed at their times; as for abandoning them, that falls under the chapter of leaving the religion. Those described as guarding are those who observe their times.

zajjaj:35-35.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أيَعِدُكم أنَّكم إذا مِتُّمْ﴾ — also "مُتُّمْ" — ﴿وَكُنْتُمْ تُرابًا وعِظامًا أنَّكم مُخْرَجُونَ﴾ ﴿هَيْهاتَ هَيْهاتَ لِما تُوعَدُونَ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 36]: this is the answer of the chiefs of the people of Thamūd. As for the first "أنَّكم", its position is accusative, in the sense of "does he promise you that (بِأنَّكم) when you die…". The position of the second "أنَّ", according to some, is like the position of the first; it is only mentioned as tawkīd (emphasis). The meaning on this view is: "Does he promise you that you will be brought out when you die?" Since the distance between the first and second "أنَّ" became long through His saying ﴿إذا مِتُّمْ وكُنْتُمْ تُرابًا وعِظامًا﴾, the mention of "أنَّ" was repeated, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ألَمْ يَعْلَمُوا أنَّهُ مَن يُحادِدِ اللَّهَ ورَسُولَهُ فَأنَّ لَهُ نارَ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ [al-Tawba: 63], the meaning being "then for him is the fire of Hell". This is according to the doctrine of Sībawayh.
There are two other views about it. The better of them is that the second "أنَّ" together with what it governs is in the position of the nominative, the meaning being: "Does he promise you that you — your being brought out (will be) when you die?" So "أنَّكم مُخْرَجُونَ" is in the sense of "إخْراجُكم" (your being brought out), as though it were said: "Does he promise you that you — your being brought out is at the time of your death and after your death?" What governs "إذا" is then "إخْراجُكم", "إذا" being an adverb of time (ẓarf), and the meaning is: "that you — your being brought out will occur when you die." The third is that what governs "إذا" is "مِتُّمْ", so the meaning is: "that you, whenever you die, your being brought out will occur", so that the khabar (predicate) of "إنَّ" is implied. The first two views are good. "أيَعِدُكم أنَّكم إذا مِتُّمْ أنَّكم مُخْرَجُونَ" is also grammatically possible, but it has not been read, so do not read it; the meaning of "يَعِدُكم" would then be "he says to you". But it is not permissible in recitation, because recitation is a sunna (a followed practice).

zajjaj:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿هَيْهاتَ هَيْهاتَ لِما تُوعَدُونَ﴾ is read with fatḥa on the tāʾ and with kasra on the tāʾ. "هَيْهاتٍ هَيْهاتٍ" with tanwīn is grammatically possible, and "هَيْهاتًا هَيْهاتًا" is possible. As for fatḥa and kasra without tanwīn, both are frequent in recitation, and the readers and grammarians have mentioned them; it has also been read with kasra and tanwīn. As for tanwīn with fatḥa, I know of no one who read it, so do not read it. As for the fatḥa, the pause is made on a hāʾ: you say "هَيْهاهْ هَيْهاهْ" if you give fatḥa and pause after it; [but when you give kasra] you pause on the tāʾ, whether you were one who uses tanwīn in the base form or one who does not. [Translator's note: the source reads «فَإذا فَتَحْتَ وقَفْتَ عَلى التّاءِ» ("when you give fatḥa you pause on the tāʾ"), which contradicts the preceding sentence; «كَسَرْتَ» (kasra) is evidently intended, and the bracket above supplies it.] Whoever gives it fatḥa — its position being the nominative and its interpretation being "far off is what you are promised (البُعْدُ لِما تُوعَدُونَ)" — does so because it is on a par with sound-words (al-aṣwāt) and is not derived from a verb; so "هَيْهاهْ" was made indeclinable (mabnī), just as "ذَيَّهْ" and "ذِيَّهْ" were made indeclinable. When you give it kasra you make it a plural and make it indeclinable on kasra. Sībawayh said: it is on a par with "عَلْقاة", meaning in its being feminine. Whoever makes it a plural treats it as on a par with the Arabs' saying: "اِسْتَأْصَلَ اللَّهُ عَرْقاتِهِمْ، وعَرْقاتَهم" (may Allah uproot their stock). The one who says "عَرْقاتِهِمْ" with kasra makes it a plural, its singular being as it were "عَرْقَة" and "عَرْق". On this basis the singular of "هَيْهاتَ" — even though it has no singular in actual use — is "هَيْهَة"; this is its implied form even though we do not pronounce it. As for "عَرْقات", its singular is actually spoken: one says "عِرْق", "عَرْقاة", "عَرْقَة" and "عَرْقان". It takes kasra in the plural only because the feminine plural tāʾ takes kasra in place of fatḥa in the plural: you say "مَرَرْتُ بِالهِنْداتِ" and likewise "رَأيْتُ الهِنْداتِ". One also says "أيْهاتَ" in the sense of "هَيْهاتَ"; and one says "هَيْهاتَ ما قُلْتَ" and "هَيْهاتَ لِما قُلْتَ". Whoever says "هَيْهاتَ ما قُلْتَ" means "far off is what you said", and whoever says "هَيْهاتَ لِما قُلْتَ" means "far off is your saying". And they recited:
؎فَأيْهاتَ أيْهاتَ العَقِيقُ ومَن بِهِ ∗∗∗ وأيْهاتَ خِلٌّ بِالعَقِيقِ نُواصِلُهْ
(Far, far off is al-ʿAqīq and those in it, and far off is a friend at al-ʿAqīq with whom we keep company.)
As for whoever gives "هَيْهاتَ" tanwīn, he makes it indefinite, and the meaning is: "a farness (بُعْدٌ) for what you are promised".

zajjaj:40-40.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿قالَ عَمّا قَلِيلٍ﴾ means "عَنْ قَلِيلٍ" (in a little while), and "ما" is redundant (zāʾida), with the sense of emphasis; it is as though its meaning were: "in a little while they will truly become regretful".

zajjaj:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿فَجَعَلْناهم غُثاءً﴾: "الغُثاء" is the perished, worn-out leaves of trees which, when the flood flows, you see mixed with its foam.

zajjaj:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ أرْسَلْنا رُسُلَنا تَتْرى﴾ — it is also read "تَتْرًى" (with tanwīn); "تَتْرِي", without tanwīn, with kasra, is grammatically possible but has not been read, so do not read it. Whoever reads with tanwīn means "وَتْرًا" (one by one): the tāʾ was substituted for the wāw, as they said "تَوْلَج", which is from "وَلَجَ", its base form being "وَوْلَج"; and as the poet said:
؎فَإنْ يَكُنْ أمْسى البِلى تَيْقُورِي
(If decay has become my dignified state…)
i.e. "وَيْقُورِي", which is on the pattern "فَيْعُول" from "الوَقار" (dignity); and as they said "تُجاه", which is really "وُجاه", from "المُواجَهَة" (facing). Whoever says "تَتْرى" without tanwīn makes it on the pattern "فَعْلى" with the feminine alif, so he does not give it tanwīn. The meaning of "تَتْرى" is from "المُواتَرَة". Al-Aṣmaʿī said: the meaning of "واتَرْتُ الخَبَرَ" is "I made parts of the report follow one another, with a short interval between the two reports". Someone else said: "المُواتَرَة" is succession. The origin of all of this is from "الوِتْر", which is "the single": it is that you place each one after its companion, singly, one by one.

zajjaj:50-50.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ وأُمَّهُ آيَةً﴾: He did not say "آيَتَيْنِ" (two signs), because the meaning in the two of them is a single sign. Had "آيَتَيْنِ" been said, it would have been permissible, because there was in each of them what was not in any male or female: Maryam gave birth without a male, and ʿĪsā is a spirit from Allah which He cast into Maryam, and this was never the case in any child.
His saying: ﴿وَآوَيْناهُما إلى رَبْوَةٍ﴾: there are three dialectal forms of "رَبْوَة": "رَبْوَة", "رِبْوَة" and "رُبْوَة", and two other variants: "رَباوَة" and "رِباوَة". According to the lexicographers it is the elevated place. It came in the exegesis that by "رَبْوَة" here is meant Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), that it is the liver (centre) of the earth, and that it is the nearest part of the earth to heaven. It has been said that it means Damascus, and it has been said Palestine and al-Ramla. All of that has come in the exegesis. [Translator's note: the source has «والرَّحْلَة»; the place-name al-Ramla (الرَّمْلَة) is evidently intended.]
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذاتِ قَرارٍ ومَعِينٍ﴾, i.e. having a place of settlement, and "مَعِين" is water flowing from springs. Some of them said it may be on the pattern "فَعِيل" from "المَعْن", derived from "الماعُون". This is far-fetched, because "المَعْن" in the language is a small thing, and "الماعُون" is zakāt, on the pattern "فاعُول" from "المَعْن". Zakāt was named with a small thing only because a quarter of a tenth of property is taken, so it is little out of much. Al-Rāʿī said:
؎قَوْمٌ عَلى التَّنْزِيلِ لَمّا يَمْنَعُوا ∗∗∗ ماعُونَهم ويُبَدِّلُوا التَّنْزِيلا
(A people (holding fast) to the revelation, who have not withheld their zakāt nor altered the revelation.)

zajjaj:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الرُّسُلُ كُلُوا مِنَ الطَّيِّباتِ واعْمَلُوا صالِحًا﴾, i.e. "eat of what is lawful"; every lawful, wholesome food is included in this. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the one addressed by this, and it was said ﴿يا أيُّها الرُّسُلُ﴾, and this address implies that all the messengers were commanded likewise. It is narrated that ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, used to eat from his mother's spinning; and the best of good things is the spoils of war.

zajjaj:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنَّ هَذِهِ أُمَّتُكم أُمَّةً واحِدَةً وأنا رَبُّكم فاتَّقُونِ﴾, i.e. "so fear Me for this". We have explained in Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ everything that is permissible in the counterpart of this verse. The sum of its interpretation is that your religion is one religion, and that is Islam.
